Because 15.23.2 nests argument-3 inside argument-2's brackets, the 1-argument reference is the ONLY shape in which argument-2 can be omitted, so there is no second case to miss. Verified end to end and INDEPENDENTLY OF THE r5 DEFECT by pinning the base year: under COBOLNET_CLOCK=1990-06-10T12:00:00, `FUNCTION DATE-TO-YYYYMMDD(500101)` and `FUNCTION DATE-TO-YYYYMMDD(500101, 50)` both print 19500101, and unpinned both print 20500101 - the two forms agree under every clock, which is what r3 asserts. The cited unit test is on disk at tests/Cobol.Net.Tests.Unit/CobolDateWindowingTests.cs and DISCRIMINATES the default (491231 under a pinned 2026 clock gives 20491231 only for offset 50; offset 0 would give 19491231); its expected values are hand-derived from 15.23.4 r1 + 15.100.4 r2a/r2b, so it is spec-derived, not a characterization.

subject: DATE-TO-YYYYMMDD function
notes: SUSTAINED, with a SECOND independent defect found. 15.23.3 r4 requires argument-3 to be an integer greater than 1600 and less than 10000. (a) THE 'OMITTED' SENTINEL SWALLOWS 0. CobolDate.YearToYyyy resolves `long b = baseYear == 0 ? RunUnit.Current.Clock.Now().Year : baseYear;` and only THEN tests `if (b is <= 1600 or >= 10000)`, so an argument-3 written explicitly as 0 - illegal under r4 - is silently replaced by the execution-time year. RUN: `>>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON` / `COMPUTE D8 = FUNCTION DATE-TO-YYYYMMDD(851003, 10, 0)` prints ZERO-A3=19851003 and continues, while the adjacent `(851003, 10, 1600)` correctly aborts 'EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION (fatal)'. (b) THE 64-BIT TRUNCATION DEFEATS THE BOUND FOR WIDE VALUES. IntrinsicRenderer.AsInt emits `(long)(<expr>)`, so argument-3 wraps modulo 2^64 before the r4 test. RUN: `01 A3 PIC S9(31) VALUE 18446744073709553618.` (= 2^64 + 2002; `DISPLAY A3` confirms the value is stored intact) / `COMPUTE D8 = FUNCTION DATE-TO-YYYYMMDD(851003, 10, A3)` prints A3WRAP=19851003 with checking ON - an argument-3 of ~1.8e19 accepted as if it were 2002, where 15.3 requires EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION to be set to exist. (c) The INTEGER half of r4 is unscreened for the same reason as r1/r2 (absent from IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified). (d) The diagnostic misattributes the rule: a DATE-TO-YYYYMMDD reference reports 'YEAR-TO-YYYY argument-3 1600 is not greater than 1600 and less than 10000 (15.100.3 r4)' when the clause governing the reference the programmer wrote is 15.23.3 r4. ROOT FIXES: carry 'argument-3 omitted' as `long?` rather than an in-band 0; range-screen at full width before narrowing to long; name the referencing function in the message. test-needed.

subject: DATE-TO-YYYYMMDD function
notes: OVERTURNED from CONFORMS. 15.23.3 r5 makes the omitted argument-3 evaluate AS THOUGH '(FUNCTION NUMVAL (FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE (1:4)))' were specified. THE IMPLEMENTATION READS A DIFFERENT CLOCK. CobolDate.YearToYyyy defaults through `RunUnit.Current.Clock.Now().Year`, while CobolDate.CurrentDate() - the function r5 names - reads `DateTimeOffset.Now` directly and is NOT on that seam (the source comment on SecondsPastMidnight says so in as many words: 'NOT the CurrentDate direct-DateTimeOffset.Now path, which predates the seam'). The default SystemClock honours the COBOLNET_CLOCK environment variable, which is a shipped runtime facility (src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/IO/Clock.cs, used across processes by the project's own temporal conformance harness), so the split is observable from an ordinary program with no host-side injection at all. CONCRETE FAILING INPUT, compiled and run with src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/cobol.exe under COBOLNET_CLOCK=1990-06-10T12:00:00: `01 CD PIC X(21). 01 Y4 PIC 9(4). 01 D8 PIC 9(8).` / `MOVE FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE TO CD` / `COMPUTE Y4 = FUNCTION NUMVAL(CD(1:4)) DISPLAY "CURRENT-DATE(1:4)=" Y4` / `COMPUTE D8 = FUNCTION DATE-TO-YYYYMMDD(500101) DISPLAY "DEFAULT-ARG3 =" D8` / `COMPUTE D8 = FUNCTION DATE-TO-YYYYMMDD(500101, 50, Y4) DISPLAY "EXPLICIT-CD-YR =" D8`. It prints CURRENT-DATE(1:4)=2026, DEFAULT-ARG3=19500101, EXPLICIT-CD-YR=20500101 - i.e. the omitted form used base year 1990 where r5 mandates the CURRENT-DATE year 2026. The two forms must be identical by r5 and are not. SECOND, INDEPENDENT DEFECT ON THE SAME RULE: the compiler cannot even PARSE the expression r5 writes - `COMPUTE Y4 = FUNCTION NUMVAL(FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE(1:4))` fails with COBOL0001 'no viable alternative at input ... FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE(1:', although 8.4.3.3.3 SR2 expressly permits reference modification of a function-identifier that 'shall reference an alphanumeric, boolean, or national function' and 15.21.1 says of CURRENT-DATE 'The type of this function is alphanumeric'. (The prior adjudication cited this as 8.4.3.2, one level short and the wrong sibling; the rule is 8.4.3.3.3 SR2.) So legal COBOL is rejected AND the program has no way to write the workaround. ROOT FIX: route CobolDate.CurrentDate() through RunUnit.Current.Clock so ONE clock serves the rule, and admit reference modification on an alphanumeric function-identifier in CobolExpressions.g4. test-needed - and note that unit:CobolDateWindowingTests.DateToYyyymmdd_Defaults_DelegateToWindowCore CANNOT serve as this row's test: it injects RunUnit.Clock, i.e. it pins the divergent source rather than CURRENT-DATE.

subject: DATE-TO-YYYYMMDD function
notes: OVERTURNED from CONFORMS. The RULE READING is right and I re-derived it: 15.23.3 r6's 'the year at the time of execution' resolves to argument-3, because 15.23.1 states 'Argument-3 specifies the year at the time of execution' (confirmed on the PRINTED page - python scripts/render-spec-page.py 867, printed folio 837 - so this is not an OCR artifact), and 15.23.4 r1 defines the returned value by reference to YEAR-TO-YYYY, whose 15.100.3 r6 reads 'The sum of the values of argument-2 and argument-3'. So `max = off + b` rejected on `max is <= 1699 or >= 10000` is the right SHAPE. THE SCREEN IS NEVERTHELESS DEFEATED, because IntrinsicRenderer.AsInt narrows every argument with `(long)(<expr>)` before the runtime sees it, so a legal COBOL integer wider than 64 bits wraps modulo 2^64 and the sum tested is not the sum the program wrote. CONCRETE FAILING INPUT, run with src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/cobol.exe: `01 D8 PIC S9(18). 01 A2 PIC S9(31) VALUE 18446744073709552614.` (= 2^64 + 998; `DISPLAY A2` confirms it is stored intact) / `>>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON` / `COMPUTE D8 = FUNCTION DATE-TO-YYYYMMDD(851003, A2, 2002)` / `DISPLAY "A2WRAP=" D8` prints A2WRAP=29851003 and continues. The true sum argument-2 + argument-3 is 18446744073709554616, which is not 'less than 10000', so 15.3 requires EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION to be set to exist; instead the wrapped offset 998 gives maximum-year 3000 and a fabricated 2985. In-range behaviour IS correct at both edges when the operands fit a long - (991231, 0, 9999) -> 99991231, (991231, 5, 9999) -> EC; argument-3 omitted at exec year 2026: argument-2 -326 -> accepted, -327 -> EC, +7973 -> accepted, +7974 -> EC - which is why small-operand sampling missed this. SECOND DEFECT, inherited from r5: when argument-3 is omitted the base of the r6 sum is RunUnit.Clock's year rather than the CURRENT-DATE year r5 mandates, so under COBOLNET_CLOCK the sum is screened against the wrong 'year at the time of execution'. ROOT FIX: screen the r1/r4/r6 ranges at the argument's real width before narrowing to long. test-needed.

subject: DATE-TO-YYYYMMDD function
notes: SUSTAINED, and verified the way 15.4.1 NOTE 2 says to verify it. The body IS the equivalent arithmetic expression: `return YearToYyyy(date / 10000, off, baseYear) * 10000 + date % 10000;`. YY = FUNCTION INTEGER(argument-1/10000) matches because 15.44.4 r1 makes INTEGER the floor and, for the r1-legal range 1..999999, C# truncating `/` IS the floor; mmdd = FUNCTION MOD(argument-1, 10000) matches for the same nonnegative range. I did not take that on argument: I wrote the equivalent arithmetic expression out in COBOL and compared it to the function through the compiler - `COMPUTE R2 = FUNCTION YEAR-TO-YYYY(FUNCTION INTEGER(851003 / 10000), 10, 2002) * 10000 + FUNCTION MOD(851003, 10000)` gives 19851003, equal to `FUNCTION DATE-TO-YYYYMMDD(851003, 10, 2002)`, and the YY=1 case (10101, 50, 2026) gives 20010101 both ways. Both 15.23.4 NOTE-1 examples reproduce end to end: (851003, 10, 2002) -> 19851003 and (981002, (-10), 1994) -> 18981002; so do the window edges (490101, 50, 1999) -> 20490101 / (500101, 50, 1999) -> 19500101 and the argument-1 endpoints (1, 50, 2026) / (999999, 50, 2026). RECEIVER VARIED, not just the arguments: PIC 9(8), PIC 9(18), PIC 9(12)V99 (-> 19851003.00), PIC 9(10)V9(9) (-> 19999999.000000000), an IF relation condition, a bare DISPLAY of the function-identifier, MOVE to PIC X(8) (-> '19851003') and MOVE to PIC Z(7)9 all give the equivalent-expression value; the only differing case, PIC 9(6)V99 -> 851003.00, is ordinary high-order MOVE truncation, not a rendering defect. The nested reference the 15.23.3 r1 NOTE suggests, FUNCTION TEST-DATE-YYYYMMDD(FUNCTION DATE-TO-YYYYMMDD(851003, 10, 2002)), returns 0. OBSERVATION (conforming - 15.3 says 'the implementor defines the result of the function reference' when checking is off, though it is inconsistent with DateOfInteger/IntegerOfDate, which return a clean 0): when the delegated YearToYyyy fails an argument rule it returns 0 and the composite yields 0*10000 + mmdd, e.g. (851003, 10, 1600) -> 1003. The argument-screening defects that reach this body are recorded on AR-15.23.3-1/-4/-6, not here.

subject: DAY-OF-INTEGER function
notes:
OVERTURNED FROM PARTIAL TO DIVERGES. 'A value in integer date form' is defined by §15.5.2 ('A value in integer date form is a positive integer ... It shall be greater than zero and shall be less than or equal to the value of FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-DATE (99991231), which is 3,067,671'), and Table 21 (§15.6) types argument-1 'Int1', i.e. §15.3 type 6 ('An arithmetic expression that will always result in an integer value or an integer data item shall be specified'). A violation makes §15.3 set EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION to exist; the implementor-defined-result latitude in that same paragraph applies ONLY 'if ... checking for EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION is not enabled'. §7.3.25.4 GR6 says that with '>>TURN ... CHECKING ON' checking IS enabled, so under checking-ON the exception must be raised. It is not, for two whole families of out-of-form argument, and the compiler returns a plausible-looking Julian date instead. That is a WRONG OBSERVABLE RESULT in a context where the spec grants no latitude, not a missing screen.

(1) INT64 WRAP DEFEATS THE §15.5.2 RANGE TEST. IntrinsicRenderer.AsInt emits an UNCHECKED narrowing cast '(long)(<Int128 expr>)' before CobolDate.DayOfInteger's 'integerDate is < 1 or > 3067671' guard ever sees the value, so any argument congruent modulo 2^64 to something in 1..3,067,671 sails through. RAN, at the DEFAULT --std 2023, with checking explicitly ON:
       IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. DOITURN1.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01 BIG PIC 9(21) VALUE 18446744073709551617.
       01 R PIC 9(7).
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN-PARA.
           >>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON
           COMPUTE R = FUNCTION DAY-OF-INTEGER(BIG).
           DISPLAY "NO EXCEPTION RAISED, R = " R.
           STOP RUN.
prints 'NO EXCEPTION RAISED, R = 1601001'. 18446744073709551617 mod 2^64 = 1, and 1601001 is exactly DAY-OF-INTEGER(1). A second witness, 18446744073709694000 (wrap 142384), prints 1990305. The item itself is undamaged — DISPLAY BIG prints 018446744073709551617 — so the corruption is introduced by the intrinsic argument path alone. Contrast the SAME program with 3067672: it correctly aborts 'EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION (fatal): DAY-OF-INTEGER argument 3067672 outside 1..3,067,671'. The prior adjudication tested only that in-range-of-long case and concluded the value half CONFORMS.

(2) A FRACTIONAL ARGUMENT IS NOT A POSITIVE INTEGER (§15.5.2) AND STILL RAISES NOTHING. IntArg silently truncates through NumRescale/Truncation. RAN, checking ON: '01 FR PIC 9(7)V9 VALUE 143951.7.' + 'COMPUTE R = FUNCTION DAY-OF-INTEGER(FR).' prints 'NO EXCEPTION RAISED, R = 1995046' — identical to the integer 143951.

(3) THE CLASS SCREEN IS ABSENT (the prior finding, still true). DAY-OF-INTEGER is in NEITHER IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified NOR DeliberatelyUnscreened, so CheckArgumentClasses returns at its 'if (!IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified.TryGetValue(sig.Name, out var rule)) return;' guard and COBOLNET1627 never fires: 'COMPUTE R = FUNCTION DAY-OF-INTEGER(A).' with '01 A PIC X(4) VALUE "ABCD"' compiles clean at --std 2023 and prints 0000000. The precedent is one row away — COMBINED-DATETIME's §15.17.3 r1 carries the identical 'shall be in integer date form' wording and IS screened ('n').

(4) A CLASS-NUMERIC FLOATING ARGUMENT EMITS RAW ROSLYN (the PB2 failure mode, unfixed for the 'i' date rows). '01 DVAL USAGE COMP-2.' + 'MOVE 143951 TO DVAL.' + 'COMPUTE R = FUNCTION DAY-OF-INTEGER(DVAL).' fails with "error CS0117: 'CobolIntrinsics' does not contain a definition for 'DayOfIntegerReal'" — an internal failure escaping as a backend error. IntrinsicRenderer routes on AnyRealArgument for EVERY exact arm, but IntrinsicRealArgDriftTests.NumericArgumentMethods scopes its guard to ArgKinds containing 'n', so the 'i' rows (DAY-OF-INTEGER, DATE-OF-INTEGER, INTEGER-OF-DATE/DAY, FACTORIAL, CHAR, the Y2K trio) are unguarded — and the class screen this row is missing would not have caught it either, since 'i' admits CLASS numeric and a COMP-2 IS class numeric (§8.5.2.1 Table 2).

ROOT CAUSE AND SWEEP (CLAUDE.md rule 4): defect (1) is in IntrinsicRenderer.AsInt, which every 'i'-kind arm shares, so it is a PATTERN, not a DAY-OF-INTEGER bug. Confirmed on a sibling in the same run: 'COMPUTE R8 = FUNCTION DATE-OF-INTEGER(BIG)' with checking ON prints 16010101, no exception. The fix is a range/representability check on the Int128 value BEFORE the narrowing cast (or an Int128-typed runtime parameter), plus the row ["DAY-OF-INTEGER"] = ('i', "§15.24.3 r1") in Verified, plus a DayOfIntegerReal body (or a rejection) for the float path.

test-needed: no spec-derived test exercises this argument rule's ENFORCEMENT for DAY-OF-INTEGER. IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests.IntegerDateForm_Epoch_PinnedToSpec passes DAY-OF-INTEGER only the valid value 1, and its single invalid-argument row is INTEGER-OF-DATE(20230230), a different function; nothing on disk runs any DAY-OF-INTEGER case under '>>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON'.

subject: DAY-OF-INTEGER function
notes: SUSTAINED, re-verified rather than inherited. DayOfInteger computes 'Epoch.AddDays(integerDate - 1)' from 'Epoch = new DateTime(1601, 1, 1)', which is the §15.5.2 mapping (integer date 1 = Monday 1601-01-01); .NET's DateTime is the proleptic Gregorian calendar §15.5.1 demands over the whole 1601..9999 range. Independent sweep: generated 62 integer dates (the §D.31.3.7 worked example 143951; the endpoints 1 and 3,067,671; the 1700/1800/1900 non-leap and 2000/2400 leap century boundaries at Feb 28 / Mar 1 / Dec 31; 2000-02-29; and 25 pseudo-random in-range values), computed the expected YYYYDDD in Python's proleptic Gregorian calendar from the spec definition alone, and diffed against the compiled program: ALL 62 MATCH. Receiver axis varied too (the PB5 lesson), all correct at 1995046 for argument 143951: PIC 9(7), 9(9), 9(18), S9(9) COMP, S9(9) BINARY, 9(7)V99, 9(9)V9(5), COMP-1, COMP-2, PIC ZZZ9999 via MOVE, plus a receiver-less IF condition, an EVALUATE subject, a direct DISPLAY, and the operand of '+ 1'. Argument shapes varied: literal, arithmetic expression (143950 + 1), and the nested FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-DATE(19950215) — all 1995046. The rule is conditioned on argument-1 being in integer date form, so the int64-wrap defect is charged to AR-15.24.3-1, not here. Coverage note (not a test-need for this row): the cited test pins only DAY-OF-INTEGER(1) -> 01601001 and the INTEGER-OF-DAY round trip of 150000.

subject: DAY-OF-INTEGER function
notes: SUSTAINED; both halves of the rule independently re-verified. 'return d.Year * 1000L + d.DayOfYear;' places the Gregorian year in the YYYY positions and the ORDINAL day of that year in DDD — the §15.5.4 Julian date form ('The Julian date form is YYYYDDD, where YYYY represents the year and DDD represents the ordinal date within that year'). YYYY half: 1 -> 1601001 (epoch year), 3067671 -> 9999365 (terminal year), 143951 -> 1995046. DDD half, over the 62-value spec-computed sweep described in RV-15.24.4-1: the leap-day ordinal is counted (2000-02-29 -> 2000060) and 366-day years reach 366 (2000-12-31 -> 2000366), while the century non-leap years do not (1900-12-31 -> 1900365, 1700-03-01 -> 1700060 vs 2000-03-01 -> 2000061), so §15.5.1's Gregorian leap rule is honoured in the DDD positions and not merely in YYYY. Identical at --std 85 / 2002 / 2014 / 2023. Coverage note (not a test-need for this row): the cited test's only DAY-OF-INTEGER expectation is 01601001, whose DDD is 001 — no on-disk spec-derived case reaches a leap-day or a three-digit ordinal, which is why the DDD half was checked by running rather than by trusting the suite.

subject: DAY-TO-YYYYDDD function
notes:
VERDICT UPHELD on re-review; every claim independently re-run, and a THIRD defect added that the adjudicator missed. Citation re-validated mechanically: `cite.py --check 15.25.3 "Argument-1 shall be a positive integer less than 100000"` -> OK (rule path 1). The §15.3 TYPE of every argument is confirmed from the spec's own summary table, NOT from the catalog under review: `cite.py --find "Argument-1 converted from YYDDD to YYYYDDD"` resolves to §15.6 4) 'DAY-TO-YYYYDDD | Int1, Int2, Int3 | Int' - so all three arguments are §15.3 type 6 Integer ('An arithmetic expression that will always result in an integer value or an integer data item shall be specified').
THE BOUND ITSELF IS RIGHT AND FIRES (re-run, not inherited): CobolDate.DayToYyyyddd opens `if (day is < 1 or > 99999) return Exceptions.ExceptionState.ArgumentError(...)`; with `>>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON`, argument-1 = 0 and = 100000 each abort exit 1 with 'DAY-TO-YYYYDDD argument-1 ... is not a positive integer less than 100000 (15.25.3 r1)'; with checking OFF both return the documented §15.3 default 0 (`A1ZERO-OFF=0000000`, `A1HIGH-OFF=0000000`). THREE DEFECTS SIT AROUND IT.
DEFECT A - LOSSY UNCHECKED NARROWING UPSTREAM OF THE BOUND. IntrinsicRenderer's Y2K-trio arm renders every argument through IntArg -> AsInt, whose scale-0 form is literally `(long)({a.Expr})` over an Int128-typed argument expression. C#'s Int128->long conversion is UNCHECKED and wraps modulo 2^64, so a magnitude >= 2^63 ALIASES into the legal 1..99999 window before DayToYyyyddd's own test runs. RE-RAN with checking explicitly ON so the §15.3 implementor-defined-result latitude cannot excuse it - exit 0, no diagnostic:
       >>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON
       01  R    PIC 9(9).
       01  BIG  PIC 9(20) VALUE 18446744073709561620.
           COMPUTE R = FUNCTION DAY-TO-YYYYDDD(BIG, 20, 2002)
           DISPLAY "WRAP=" R
prints `WRAP=002010004`. 18446744073709561620 = 2^64 + 10004, so the wrap delivers 10004. PREMISE VALIDATED, not just the rule: `cite.py --check 8.3.3.3.2 "The implementor shall allow for fixed-point numeric literals of 1 through 31 digits in length"` -> OK, so a 20-digit literal and a PIC 9(20) integer item are both legal COBOL and this is a pure r1 VALUE violation. §15.3 (validated) then requires: 'If the evaluation of an argument results in an incorrect value for that argument ... the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist.' It is not set. Same whole-channel AsInt defect already recorded against CHAR-NATIONAL - sweep the channel.
DEFECT B - THE §15.3 TYPE-6 SCREEN NEVER RUNS FOR THIS FUNCTION. IntrinsicBinder.CheckArgumentClasses opens `if (!IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified.TryGetValue(sig.Name, out var rule)) return;` and DAY-TO-YYYYDDD appears in NEITHER Verified NOR DeliberatelyUnscreened (both re-read on disk), so PB1's screen is a no-op here. RE-RAN: `01 AX PIC X(5) VALUE "10004".` with `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION DAY-TO-YYYYDDD(AX, 20, 2002)` compiles clean at --std 2023 and prints `ALPHA=2010004`. Related over-acceptance from the same hole, also re-run: `FUNCTION DAY-TO-YYYYDDD(FUNCTION NUMVAL("10004"), 20, 2002)` prints `SR11=2010004`, but §8.4.3.2.3 SR11 (validated by reading the clause) says 'A numeric function shall not be specified where an integer operand is required, even though a particular reference of the numeric function might yield an integer value.'
DEFECT C - NEW, MISSED BY THE ADJUDICATOR, AND THE HARDEST FAILURE OF THE THREE: a FLOATING-POINT argument-1 makes the BACKEND fail, not the front end. `AnyRealArgument` -> `RenderFloat(ic, RealMethod("DayToYyyyddd"))` emits `CobolIntrinsics.DayToYyyydddReal(...)`, a method that does not exist in CobolIntrinsics.RealArgs.cs (grep-verified: the file has AbsReal/ModReal/CombinedDatetimeReal etc., no date-window bodies) - and the Y2K trio's exact bodies live in CobolDate, not CobolIntrinsics, so the emitted TYPE is wrong too. RAN:
       01  R  PIC 9(7).
       01  F  COMP-2 VALUE 10004.
           COMPUTE R = FUNCTION DAY-TO-YYYYDDD(F, 20, 2002)
-> `error: backend compilation failed (generated C# at t1.g.cs): (44,90): error CS0117: 'CobolIntrinsics' does not contain a definition for 'DayToYyyydddReal'`, exit 70. This is NOT a re-report of PB2: PB2's own drift guard (tests/Cobol.Net.Tests.Unit/IntrinsicRealArgDriftTests.cs, method NumericArgumentMethods) deliberately scopes itself to catalog rows whose ArgKinds contain 'n' or are empty, on the stated ground that an 'i'-kind function 'cannot receive a float without violating their own argument rule first, which is PB1's business, not this test's'. PB1 then never screened this function. The two landed fixes hand the case to each other and it falls through as a raw Roslyn error. The COBOL is in error (a COMP-2 is neither an integer data item nor an always-integer expression), but the required response is the §4.2.2 diagnostic, not an internal backend failure. Root fix: screen the trio in IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified, which closes B, C and (as a class) the SR11 case together.
test-needed: a checking-ON conformance case asserting the abort for argument-1 = 0, = 100000 and = 2^64 + 10004; a negative case rejecting a PIC X argument-1; and a negative case rejecting a COMP-2 argument-1 with a diagnostic rather than CS0117.
EDITIONS: NOT derived from IntrinsicCatalog's row. The 2023 document under review carries §15.25 with no removal marker and no Annex-E addition entry, so 2014 and 2023 both have it; the 2002 lower bound is the ISO/IEC 1989:2002 introduction, which is NOT derivable from the 2023 text - asserted, and consistent with the compiler's own D8 gate (COBOLNET1502 at --std 85, accepted at 2002/2014/2023 - all four editions re-run).

subject: DAY-TO-YYYYDDD function
notes:
VERDICT UPHELD, BUT THE ADJUDICATOR'S REASONING IS OVERTURNED AND ITS FIXER NOTE WAS BACKWARDS - do not act on the original. Citation re-validated: `cite.py --check 15.25.3 "Argument-2 shall be an integer"` -> OK (rule path 2). §15.6 4)'s summary row 'DAY-TO-YYYYDDD | Int1, Int2, Int3 | Int' confirms argument-2 is §15.3 type 6 Integer.
WHAT IS ACTUALLY BROKEN: nothing enforces integer-ness at any stage. There is no argument-2 arm in IntrinsicBinder for the Y2K trio, DAY-TO-YYYYDDD is absent from IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified so CheckArgumentClasses returns immediately, and CobolDate.DayToYyyyddd passes `off` straight to YearToYyyy with no integer-ness test - the only constraint anywhere on argument-2 is the r6 SUM check.
CONCRETE FAILING INPUT (re-run at --std 2023 with checking ON, exit 0): `01 F2 PIC S9(3)V99 VALUE 20.75.` then `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION DAY-TO-YYYYDDD(10004, F2, 2002)` prints `FRAC=2010004`. IntrinsicRenderer.AsInt's non-zero-scale form silently rescales with CobolRounding.Truncation, so 20.75 becomes 20 and the answer is manufactured from a value the program never wrote. F2 is class NUMERIC and its class is fine; what it is not is an INTEGER data item, and `F2` alone is not an arithmetic expression that will ALWAYS result in an integer value. §15.3: EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION is required when 'the evaluation of an argument results in an incorrect value for that argument ... according to the rules specified in the function definition'. Nothing is set.
SECOND FAILING INPUT, SAME ROOT (re-run, exit 0): `01 ED PIC ZZ9.99 VALUE 20.00.` -> `FUNCTION DAY-TO-YYYYDDD(10004, ED, 2002)` prints `EDITED=2010004`. ⛔ THE ADJUDICATOR CALLED THIS A CLASS VIOLATION AND THAT IS WRONG BY THIS REPOSITORY'S OWN SETTLED SPEC READING. IntrinsicArgumentRules.Admissible('i') is `[CobolClass.Numeric, CobolClass.NumericEditedDeEditing]`, with a long comment recording that screening a numeric-edited operand out of a §15.3 type-6 position REJECTED LEGAL COBOL and broke a golden plus an AssertSpec test (DA6). The operative violation in this repro is therefore the declared non-zero SCALE, exactly as in the first repro - not the class.
⛔ CORRECTED FIXER NOTE (the original said 'adding DAY-TO-YYYYDDD to Verified as (''i'', ...) closes input 1 only' - it closes NEITHER): with kind 'i', Admissible admits both Numeric and NumericEditedDeEditing, so the class screen as it stands leaves BOTH repros accepted. Adding the row is still right (it is what closes the PIC X argument-1 case and the COMP-2 backend crash in AR-15.25.3-1), but r2 needs a SECOND mechanism the screen does not have today: a declared-scale test. A non-zero declared PICTURE scale IS a static property of the source and so is syntactically distinguishable under §4.2.2, which is the same justification IntrinsicArgumentRules already writes down for the class screen; a runtime integer-ness test in CobolDate before the truncation is the fallback for the operands whose scale is not static.
RELATED HARD FAILURE (verified, and the same missing screen): a COMP-2 argument-2 emits `CobolIntrinsics.DayToYyyydddReal(...)`, which does not exist -> `error CS0117`, exit 70. See AR-15.25.3-1 DEFECT C.
test-needed: a checking-ON case asserting the abort for a fractional argument-2 (PIC S9(3)V99 VALUE 20.75) and for a numeric-edited argument-2 with a fractional PICTURE; a negative case rejecting a PIC X argument-2; a negative case rejecting a COMP-2 argument-2 with a diagnostic rather than CS0117.
EDITIONS: as for AR-15.25.3-1 - the 2023 document establishes 2014/2023, the 2002 lower bound is asserted from ISO/IEC 1989:2002, and all four --std settings were re-run. Not taken from IntrinsicCatalog's row.

subject: DAY-TO-YYYYDDD function
notes: Verdict unchanged; supplies the missing spec-derived test. 'Evaluated as though 50 were specified' is an equivalence, asserted directly against the explicit-50 form. Argument-2 IS the windowing cut, so it is probed below it, AT it and above it (years 12/49/50/51/75) - a single sample on one side would pass while the windowing was wrong. The result VALUE is deliberately not pinned: 15.25.3 r5 defaults argument-3 to the current year, so the YYYY half is a clock reading; the DDD half is printed instead as the non-vacuity witness.

subject: DAY-TO-YYYYDDD function
notes:
VERDICT UPHELD; every claim re-run. Citation re-validated: `cite.py --check 15.25.3 "Argument-3 shall be an integer greater than 1600 and less than 10000"` -> OK (rule path 4).
THE BOUND IS ENFORCED EVERYWHERE EXCEPT AT ONE VALUE, AND THAT VALUE IS ILLEGAL. CobolDate.YearToYyyy - the ONE windowing core §15.25.4 r1 delegates to - reads `long b = baseYear == 0 ? RunUnit.Current.Clock.Now().Year : baseYear;` and only THEN tests `if (b is <= 1600 or >= 10000)`. Zero is consumed as the 'argument-3 omitted' SENTINEL, and the renderer gives the runtime no other way to tell an omitted argument from a written one (it emits only the arguments present). An explicit argument-3 of 0 violates r4 outright ('greater than 1600') and additionally violates r6 (20 + 0 = 20 is not greater than 1699), yet it is silently replaced by the execution-time year and a well-formed WRONG value is returned.
CONCRETE FAILING INPUT, RE-RUN with COBOLNET_CLOCK=2002-06-15T10:00:00 and checking explicitly ON - exit 0, no diagnostic:
       >>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON
       01  R  PIC 9(7).
           COMPUTE R = FUNCTION DAY-TO-YYYYDDD(10004, 20, 0)
           DISPLAY "A3ZERO=" R
prints `A3ZERO=2010004` - the answer for argument-3 = 2002, which the program never wrote. Expected: EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION set (§15.3), fatal under the enabled check.
CONTROLS PROVING THE HOLE IS EXACTLY AND ONLY 0 (checking ON, all abort exit 1): argument-3 = 1600 -> 'argument-3 1600 is not greater than 1600 and less than 10000'; -5 and 10000 likewise; and a DEFAULTED argument-3 under COBOLNET_CLOCK=1600-06-15 aborts with the same message, so the predicate is right and the SENTINEL is the defect.
SECOND ESCAPE ON THIS SAME ROW, MISSED BY THE ADJUDICATOR: the AsInt `(long)` narrowing (AR-15.25.3-1 DEFECT A) also aliases argument-3. Any written argument-3 congruent mod 2^64 to a legal year passes r4 unchallenged - the mechanism is proven on argument-2 in AR-15.25.3-6 with a PIC 9(20) operand, and the argument-3 position renders through the identical IntArg call.
THIRD: a COMP-2 argument-3 does not diagnose either - it crashes the backend. RAN `01 F3 COMP-1 VALUE 2002.` with `FUNCTION DAY-TO-YYYYDDD(10004, 20, F3)` -> `error CS0117: 'CobolIntrinsics' does not contain a definition for 'DayToYyyydddReal'`, exit 70 (AR-15.25.3-1 DEFECT C).
ROOT FIX (CLAUDE.md rules 4/5 - the shape, not the smallest diff): omitted-ness must be carried by the CALL SHAPE, not by an in-band value the spec declares illegal - a distinct overload or a `long?` argument-3, decided by the renderer from ic.Args.Count, which is already the thing that knows. THE DEFECT IS THE TRIO'S: DateToYyyymmdd and YearToYyyy share the identical `baseYear = 0` sentinel - sweep all three.
COLLATERAL CITATION NIT, confirmed by reading the emitted diagnostics: a DAY-TO-YYYYDDD reference that trips r4 or r6 reports '15.100.3 r4' / '15.100.3 r6' because the check lives in the shared YearToYyyy core. The governing rules for THIS function reference are §15.25.3 r4 / r6 (textually identical, so no behavioural difference - but the user is sent to the wrong clause).

subject: DAY-TO-YYYYDDD function
notes:
⛔ OVERTURNED: PARTIAL -> DIVERGES. The adjudicator found the right defect and then graded it down on a premise I could not sustain - that the divergence 'is reachable only through an implementor test facility ... and not through any COBOL construct'. It is reachable through the SHIPPED runtime with no test code at all, and I have a concrete same-execution repro. Citation re-validated: `cite.py --check 15.25.3 "FUNCTION NUMVAL (FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE (1:4))"` -> OK (rule path 5).
WHAT r5 REQUIRES: not 'the current year' loosely, but that the defaulted argument-3 be IDENTICAL to `FUNCTION NUMVAL (FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE (1:4))`. Those are TWO SEPARATE CLOCK MECHANISMS in this tree. CobolDate.CurrentDate() is `Format21(DateTimeOffset.Now)` - a direct read that bypasses the run-unit seam, as the file's own SecondsPastMidnight comment admits ('NOT the CurrentDate direct-DateTimeOffset.Now path, which predates the seam') - while YearToYyyy reads `RunUnit.Current.Clock.Now().Year`.
CONCRETE FAILING INPUT, RAN - one program, ONE execution, no test harness:
       01  CD PIC X(21).  01 YR PIC 9(4).  01 DT PIC 9(6).  01 R PIC 9(7).
           MOVE FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE TO CD
           MOVE FUNCTION NUMVAL(CD(1:4)) TO YR
           ACCEPT DT FROM DATE
           COMPUTE R = FUNCTION DAY-TO-YYYYDDD(70100)
           DISPLAY "CURDATE-YR=" YR " ACCEPT-DATE=" DT " DEFAULT=" R
with COBOLNET_CLOCK=2013-06-15T10:00:00 prints `CURDATE-YR=2026 ACCEPT-DATE=130615 DEFAULT=1970100`. r5 says the default IS 2026; the function used 2013. The control run without the pin prints `CURDATE-YR=2026 ACCEPT-DATE=260730 DEFAULT=2070100` - the two agree, isolating the mechanism split as the sole cause (1970100 vs 2070100 is the §15.100.4 r2a/r2b flip at max 2063 vs 2076, hand-derived).
WHY THIS IS NOT A TEST-ONLY ARTEFACT: `SystemClock` is the DEFAULT `IClock` in the shipped Cobol.Net.Runtime and its `Now()` consults COBOLNET_CLOCK on EVERY call, unconditionally - it is not compiled out, not test-scoped, and its own doc-comment describes it as pinning the clock ACROSS PROCESSES. Any user who sets that variable gets ACCEPT FROM DATE and the DAY-TO-YYYYDDD default pinned while CURRENT-DATE runs free - a 13-year disagreement inside one statement sequence. §15.4.1 (validated by `cite.py --find`, the text is in §15.4.1, NOT §15.2) does grant that 'the DAY-TO-YYYYDDD function when argument-3 is not specified' need not return the same value for all instances within one execution - but that latitude is about the clock ADVANCING, not about two clocks disagreeing by 13 years, and it cannot override r5's explicit identity.
ROOT FIX: one_mechanism_per_job - route CobolDate.CurrentDate (and FormattedCurrentDate, which is the same `DateTimeOffset.Now` direct read) through RunUnit.Current.Clock like every other temporal source. That is a §15.21/§15.38 change as much as a §15.25 one; the r5 equivalence is a consequence of it, not a separate fix.
COLLATERAL, and directly on this rule's text: the expression r5 names CANNOT BE WRITTEN in this compiler. RAN `MOVE FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE(1:4) TO Y4` -> `error COBOL0001: no viable alternative at input '('` (exit 65). That is legal COBOL: `cite.py --check 8.4.3.3.3 "it shall reference an alphanumeric, boolean, or national function"` -> OK, and `cite.py --check 8.4.3.2.3 "the left parenthesis is always treated as the left parenthesis of that function's arguments"` -> OK, whose antecedent ('if a function's definition PERMITS ARGUMENTS') is false for CURRENT-DATE, so the '(' belongs to the reference modifier. `functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (LPAREN functionArgList? RPAREN)?` in src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolExpressions.g4 has no reference-modifier tail. Adjudicate under §8.4.3.2/§8.4.3.3, not here - recorded because it is the exact expression this rule cites and it means no COBOL program can assert the r5 equivalence directly today.
test-needed: a pinned-clock conformance case asserting DAY-TO-YYYYDDD's defaulted argument-3 equals NUMVAL(CURRENT-DATE(1:4)) in the same execution. CobolDateWindowingTests.YearToYyyy_DefaultArg3_IsExecutionYear covers the sibling function only and never compares against CURRENT-DATE, so it stays green straight through this defect.

subject: DAY-TO-YYYYDDD function
notes:
⛔ OVERTURNED: PARTIAL -> DIVERGES. The adjudicator graded PARTIAL because the only escape it found was inherited from the AR-15.25.3-4 sentinel ('fixing the sentinel closes this row too - no independent change is needed here'). That is not true: there is a SECOND, INDEPENDENT escape that the sentinel fix does not touch, and I have a concrete failing input for it. Citation re-validated: `cite.py --check 15.25.3 "The sum of the values of argument-2 and argument-3 shall be less than 10000 and greater than 1699"` -> OK (rule path 6).
THE PREDICATE ITSELF IS CORRECT AND BOTH BOUNDS FIRE (re-run, checking ON): CobolDate.YearToYyyy computes `long max = off + b;` then `if (max is <= 1699 or >= 10000)` -> ArgumentError, matching the rule's strict inequalities. `FUNCTION DAY-TO-YYYYDDD(10004, -303, 2002)` (sum 1699) aborts exit 1 with 'argument-2 + argument-3 = 1699 is not greater than 1699 and less than 10000'; sum 10000 aborts identically. The adjacent LEGAL values are accepted and correct: sum 1700 -> `FUNCTION DAY-TO-YYYYDDD(10, -302, 2002)` = 1700010; sum 9999 -> `FUNCTION DAY-TO-YYYYDDD(99365, 7997, 2002)` = 9999365, both hand-derived from §15.25.4 r1 + §15.100.4 r2a. The DEFAULTED-argument-2 path also feeds r6 correctly (COBOLNET_CLOCK=1620 -> sum 1670 -> abort).
CONCRETE FAILING INPUT - THE INDEPENDENT ESCAPE (checking explicitly ON, exit 0, no diagnostic):
       >>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON
       01  R      PIC 9(7).
       01  BIGOFF PIC 9(20) VALUE 18446744073709551636.
           COMPUTE R = FUNCTION DAY-TO-YYYYDDD(10004, BIGOFF, 2002)
           DISPLAY "R6WRAP=" R
prints `R6WRAP=2010004`. 18446744073709551636 = 2^64 + 20, so IntrinsicRenderer.AsInt's unchecked `(long)(Int128)` narrowing wraps it to 20 before the runtime ever adds it to argument-3. The sum of the values the program WROTE is 2^64 + 2022, which is not less than 10000 - r6 is violated outright and EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION is never set. PIC 9(20) is a legal integer data item (`cite.py --check 8.3.3.3.2 "The implementor shall allow for fixed-point numeric literals of 1 through 31 digits in length"` -> OK), so this is a pure r6 VALUE violation and §15.3 requires the exception. Fixing the AR-15.25.3-4 sentinel does NOT close it; fixing the AsInt narrowing channel does.
SECOND ESCAPE (the one the adjudicator found, retained): the sum checked is argument-2 + EFFECTIVE argument-3, so when argument-3 is written as an explicit 0 the effective value silently becomes the execution-time year and the WRITTEN sum is never tested - `FUNCTION DAY-TO-YYYYDDD(10004, 20, 0)` has a written sum of 20 and still prints 2010004 at exit 0 with checking ON (COBOLNET_CLOCK=2002-06-15).
THIRD, UNTESTED RATHER THAN WRONG: when argument-3 is DEFAULTED the r6 sum depends on the clock, so a program legal today can violate r6 in a later year. That is inherent to r5 + r6 and IS handled correctly (the check runs on the effective sum, proven by the 1620 probe above), but nothing pins it.
test-needed: a checking-ON conformance case pinning both r6 edges (sum 1699 and sum 10000 rejected, 1700 and 9999 accepted), a case asserting the abort for an out-of-long argument-2, and a pinned-clock case for the defaulted-argument-2 r6 abort. tests/conformance/2002/intrinsics_date_window.cob (read on disk) exercises no r6 boundary at all.

subject: DAY-TO-YYYYDDD function
notes:
⛔ OVERTURNED: CONFORMS -> PARTIAL. The adjudicator recorded the defect INSIDE the CONFORMS row ('OBSERVATION, NOT A DIVERGENCE ... recorded so the row is not read as cleaner than it is') and closed it anyway. A finding worth writing down is a row that must stay open - a closed row never gets revisited. Citations re-validated: `cite.py --check 15.25.4 "The equivalent arithmetic expression is as follows"`, `--check 15.25.4 "FUNCTION YEAR-TO-YYYY (YY, argument-2, argument-3)"` and `--check 15.25.4 "In the year 2002 the returned value for FUNCTION DAY-TO-YYYYDDD (10004, 20) is 2010004"` -> all OK (rule path 1).
THE LEGAL DOMAIN - VERIFIED, AND I REPRODUCED EVERY VALUE. `return YearToYyyy(day / 1000, off, baseYear) * 1000 + day % 1000;` is r1 literally: a BY-REFERENCE delegation to the ONE §15.100.4 windowing core, matching r1's own by-reference definition, with no second copy of the algorithm. The substitutions are exact over the r1-legal domain - r1 defines YY = FUNCTION INTEGER(argument-1/1000) (floor) and nnn = FUNCTION MOD(argument-1, 1000); §15.25.3 r1 constrains argument-1 positive, so both operands are non-negative and C#'s truncating `/` coincides with floor while `%` coincides with MOD; the sign case is unreachable. RE-RAN the standard's own worked values end-to-end through the compiler with a pinned clock so the DEFAULTED argument-3 is deterministic: NOTE 1 first example, COBOLNET_CLOCK=2002-06-15, `FUNCTION DAY-TO-YYYYDDD(10004, 20)` -> N1=2010004; NOTE 1 second example, COBOLNET_CLOCK=2013-06-15, `FUNCTION DAY-TO-YYYYDDD(95005, (-10))` -> N2=1995005. Hand-derived edges re-run (argument-3 = 2002, argument-2 = 50): argument-1 = 1 -> 2000001; argument-1 = 99999 -> 1999999; nnn = 0 via 10000 -> 2010000; sum 1700 -> 1700010; sum 9999 -> 9999365. RECEIVER VARIED (the PB5 lesson the brief calls out) - PIC 9(7), PIC S9(18)V9(9), PIC 9(31) via a *10^18 composite, PIC S9(9)V99 via /8, PIC 9(4), and a COMP-2 receiver: all correct (2010004 / +2010004.000000000 / 2010004000000000000000000 / +251250.50 / truncated 0004 / 2010004), so no receiver scale hides a defect. Composition also holds: `FUNCTION TEST-DAY-YYYYDDD(FUNCTION DAY-TO-YYYYDDD(10004, 20, 2002))` -> 00 (valid), which is the §15.25.3 NOTE's own suggested use.
WHY NOT CONFORMS - THE RETURNED VALUE ON THE EC PATH IS SELF-INCONSISTENT AND CONTRADICTS THE IMPLEMENTATION'S OWN DOCUMENTED DEFINITION. §15.3 (validated): 'If the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist and checking for EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION is not enabled, the implementor defines the result of the function reference' - so the implementor is obliged to DEFINE it, and under §4.2.16 to document it. CobolDate.cs documents it in two places ('Violations -> EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION (§15.3, default 0)'). RAN with checking OFF, one program, three references:
       FUNCTION DAY-TO-YYYYDDD(0, 20, 2002)      -> A1ZERO-OFF=0000000   (matches the documented default)
       FUNCTION DAY-TO-YYYYDDD(100000, 20, 2002) -> A1HIGH-OFF=0000000   (matches)
       FUNCTION DAY-TO-YYYYDDD(99365, 20, 9999)  -> SUMHIGH-OFF=0000365  (does NOT match)
       FUNCTION DAY-TO-YYYYDDD(10004, 20, 1601)  -> LEAK=0000004         (does NOT match)
An argument-1 violation returns the documented 0 because DayToYyyyddd raises before the composite; an r4/r6 violation returns `0 * 1000 + nnn` because the wrapper multiplies the delegated core's EC default and adds nnn on top. Two different implementor-defined results for one function, only one of them documented. This IS this row's subject - the returned value - and it is exactly the half a CONFORMS would bury. Fix with the AR-15.25.3-4 sentinel work: make the delegated core's EC state visible to the wrapper so the composite returns the documented default instead of manufacturing a value out of a failed evaluation.
TEST: tests/conformance/2002/intrinsics_date_window.cob and its .out are both on disk; T10 = `FUNCTION DAY-TO-YYYYDDD(10004, 20, 2002)` -> 2010004 and T11 = `FUNCTION DAY-TO-YYYYDDD(95005, -10, 2013)` -> 1995005, with the derivation written into the case as comments citing §15.25.4 NOTE 1. Spec-derived and exercises this rule over the legal domain. (tests/conformance/negative/date_window_below_2002.cob covers only the D8 edition gate.) test-needed: a checking-OFF case pinning the EC-path returned value for an r4/r6 violation against the documented default.

subject: DISPLAY-OF function
notes:
UPHELD on re-review, and REPRODUCED independently. The 15.26.3 r1 screen exists and fires for elementary operands, but it FAILS OPEN for every shape whose static category the binder cannot name.
SPEC (each re-validated with cite.py --check, not inherited): 15.26.3 r1 'Argument-1 shall be of class national'; 15.3 argument type 9 'A national group item, a national literal, or an elementary data item of class national shall be specified'; 8.5.2.1 '- an alphanumeric group item has class and category alphanumeric'. An alphanumeric group is therefore NOT an admissible argument-1, and 15.3 makes an incorrect argument an EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION.
CODE: CheckRepertoireArgs guards on 'OperandCategory(args[0]) is { } c1', and OperandCategory is 'BoundFieldOperand f => f.Place.Item.IsGroup ? null : f.Place.Item.Pic?.Category' - null for EVERY group and for every BoundFigurative / BoundAllLiteral - so the whole class arm is skipped.
RAN MYSELF (--std 2023, exit 0, NO diagnostic, prints 'R=ABCDEF'):
       IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. REFDOF01.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01 A-GRP.
          05 A-1 PIC X(3) VALUE "ABC".
          05 A-2 PIC X(3) VALUE "DEF".
       01 A-DEST PIC X(6).
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN.
           MOVE FUNCTION DISPLAY-OF(A-GRP) TO A-DEST.
           DISPLAY "R=" A-DEST.
           STOP RUN.
Spec-correct: COBOLNET1546, exactly as the elementary PIC X(3) / PIC 9(4) shapes already are.
SECOND LEG, also ran: FUNCTION DISPLAY-OF(SPACE) binds clean and dies at RUN time with NotImplementedCobolFeatureException 'intrinsic string argument BoundFigurative'. A figurative constant is admissible wherever a rule allows a literal (8.3.3.6.3 SR1 'A figurative constant may be used whenever 'literal' appears in a format or when a rule allows it' - cite.py --check OK on 8.3.3.6.3, and it FAILS on the one-level-short 8.3.3.6) and its length is one character (8.3.3.6.4 GR3 b). Under EITHER reading the compiler is wrong: if legal it must convert, if illegal it must diagnose - it does neither. Same for FUNCTION DISPLAY-OF(ALL "A").
LATENT THIRD LEG (record it, do not fix blind): OperandCategory has no NationalEdited member at all - I read the PicCategory enum in Binding/Model/PicInfo.cs - so once the COBOLNET0899 national-edited residue lands, a category-national-edited item, which IS class national, will be FALSELY REJECTED by this same arm. The mis-fire is already observable: 01 N-ED PIC NNBNN as argument-1 emits COBOLNET1546 'argument-1 shall be of class national' alongside the 0899.
CORRECTLY ACCEPTED, verified by running: PIC N(5) item, N"ABC" literal, a NATIONAL GROUP (15.3 type 9), a national item's reference modification, and the zero-length national literal N"" (note that 15.26.3 has NO 'shall not be a zero-length literal' rule - its 15.66.3 r3 twin does - so accepting N"" is correct).
ROOT CAUSE - ONE RULE, TWO PLACES: the 15.3 class screen exists twice, as IntrinsicArgumentRules.ClassOf (which DOES classify groups) and as this hand-written repertoire arm (which does not). DISPLAY-OF is in NEITHER IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified NOR DeliberatelyUnscreened - I read both dictionaries - so the drift test cannot hold the two in agreement. Fix: drive CheckRepertoireArgs from IntrinsicArgumentRules.ClassOf and record the row. Caution: IntrinsicBinder.OperandCategory is RIGHT about ref-mod (8.4.3.3.4 GR3 keeps the item's class); IntrinsicArgumentRules.ClassOfPlace's blanket 'RefModPlace => Alphanumeric' is the wrong half.
TEST: conformance:negative/display-of-wrong-category verified on disk with its .err (COBOLNET1546) and registered in tests/conformance/negative/manifest.json - but it covers ONLY the elementary alphanumeric leg. test-needed for the group leg, the figurative leg and the ALL-literal leg.
EDITIONS: 85 excluded because class national does not exist in COBOL-85, so 15.26.3 r1 is unsatisfiable there; national data and the DISPLAY-OF/NATIONAL-OF pair were introduced by ISO/IEC 1989:2002, and Annex E of the 2023 text lists NO change to 15.26 (grepped), so 2014 and 2023 are identical. Derived from the standard's own history + Annex E, NOT from the IntrinsicCatalog row (I did check that a --std 85 compile is refused, but the refusing diagnostic COBOLNET1502 reads the catalog row, so it is a consistency check, not the source of the window).

notes:

subject: DISPLAY-OF function
notes:
UPHELD, with both halves re-verified from scratch rather than inherited. The rule carries TWO obligations and only the first is discharged.
HALF ONE - the conversion - VERIFIED. DisplayOf routes to the ONE Repertoire translator ('toNational || c <= 0xFF ? c : sub ?? Sub()'), which keeps a code point <= 0xFF and substitutes otherwise. Ran: DISPLAY-OF(PIC N(5) VALUE N"HELLO") -> HELLO; DISPLAY-OF(N"ABC") -> ABC; DISPLAY-OF(N"") -> zero-length.
HALF TWO - 'The implementor shall define the correspondence of characters between the alphanumeric character set and the national character set' - NOT discharged, in two independent ways.
(a) NOT DOCUMENTED. Annex A is NORMATIVE (I checked the annex header: '## Annex A' followed by '(normative)'), and A.1 item 33 (cite.py --check A.1 'correspondence between alphanumeric and national characters' OK) reads 'Computer's coded character set (correspondence between alphanumeric and national characters). This item is required. This item shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation. (... 15.26, DISPLAY-OF function, Returned value rules 1 and 3 ...)'. I grepped docs/CONFORMANCE.md (285 lines) for 15.26, DISPLAY-OF and 'Computer's coded': the only hit in the whole file is an unrelated 14.9.33 line. The correspondence is stated only in source comments and design docs.
(b) DEFINED TWO CONTRADICTORY WAYS. DISPLAY-OF's correspondence assumes an 8-bit Latin-1 alphanumeric set (Repertoire substitutes above 0xFF) while fix-queue CA26 LANDED the opposite declaration ('the native alphanumeric repertoire is UTF-16 ... no longer 8-bit-aliased', CONFORMANCE-FIX-QUEUE.md CA26). I PROVED BOTH SIDES IN ONE RUN at --std 2023 (source UTF-8, U+4E16): MOVE the character into 01 A-1 PIC X(1) then FUNCTION ORD(A-1) -> ORD-ANUM=019991, so a PIC X item holds it and it IS in the alphanumeric collating sequence; then MOVE N"<U+4E16>" to 01 N-1 PIC N(1), MOVE FUNCTION DISPLAY-OF(N-1) TO A-1, FUNCTION ORD(A-1) -> ORD-DOF=000064, the ordinal of '?'. The same character is simultaneously a member of the alphanumeric character set and has 'no corresponding alphanumeric character representation'.
NOT charged as DIVERGES: r1 leaves the correspondence to the implementor and a PARTIAL correspondence is contemplated by r1's 'if any' and by r3, so the current behaviour is defensible under the D-N4 declaration. PARTIAL because the implementor has to pick ONE declaration and write it down, and has done neither.
CROSS-REFERENCE, not double-charged: FUNCTION DISPLAY-OF(SPACE) - a legal argument-1 shape under 8.3.3.6.3 SR1 - crashes at run time, so r1's conversion cannot even be reached for that shape; booked under AR-15.26.3-1.
FIX SHAPE: reconcile Repertoire's 0xFF boundary with the declared repertoire (per CA26's landed disposition, upward to UTF-16, which retires DISPLAY-OF's substitution path entirely) AND add the Annex A.1 item 33 row to docs/CONFORMANCE.md. One owner-ratifiable change set, not two.

subject: DISPLAY-OF function
notes:
OVERTURNED CONFORMS -> DIVERGES. The prior adjudication verified only the shapes that happen to render and missed a legal argument-2 shape on which the compiler produces no returned value at all.
SPEC: 15.26.4 r2 'If argument-2 is specified, the alphanumeric substitution character is returned for each national character in argument-1 that has no corresponding alphanumeric character representation' (cite.py --check 15.26.4 OK). 15.3 argument type 2 admits 'an alphanumeric literal', and 8.3.3.6.3 SR1 - 'A figurative constant may be used whenever 'literal' appears in a format or when a rule allows it' (cite.py --check 8.3.3.6.3 OK; the one-level-short 8.3.3.6 FAILS --check) - extends that to a figurative constant, whose length is one character per 8.3.3.6.4 GR3 b 'When a figurative constant is other than ALL literal-1, the length of the string is one character' (--check OK). SPACE and QUOTE are therefore legal one-character-position class-alphanumeric argument-2 values.
RAN MYSELF (--std 2023, source UTF-8, 01 N-W PIC N(3) holding N"A<U+4E16>B"):
           MOVE FUNCTION DISPLAY-OF(N-W, SPACE) TO A-DEST.
compiles with NO diagnostic and terminates with
  Unhandled exception. CobolNet.Runtime.NotImplementedCobolFeatureException: ... intrinsic string argument 'BoundFigurative'
Identical with QUOTE. Spec-correct is 'A B' - the space substituted for U+4E16. The finding is robust to the spec reading: if the figurative is legal the substitution character must be returned; if it is not legal it must be diagnosed at compile time - accept-then-crash is wrong either way.
ROOT CAUSE: IntrinsicRenderer.RenderString has no BoundFigurative arm and falls through to NotImplemented.Value, and IntrinsicBinder.OperandCategory returns null for BoundFigurative so nothing rejects it at bind either - the same fail-open null that AR-15.26.3-1/-2 record. It is a shared gap (FUNCTION UPPER-CASE(SPACE) fails identically - I ran the control), which makes it a pattern to sweep, not a reason to leave this row green.
WHAT DOES WORK, verified by running each: a literal "#" -> A#B; a PIC X(1) item; a PIC A(1) item; a one-character GROUP -> A@B; a reference-modified A-SUB(1:1) -> A@B; a nested function FUNCTION CHAR(67) -> ABB (correct - ordinal position 67 is 'B'); and the r2/r3 split is honoured, since with argument-2 present Sub() is never reached so no EXCEPTION-STATUS is set (I ran it with the argument-2 form FIRST in the program so the blank cannot be a stale register).
TEST: conformance-test:NationalBooleanLiteralTests.NationalLiteral_NonLatin1Char_Accepted_DisplayOfSubstitutes verified on disk (tests/Cobol.Net.Tests.Conformance/NationalBooleanLiteralTests.cs, 'public sealed class NationalBooleanLiteralTests') and is spec-derived - it asserts Equal("A?B\nA#B"), computed from r2/r3, not pinned from behaviour. It covers only the literal argument-2 leg. test-needed for the figurative leg.
EDITIONS: 85 excluded because class national does not exist in COBOL-85, so 15.26.3 r1 is unsatisfiable there; national data and the DISPLAY-OF/NATIONAL-OF pair were introduced by ISO/IEC 1989:2002, and Annex E of the 2023 text lists NO change to 15.26 (grepped), so 2014 and 2023 are identical. Derived from the standard's own history + Annex E, NOT from the IntrinsicCatalog row (I did check that a --std 85 compile is refused, but the refusing diagnostic COBOLNET1502 reads the catalog row, so it is a consistency check, not the source of the window).

subject: DISPLAY-OF function
notes:
OVERTURNED CONFORMS -> DIVERGES. The prior adjudication verified the EC half from ONE statement shape (a MOVE) and generalized. The exception condition is raised only from the handful of verbs a hand-maintained switch happens to list; from every other statement the substitution happens and the EC is NOT set.
SPEC: 15.26.4 r3 '... an implementor-defined substitution character is used as the corresponding alphanumeric character and the EC-DATA-CONVERSION exception condition is set to exist' (cite.py --check 15.26.4 OK). EC-DATA-CONVERSION is NONFATAL - 'EC-DATA-CONVERSION | NF' is in Table 13, which lives in 14.6.13.1.6, NOT in 14.6.13.1.1 (both --check'ed; 14.6.13.1.1 is where the checking gate lives: 'if checking for an exception condition is not enabled, the exception condition will not be raised'). So limiting the raise to a >>TURN ... CHECKING ON region is correct; limiting it to SOME statements is not.
RAN MYSELF - ONE program, ONE checking directive, self-controlling (--std 2023, source UTF-8, 01 N-W PIC N(3) holding N"A<U+4E16>B"):
       >>TURN EC-DATA-CONVERSION CHECKING ON
           STRING FUNCTION DISPLAY-OF(N-W) DELIMITED BY SIZE
              INTO A-DEST.
           DISPLAY "AFTER-STRING STR=[" A-DEST "] EC=["
              FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATUS "]".
           MOVE FUNCTION DISPLAY-OF(N-W) TO A-DEST.
           DISPLAY "AFTER-MOVE   STR=[" A-DEST "] EC=["
              FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATUS "]".
prints
  AFTER-STRING STR=[A?B---] EC=[                               ]
  AFTER-MOVE   STR=[A?B   ] EC=[EC-DATA-CONVERSION             ]
The STRING DID perform the r3 substitution - the '?' is in the receiver - yet no exception condition was set; the very next MOVE, same program, same directive, sets it. So this is not a stale/cleared register and not a checking-scope artefact. PERFORM UNTIL FUNCTION DISPLAY-OF(N-W) = "A?B" behaves the same way (verified with the identical two-statement control), and so does an EVALUATE whose only branch is WHEN OTHER.
ROOT CAUSE - a hand-maintained list where a structure belongs: EcBinder attaches the ambient gate only when ContainsIntrinsic(node) is true, and ContainsIntrinsic delegates to DirectIntrinsic, a switch enumerating exactly BoundDisplay, BoundMove, BoundCompute, BoundComputeBoolean, the six arithmetic nodes, BoundIf's condition, BoundSetTo and BoundEvaluate's WHEN matches, with '_ => false' for everything else. STRING, UNSTRING, INSPECT, INITIALIZE, CALL/INVOKE arguments, WRITE/REWRITE FROM, SEARCH, RAISE, the PERFORM UNTIL/VARYING condition and the EVALUATE SUBJECT are all absent, so neither EC-DATA-CONVERSION nor its EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION twin (same predicate, the adjacent line in EcBinder) can ever be raised from them. The fix is a total walk over the statement's own expression positions plus a drift test, not eight more case arms.
SECOND, INDEPENDENT HALF ALSO OPEN: r3's 'implementor-defined substitution character' is one of the elements normative Annex A.1 item 33 requires be documented in the implementor's user documentation - item 33's cross-reference list names '15.26, DISPLAY-OF function, Returned value rules 1 AND 3'. docs/CONFORMANCE.md carries no such entry (grepped; see RV-15.26.4-1).
WHAT IS CORRECT: Sub() returns '?' and calls ExceptionState.DataConversionError, which does Set("EC-DATA-CONVERSION", fatal: false) when DataConversionChecking is on; EcEmitter's NonfatalAmbientGates sets/resets that flag in a try/finally around the statement. Verified live from a MOVE, a DISPLAY, an IF condition and a nested FUNCTION LENGTH(FUNCTION DISPLAY-OF(...)), each isolated in its own program so the register cannot carry over. With checking OFF the substitution stands and nothing is raised, which is the 14.6.13.1.1 gate, not a miss.
TEST: the cited conformance-test exists on disk and is spec-derived, but it - and conformance:2002/national_intrinsics - run with checking OFF, so they cover only r3's substitution half. test-needed: a case with '>>TURN EC-DATA-CONVERSION CHECKING ON' asserting FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATUS, and it must exercise a NON-MOVE statement or it will pass straight over the defect.
EDITIONS: 85 excluded because class national does not exist in COBOL-85, so 15.26.3 r1 is unsatisfiable there; national data and the DISPLAY-OF/NATIONAL-OF pair were introduced by ISO/IEC 1989:2002, and Annex E of the 2023 text lists NO change to 15.26 (grepped), so 2014 and 2023 are identical. Derived from the standard's own history + Annex E, NOT from the IntrinsicCatalog row (I did check that a --std 85 compile is refused, but the refusing diagnostic COBOLNET1502 reads the catalog row, so it is a consistency check, not the source of the window).

subject: DISPLAY-OF function
notes: UPHELD after varying the RECEIVER as well as the argument. Repertoire appends exactly one character per input character (a substitution replaces, never expands or drops), so the returned string's length is always argument-1's character count, and under D-N1 one national position is one UTF-16 char and one usage-display position. RAN MYSELF at --std 2023: FUNCTION LENGTH(FUNCTION DISPLAY-OF(PIC N(5))) -> 005; the same over a PIC N(3) containing a SUBSTITUTED U+4E16 -> 003, so substitution does not change the length; the ZERO-LENGTH national literal FUNCTION DISPLAY-OF(N"") -> LENGTH 000 and an all-space receiver, which is correct since 15.26.3 carries no zero-length-literal prohibition (its 15.66.3 r3 twin does); a SUPPLEMENTARY-plane national literal in a PIC N(2) -> LENGTH 002 and '??', consistent with the declared D-N1 one-code-unit-per-position model; a reference-modified argument N-SRC(1:3) -> 3; a national GROUP of two PIC N(2) items -> 4. Receiver variation: STRING FUNCTION DISPLAY-OF(N-SRC) DELIMITED BY SIZE INTO a PIC X(10) prefilled with '-' gives [HELLO-----], i.e. exactly 5 positions transferred; MOVE to a PIC X(6) gives 'HELLO '; and the length consequence in comparison is right in both directions - the result compares EQUAL to "HELLO", to "HELLO   " and to a PIC X(8) item, so the shorter operand is space-padded per 8.8.4.1.1 rather than compared as a raw .NET string. There is no static width model for an intrinsic result in the compiler, so the length is purely the runtime string's and FUNCTION LENGTH reads that. conformance:2002/national_intrinsics verified on disk with its golden (LEN-D=05) and its tests/conformance/2002/manifest.json entry; the LEN-D line is computed from 15.26.4 r4, not pinned from behaviour. NOTED, and deliberately not charged here: FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH(FUNCTION DISPLAY-OF(N-W)) crashes at run time with a NotImplementedCobolFeatureException naming 'ISO 15.14.3' - that is a 15.14 argument-shape gap for whoever adjudicates BYTE-LENGTH, not a 15.26.4 r4 defect.

subject: E function
notes: OVERTURNED - the adjudicator recorded CONFORMS. It verified only the FIRST half of the rule (is the value an approximation?) and asserted a second-half fact that is FALSE. test-needed. Citations re-validated: cite.py --check 15.27.3 'implementor-defined approximation' -> OK (rule 1); cite.py --check 15.4.1 'the characteristics and representation of the returned value are defined by the implementor' -> OK; cite.py --check A.1 'Function returned values (characteristics, representation, and returned value for native arithmetic)' -> OK (A.1 item 92: 'This item is REQUIRED. The value returned does not have to be documented' - i.e. the VALUE is free, the CHARACTERISTICS and REPRESENTATION are a required documented item). HALF 1 - THE VALUE - CONFORMS, re-measured by me, wider than the adjudicator's sweep. CobolIntrinsics.E() => Math.E, routed by IntrinsicRenderer.RenderFloat (catalog row Float:true) which keeps the raw double for a float receiver and otherwise quantizes through the one CobolIntrinsics.FromDouble at ws = max(Receiver.Scale, 9). Measured at --std 2023: PIC 9.9(5) -> 2.71828; PIC 9.9(9) -> 2.718281828; PIC 9.9(17) -> 2.71828182845904512; PIC 9V9(19) -> 2.7182818284590452736; PIC 9V9(30) -> 2.718281828459045010062878703616; PIC 9V9(30) COMP-3 -> same; PIC 9V9(17) COMP -> 2.71828182845904512; COMP-2 -> 2.718281828459045; COMP-1 -> 2.7182817. 15.4.1 sets NO accuracy floor under native ('the value returned is an implementor-defined approximation'), so each of these satisfies rule 1. THE PB5 SATURATION LEG IS GENUINELY CLOSED and I re-derived the reason instead of trusting it: FromDouble now returns Int128 and saturates only at |d * 10^scale| >= 1.7e38, which for e needs scale >= 38, while the compiler caps a fixed-point item at 31 digits (COBOLNET0801 rejects PIC 9V9(31) as 32 digit positions), so saturation is unreachable from any declarable receiver. (PIC V9(31) prints 0.7182818284590446722929066508288 - that is ordinary high-order size truncation of a 2.7 value into an all-fraction receiver, not a returned-value defect.) HALF 2 - THE CHARACTERISTICS - FAILS. 15.4.1 grants the native latitude only in the same breath as 'the characteristics and representation of the returned value are DEFINED BY THE IMPLEMENTOR', and A.1 item 92 makes documenting them a REQUIRED item. COBOL.NET's discharge of A.1 item 92 is the docs/CONFORMANCE.md section-7 row keyed '- (15.4.1 / 14.9.11.4 GR1)', whose determination reads: 'A FLOAT-valued function (SQRT, trig, financial) renders through the same shortest-round-trip CobolFloat.Display a COMP-2 item does, SO THE FUNCTION AND AN ITEM HOLDING ITS VALUE AGREE.' That published determination is FALSE, on its own named example as well as on E. Verified input, run at --std 2023: 'IDENTIFICATION DIVISION. PROGRAM-ID. EDOC01. DATA DIVISION. WORKING-STORAGE SECTION. 01 D2 USAGE COMP-2. PROCEDURE DIVISION. MAIN-PARA. DISPLAY "DISP-FUNC-E =" FUNCTION E. COMPUTE D2 = FUNCTION E. DISPLAY "ITEM-HOLDING=" D2. MOVE FUNCTION E TO D2. DISPLAY "MOVE-INTO-D2=" D2. DISPLAY "DISP-SQRT2  =" FUNCTION SQRT(2). COMPUTE D2 = FUNCTION SQRT(2). DISPLAY "ITEM-SQRT2  =" D2. STOP RUN.' prints DISP-FUNC-E =2.718281828 / ITEM-HOLDING=2.718281828459045 / MOVE-INTO-D2=2.718281828 / DISP-SQRT2  =1.414213562 / ITEM-SQRT2  =1.4142135623730951. The function and an item holding its value do NOT agree, in either case. ROOT CAUSE, read in the code: RenderFloat branches on num.Receiver (Real -> raw binary64, else FromDouble at max(Receiver.Scale,9)), and num.Receiver is populated on the COMPUTE path but not on the MOVE / DISPLAY / relation-condition paths, so the SAME function returns a different value in the SAME receiver depending on the STATEMENT: 'MOVE FUNCTION E TO <COMP-2>' yields 2.718281828 (10 significant digits) where COMPUTE into the identical item yields 2.718281828459045 (16); 'MOVE FUNCTION E TO PIC 9V9(30)' yields 2.718281828000000000000000000000 where COMPUTE into the identical item yields 2.718281828459045010062878703616; 'MOVE FUNCTION E TO PIC 9.9(17)' yields 2.71828182800000000. Each result is still AN approximation, which is why this is PARTIAL and not DIVERGES - but there is no single implementor-defined characteristic to document, and the one that IS documented is contradicted. ACTIONABLE: thread the receiver into the MOVE / DISPLAY / condition operand channels so RenderFloat sees the real receiver (the same seam the DIVERGES row RV-15.27.3-3 must touch), then correct or re-derive the docs/CONFORMANCE.md section-7 A.1-item-92 row to match. TEST COVERAGE: none - no test under tests/ references FUNCTION E in any spelling; a spec-derived golden computing 2.71828... from rule 1's own constant, exercising COMPUTE and MOVE into the SAME receiver, is needed.

subject: E function
notes: Verdict SURVIVES; the note is corrected and the SPEC BASIS the adjudicator missed is supplied. test-needed. Citations re-validated: cite.py --check 15.27.3 'standard-binary arithmetic is in effect' -> OK (rule 2). THE PRECONDITION CAN NEVER HOLD IN THIS COMPILER, re-verified by me on the built CLI: DataBinder.BindDeclarations rejects the mode with COBOLNET0806 'ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY is an obsolete feature (ISO 8.8.1.4.1 NOTE 1 / Annex F) and is not supported; use NATIVE or STANDARD-DECIMAL' - a HARD error at --std 2002 (alongside COBOLNET0900 'requires COBOL-2014'), 2014 and 2023, and NOT downgradable by --permissive (2023 adds the COBOLNET0903 obsolescence warning and still errors). Nothing in the tree computes 14114126198520207781233383725636853 / (2 ** 112); CobolIntrinsics.E() is the only body and is Math.E in every mode. WHAT THE ADJUDICATOR MISSED, and it is what makes this an owner DECISION rather than a bug: the standard itself classes this clause as processor-dependent. Annex A.3 item 2, validated verbatim - cite.py --check A.3 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor' -> OK - and 4.5 NOTE, validated verbatim ('These factors can include the use of optional, processor-dependent, or implementor-defined language elements'), together mean a conforming implementation may fail to translate a compilation group that uses it without ceasing to conform. Annex F.2 additionally makes STANDARD-BINARY an obsolete feature, and the standard's own Annex E remark records that it 'has not been implemented as of the writing of this revision by any COBOL provider'. The non-support is already recorded at docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 2 row 2 ('| 2 | ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY | 11.9.5 | Not claimed | Obsolete feature (A.3 NOTE 1); the native/standard-decimal modes are provided |') - the DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT shape, a verdict only the owner may set, hence NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION. BARE QUESTION: should 15.27.3 rule 2 be recorded as discharged by the existing documented non-support of ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY (Annex A.3 item 2 processor-dependence) rather than carried as an open inventory GAP? Identical to the already-adjudicated sibling RV-15.73.3-2 for PI; one decision should settle the whole 15.4.1 family. EDITIONS DERIVED INDEPENDENTLY OF INTRINSICCATALOG: the STANDARD-BINARY keyword of the ARITHMETIC clause is a COBOL-2014 addition (the 2002 clause offered NATIVE and STANDARD only; the compiler's own edition gate agrees - 'OPTIONS. ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY.' at --std 2002 draws COBOLNET0900 'requires COBOL-2014 (targeting COBOL-2002)', re-run by me), so the rule's precondition cannot arise at 85 or 2002. TEST COVERAGE: none - no test references FUNCTION E under any arithmetic mode. The honest cover is a negative case pinning that FUNCTION E under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY is refused BY MODE; a mode-only rejection test that never names E would not cover this row.

subject: E function
notes: Verdict SURVIVES - independently reproduced by this refuter; two citation errors in the adjudicator's note are corrected and the required value is re-derived. test-needed. Citations re-validated: cite.py --check 15.27.3 'standard-decimal arithmetic is in effect' -> OK (rule 3); cite.py --check 15.4.1 'the returned value shall equal the value of the equivalent arithmetic expression' -> OK; cite.py --check 8.8.1.5.2 '128-bit basic decimal interchange format' -> OK. CORRECTED CITATION: the truncation rule for a COMPUTE without ROUNDED is 14.7.4.3 GR2, validated verbatim ('If the ROUNDED phrase is not specified, execution is as if ROUNDED MODE IS TRUNCATION had been specified') - the adjudicator's '14.7.4' is ONE LEVEL SHORT and cite.py --check 14.7.4 'truncation' FAILS. REQUIRED VALUE RE-DERIVED: rule 3 gives the exact 2.718281828459045235360287471352662 (34 significant digits) and 8.8.1.5.2 makes the standard-decimal intermediate data item exact for everything representable in decimal128, i.e. 34 significant digits, so the whole constant is required - it is not clipped by the intermediate. FAILING COBOL INPUT, RUN BY ME at BOTH --std 2014 and --std 2023: 'IDENTIFICATION DIVISION. PROGRAM-ID. ESD02. OPTIONS. ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL. DATA DIVISION. WORKING-STORAGE SECTION. 01 R17 PIC 9.9(17). 01 R30 PIC 9V9(30). PROCEDURE DIVISION. MAIN-PARA. COMPUTE R17 = FUNCTION E. DISPLAY "SD-R17=" R17. COMPUTE R30 = FUNCTION E. DISPLAY "SD-R30=" R30. IF FUNCTION E = 2.7182818284590452353602874713 DISPLAY "EAE-EQ=TRUE" ELSE DISPLAY "EAE-EQ=FALSE" END-IF. STOP RUN.' prints SD-R17=2.71828182845904512, SD-R30=2718281828459045010062878703616 and EAE-EQ=FALSE. Truncated to those receivers rule 3 requires 2.71828182845904523 and 2.718281828459045235360287471352, and 15.4.1 NOTE 2 requires the relation 'function-identifier = equivalent-arithmetic-expression' to be TRUE - it prints FALSE. The standard-decimal output is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the native output, i.e. the arithmetic mode is ignored for this function. (Aside worth recording for the fix's test: the full 34-digit constant cannot be written as a COBOL literal at all - COBOLNET0801 rejects it against the 31-digit fixed-point literal limit of 8.3.3.3.2, validated: 'The implementor shall allow for fixed-point numeric literals of 1 through 31 digits in length' - so the NOTE-2 relation test has to be written at 31 digits or fewer.) ANNEX A.3 DOES NOT EXCUSE THIS, and the distinction matters because it is what separates this row from RV-15.27.3-2: A.3 item 3 does make ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL processor-dependent, but COBOL.NET ACCEPTS the clause and advertises it (the COBOLNET0806 text tells the user to 'use NATIVE or STANDARD-DECIMAL'), so having claimed the mode it owes the mode's semantics. ROOT CAUSE, read in the code: E's IntrinsicCatalog row is Float:true, so IntrinsicRenderer.RenderFloat is taken unconditionally and never consults num.StandardDecimal (only the MeanScaled arm does), and E is absent from the IntrinsicBinder.BindIntrinsicCore staged-loud list, which holds only ANNUITY / PRESENT-VALUE / VARIANCE / STANDARD-DEVIATION. THE PREMISE BEHIND THAT OMISSION IS FALSE and it is written down in TWO places - the CobolIntrinsics.Float.cs class header and the BindIntrinsicCore staging comment - as 'the prose-"approximation" functions (SQRT, the trig/log family) have NO equivalent arithmetic expression - implementor-defined in every mode (15.4.1 last paragraph)'. It fails on two independent grounds: (a) 15.27.3 rule 3 says in so many words 'the EQUIVALENT ARITHMETIC EXPRESSION is the exact value of the arithmetic expression (2.718...)', so E demonstrably HAS one and 15.4.1's shall-equal rule bites; and (b) on the no-EAE reading, 15.4.1's last paragraph is 'its returned value is implementor-defined UNLESS OTHERWISE SPECIFIED IN THE FUNCTION DEFINITION' - and rules 2 and 3 are exactly that specification. Both comments must be corrected in the same change set. THE FIX MUST ALSO COVER ArithmeticMode.Standard AND --std 2002: I verified 'OPTIONS. ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD.' at --std 2002 prints the same SD-R17=2.71828182845904512 / SD-R30=2718281828459045010062878703616 / EAE-EQ=FALSE (at 2014 it warns COBOLNET0903 and still diverges; at 2023 the clause is correctly removed, COBOLNET0807). Editions are left at 2014,2023 because the NAMED standard-decimal mode is a COBOL-2014 introduction (re-verified: 'ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL' at --std 2002 -> COBOLNET0900 'requires COBOL-2014'), matching the convention already landed on the PI sibling row - but the fix and its test must cover ArithmeticMode.Standard at 2002/2014 as well. SIBLING: identical root cause adjudicated for PI at RV-15.73.3-3 - one fix. TEST COVERAGE: none - no test references FUNCTION E under any arithmetic mode.

subject: EXCEPTION-FILE function
notes: UPHELD on re-review, with a second witness. The rule has two halves; only the first is enforced. Half 1 ("shall be the NAME OF A FILE CONNECTOR") is enforced -- BindExceptionFileArg resolves argCtx.GetText() against ctx.Data.Files and emits COBOLNET1574 otherwise; re-ran `FUNCTION EXCEPTION-FILE(WS-ITEM)` over `01 WS-ITEM PIC X(5)` and got "error COBOLNET1574: FUNCTION EXCEPTION-FILE argument 'WS-ITEM' is not the name of a file connector specified in an FD statement (ISO 15.28.3 rule 1)". Half 2 ("that is specified in an FD statement" -- validated mechanically: cite.py --check 15.28.3 "shall be the name of a file connector that is specified in an FD" -> OK, and the PRINTED page (render-spec-page.py 874, folio 844) carries the same sentence) is NOT enforced. BindExceptionFileArg accepts any FileModel and never consults FileModel.IsSortMerge (set in DataBinder.cs for an SD -- ISO 13.4.6 Sort-merge file description entry). TWO ran witnesses, both compiling with ZERO diagnostics at --std 2023: (a) `SD SORTWK.` + `DISPLAY "SD=[" FUNCTION EXCEPTION-FILE(SORTWK) "]"` prints `SD=[  ]` -- an SD file-name is specified in an SD statement, not an FD one; (b) a file-name with a SELECT and NO file description entry at all (`SELECT NOFDF ASSIGN TO "refnofd.dat"`, no FD) -- `FUNCTION EXCEPTION-FILE(NOFDF)` also compiles silently and prints `  `. So the implemented predicate is 'is a known file-name', not 15.28.3's 'is specified in an FD statement'. The sibling arm already owns the guard -- SequentialIoBinder.cs rejects an SD file-name with "an SD file-name may appear only in SORT/MERGE/RELEASE/RETURN (ISO 13.4.6 SR3/SR4)" -- so this is that one guard missing on the EXCEPTION-FILE/-N path, and the fix is a FileModel-shaped predicate, not a second hand-written test. Compile-time diagnosis is the right disposition (ISO 4.2.2, syntactically distinguishable elements) and the compiler already takes that position for half 1. Editions: the whole rule text exists only from 2023 -- Annex E.3.3 item 25 (spec line 43962) "FUNCTION EXCEPTION-FILE. An optional argument has been added to this function"; derived from the Annex, not from the IntrinsicCatalog row. test-needed: no negative case on disk exercises the CONSTRAINT (no COBOLNET1574 case anywhere under tests/conformance/negative/, no SD or missing-FD witness); tests/conformance/2023/exception_file_arg.cob exercises only the conforming side (two FD file-names accepted).

subject: EXCEPTION-FILE function
notes:
OVERTURNED from CONFORMS. r1a and r1b hold; r1c is WRONG for two kinds of file connector, and the adjudication missed it by varying the exception ORIGIN while holding the connector KIND fixed at 'ordinary program file'.
WHAT HOLDS (re-run, not inherited). r1a: EcFunctions.File returns "00" when LastName is null or !ExceptionCatalog.IsIoName(name); ran `A=[00]` before any I-O, and also after `SET LAST EXCEPTION TO OFF` following a real 10-status READ (`B=[00]`, EXCEPTION-STATUS blank) -- correct, because 14.6.13.1.1 says the last exception status persists until re-raised or SET-cleared, so a later SUCCESSFUL statement must NOT reset it. r1b: ExceptionEngine.Set() nulls LastFile and only SetIo() populates it, so a NAMED raise structurally cannot carry a connector; ran `RAISE EXCEPTION EC-I-O-AT-END` after a 10-status READ -> `B=[  ]` with EXCEPTION-STATUS still EC-I-O-AT-END (genuinely the r1b branch, not r1a).
WHAT DIVERGES -- r1c, validated: cite.py --check 15.28.4 "exactly as specified in the SELECT clause" -> OK (15.28.4 1) c)), and the printed page 844 reads "The succeeding characters contain the file-name exactly as specified in the SELECT clause". The implementation does not carry the SELECT spelling: it recovers a display name by string surgery on the RUNTIME CONNECTOR KEY -- EcFunctions.File takes `file.LastIndexOf("::")` and returns everything after it. That key is an emit-side namespacing artifact, and for two connector kinds it is not the file-name.
FAILING INPUT 1 -- an OO per-object instance file. BinderDriver.QualifyClassFiles gives an OBJECT-paragraph file the key `Class::INST::NAME` and FileRegistry.MintInstanceKey then appends `#N`, which the `::` strip does not remove:
       >>TURN EC-I-O CHECKING ON
       ... PROGRAM-ID. REFOOF1. REPOSITORY. CLASS OFCLSR. 01 T USAGE OBJECT REFERENCE OFCLSR.
           INVOKE OFCLSR "NEW" RETURNING T.  INVOKE T "DOIT".  STOP RUN.
       CLASS-ID. OFCLSR. ... OBJECT. ... FILE-CONTROL. SELECT OFile ASSIGN TO "refoo-obj.dat".
       FD OFile. 01 OFILE-REC PIC X(12).
       METHOD-ID. DOIT. ... OPEN OUTPUT OFile / WRITE / CLOSE / OPEN INPUT OFile / READ OFile / READ OFile
           DISPLAY "NOARG=[" FUNCTION EXCEPTION-FILE "]".
ACTUAL `NOARG=[10OFile#1]` -- EXPECTED `NOARG=[10OFile]`. The SELECT clause says `OFile`; `#1` is the runtime's per-object key counter leaking into a user-visible function result.
FAILING INPUT 2 -- an EXTERNAL file. DataBinder.cs sets `file.ExternalName = name.ToUpperInvariant()` and BinderDriver keys the connector `::EXT:: + ExternalName`, so the SELECT spelling is destroyed before the strip ever runs:
       >>TURN EC-I-O CHECKING ON
       ... SELECT ExtF ASSIGN TO "refext1.dat".  FD ExtF IS EXTERNAL.  01 EREC PIC X(5).
           OPEN OUTPUT ExtF / WRITE / CLOSE / OPEN INPUT ExtF / READ ExtF / READ ExtF
           DISPLAY "NOARG=[" FUNCTION EXCEPTION-FILE "]".
ACTUAL `NOARG=[10EXTF]` -- EXPECTED `NOARG=[10ExtF]`. Both the SELECT and the FD spell it `ExtF`; nothing in 13.18.22 licenses folding the case of the returned string, and 15.28.4 r1c says "exactly as specified in the SELECT clause". That the implementation ALREADY takes spelling seriously elsewhere is the proof this is a defect and not pedantry: for an ordinary file `SELECT MyFile` + `FD MYFILE` correctly yields `10MyFile` (ran).
ROOT CAUSE (one rule, one place): the SELECT-clause spelling is a property of the FileModel and must be carried to the runtime connector as its OWN field, not re-derived by parsing a key whose format is owned by three different qualification sites (PROG::, ::EXT::, Class::INST::+#N, Class::FACT::, Class::SORT::). Every future key-shape change silently re-breaks 15.28.4 r1c/r2b the way ::INST:: and ::EXT:: already have.
Test coverage: the cited test exists on disk, is spec-derived (AssertSpec, expected "F: 10TF" computed from 9.1.13.1 status 10 + the SELECT name) and pins the ORDINARY-file r1c leg only. test-needed for r1a, for r1b, and for both failing legs above -- tests/conformance/2002/exception_file_n.cob covers the analogous 15.29.4 legs of the -N twin, a different function and clause, so it does not count here.

subject: EXCEPTION-FILE function
notes:
UPHELD, and I reproduced both the original failing input and a SECOND, independent failing leg it did not cover.
