Proposed fix-queue item DA8 (see AR-15.72.3-1). test-needed: a tests/conformance/negative fixture.

subject: ORD-MIN function
notes: The binder's only class logic for an ArgKinds "p" row is 'args.All(IsStringOperand)', which SELECTS the string-vs-numeric runtime body rather than VALIDATING that the arguments share a class (§15.72.3 rule 3), so a mixed-class list is silently accepted. Re-verified at --std 2023: with '01 N1 PIC 9(4) VALUE 7.' and '01 A1 PIC X(4) VALUE "0003".', 'MOVE FUNCTION ORD-MIN(N1 A1) TO R' compiles clean and prints 0002 — the alphanumeric operand is coerced onto the numeric path and 7 is compared against 3. National mixed with alphanumeric is accepted likewise. The PERMITTED alphabetic/alphanumeric mixture is correctly accepted and gives the right answer (PIC A(3) "BBB" + PIC X(3) "AAA" prints 0002) — PicInfo.PicCategory.Alphanumeric covers both PIC A and PIC X, so there is no false rejection to fix. Proposed fix-queue item DA8 (see AR-15.72.3-1). test-needed: negative fixtures for numeric+alphanumeric and national+alphanumeric, plus a positive fixture pinning the legal alphabetic/alphanumeric mixture so a future screen does not over-reject.

subject: ORD-MIN function
notes: PB2 LANDED. Same rule and same fix as AR/RV-15.71 - ORD-MIN's body is ORD-MAX's body with the comparison reversed, so fixing one without the other would have been the split the DA wave warned about (feedback_scan_all_similar).

subject: ORD-MIN function
notes: §8.8.4.2 is honoured on every path that actually emits a comparison: fixed-point numeric arguments are scale-ALIGNED before the unscaled Int128 compare (alignment makes unscaled comparison equal algebraic comparison, §8.8.1) — CLI-verified ORD-MIN(1.0 1.00 1)=1; string arguments go through CobolString.Compare, which space-extends the shorter operand (§8.8.4.2.7 r2 — verified ORD-MIN("A" "A ")=1) and honours the alphanumeric PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE — independently re-verified: under 'ALPHABET REVSEQ IS "Z" "Y" "X" "A" "B"' with PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE IS REVSEQ, ORD-MIN("A" "Z") returns 2 and the program's own 'IF "Z" < "A"' is TRUE, so the function and the relation condition agree — or the national PCS. PARTIAL for the SAME carrier holes as RV-15.72.4-1: a FLOAT-LONG/COMP-1/COMP-2 list, and (adversarial-pass addition) a division subexpression under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL, never reach a comparison at all because the emitted C# does not compile (CS1503 double/CobolDec -> Int128). Coverage gap: no test exercises the ORD-MIN PCS leg — tests/conformance/2002/intrinsic_max_collating.cob names ORD-MIN in its CA23 header comment but its body exercises only FUNCTION MAX, so it is deliberately NOT cited; only nist:IF129A is cited (numeric legs 01-07, unequal-length alphanumeric legs 08/09 which exercise the space padding). test-needed: an ORD-MIN PCS fixture and a float/decimal fixture.

subject: ORD-MIN function
notes: OVERTURNED from CONFORMS by the adversarial pass. The leftmost-wins selection itself is right on every path that emits one: both bodies update only on a STRICTLY-less compare (OrdMin: 'if (xs[i] < m)'; ExtremeIndex: 'if (max ? c > 0 : c < 0)'), CLI-verified ORD-MIN(3 3 3)=1, ORD-MIN(-1 0 -1)=1, ORD-MIN(1.0 1.00 1)=1, ORD-MIN("BB" "AA" "AA")=2, ORD-MIN("A" "A ")=1 (equal after §8.8.4.2.7 space padding), and NIST IF129A test (j) 'FUNCTION ORD-MIN(A, 5, 5, A)' with A PIC S9(10) VALUE 5 — four equal values, expected 1 — genuinely covers the tie. But the verdict cannot be CONFORMS: for the SAME operand shapes that make RV-15.72.4-1/-2 PARTIAL there is NO returned value at all, so rule 3 is unrealized there. Verified: '01 F1 USAGE COMP-2. 01 F2 USAGE COMP-2. MOVE 1.5 TO F1 MOVE 1.5 TO F2 MOVE FUNCTION ORD-MIN(F1 F2) TO R' — an exact tie that should return 1 — instead fails with raw Roslyn 'error CS1503: cannot convert from double to System.Int128'; the same happens for a division subexpression under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL (CobolDec -> Int128). Root cause and proposed owner are identical to RV-15.72.4-1 (DA9: float AND decimal legs for the Int128 variadic statistical family); this record must be re-adjudicated together with it. test-needed: a float/decimal tie fixture.

subject: PI function
notes: CobolIntrinsics.Pi() = Math.PI is a legitimate implementor-defined approximation of (3 + 0.1415926535897932384626433832795), and the documentation obligation is discharged: Annex A.1 item 92 (validated - 'Function returned values (characteristics, representation, and returned value for native arithmetic) ... The value returned does not have to be documented') exempts the VALUE while still requiring the characteristics/representation, and those ARE documented in CONFORMANCE.md SS7 (the row keyed '- (SS15.4.1 / SS14.9.11.4 GR1)', read and confirmed to state that a FLOAT-valued function renders through the same shortest-round-trip CobolFloat.Display a COMP-2 item does). PARTIAL for a receiver-shape leg, re-verified independently on the built CLI at --std 2023: IntrinsicRenderer.RenderFloat quantizes through the ONE FromDouble at ws = max(Receiver.Scale, 9), and FromDouble's scaled double exceeds Int64 at scale >= 19 and SATURATES to long.MaxValue with no size error and no diagnostic - '01 R19 PIC 9V9(19). COMPUTE R19 = FUNCTION PI. DISPLAY R19.' prints 0.9223372036854775807 and PIC 9V9(30) prints 0.000000000009223372036854775807. Neither is an approximation of pi, so rule 1 is violated for every legal 2002+ receiver of 20..31 digits (scale <= 18 is fine: PIC 9V9(18) prints 3.141592653589793280, within approximation license). Not PI-specific - the whole SS15.4.1 float family funnels through the same FromDouble. TEST COVERAGE: the cited test does compile-and-run and asserts the value 3.14159, so it genuinely covers rule 1's happy path, but only at PIC 9.9(5) and only at edition 2014 (AssertSpec dialect argument); the scale >= 19 saturation leg and editions 2002/2023 are test-needed.

subject: PI function
notes: EDITIONS CORRECTED to 2014,2023: standard-binary arithmetic is a COBOL-2014 introduction (ConstructRegistry row 'arithmetic-standard-binary-2014', IntroducedIn 2014, ObsoleteIn 2023), so this rule cannot apply at 2002 - confirmed empirically, the sibling STANDARD-DECIMAL clause is rejected at --std 2002 with COBOLNET0900 'requires COBOL-2014'. The rule's precondition can never hold: ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY is rejected at bind time with COBOLNET0806 (DataBinder.BindDeclarations), re-verified on the built CLI as a HARD error at both --std 2014 and --std 2023 and NOT downgradable by --permissive. No code computes the exact binary128 value 16312081666030376401667486162748272 / 2**112, and none can while the mode is refused. The non-support is already recorded in CONFORMANCE.md SS2 row 2 ('ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY | 11.9.5 | Not claimed | Obsolete feature (A.3 NOTE 1)') and licensed by ISO Annex A.3 item 2, validated verbatim: 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor.' BARE QUESTION: should SS15.73.3 rule 2 be recorded as discharged by that existing Annex A.3 item-2 non-support of ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY rather than carried as an open inventory GAP? TEST-REF STRUCK on review: the previously cited StandardDecimalTests.StandardBinary_DocumentedUnsupported exercises the MODE rejection and never references PI or any returned value, so it does not cover this rule - test-needed (a test pinning that FUNCTION PI under STANDARD-BINARY is refused by name would be the honest cover).

subject: PI function
notes: EDITIONS CORRECTED to 2014,2023: standard-decimal arithmetic is a COBOL-2014 introduction (ConstructRegistry row 'arithmetic-standard-decimal-2014', IntroducedIn 2014) - re-verified, 'OPTIONS. ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL.' at --std 2002 is rejected with COBOLNET0900 'requires COBOL-2014 (targeting COBOL-2002)'. SS15.73.3 rule 3 requires the returned value to be EXACTLY 3.141592653589793238462643383279503; PI is absent from the IntrinsicBinder staged-loud list (which holds only ANNUITY / PRESENT-VALUE / VARIANCE / STANDARD-DEVIATION) and rides the ordinary RenderFloat/Math.PI/binary64 path in EVERY arithmetic mode, so a STANDARD-DECIMAL program silently gets native binary64 digits. FAILING INPUT (re-run independently on the built CLI): 'IDENTIFICATION DIVISION. PROGRAM-ID. PISDREV2. OPTIONS. ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL. DATA DIVISION. WORKING-STORAGE SECTION. 01 R17 PIC 9V9(17). PROCEDURE DIVISION. COMPUTE R17 = FUNCTION PI. DISPLAY R17.' at --std 2014 and --std 2023 prints 3.14159265358979328; rule 3 truncated to the receiver (COMPUTE without ROUNDED truncates, SS14.7) requires 3.14159265358979323 - note the earlier draft's expected '...324' was the ROUNDED value and is wrong. At PIC 9V9(30) it prints 0.000000000009223372036854775807 (the FromDouble Int64 saturation) against a required 3.141592653589793238462643383279. THE FALSE PREMISE, written in two places - the CobolIntrinsics.Float.cs class header and the IntrinsicBinder staging comment - is 'their returned-value rules are prose approximations, NOT equivalent arithmetic expressions, so the value is implementor-defined in EVERY mode (SS15.4.1 last paragraph)'. It fails on TWO independent grounds, both validated: (a) SS15.73.3 rule 1 is phrased exactly as SS15.4.1's equivalent-arithmetic-expression sentence ('an implementor-defined approximation of the arithmetic expression (3 + 0.14159...)'), so PI DOES have an EAE, and SS15.4.1 then states 'When standard-decimal arithmetic or standard-binary arithmetic is in effect and an equivalent arithmetic expression is specified: 1) the returned value shall equal the value of the equivalent arithmetic expression'; and (b) even on the no-EAE reading, SS15.4.1's last paragraph reads 'its returned value is implementor-defined UNLESS OTHERWISE SPECIFIED IN THE FUNCTION DEFINITION' - and rules 2 and 3 are precisely that specification. Test-needed (no test references PI under any standard arithmetic mode). SIBLING CONFIRMED, not merely suspected: 'COMPUTE R17 = FUNCTION E.' under STANDARD-DECIMAL prints 2.71828182845904512 where SS15.27.3 rule 3 (validated) requires the exact value truncating to 2.71828182845904523. ALSO: ArithmeticMode.Standard (the 2002-2014 'ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD' clause, which DataBinder routes to the same CobolDec engine) diverges identically - verified, --std 2002 with ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD prints the same 3.14159265358979328 - so the fix must cover ArithmeticMode.Standard as well as StandardDecimal.

subject: PRESENT-VALUE function
notes: PB1; the family fixture now covers PRESENT-VALUE's own 15.74.3 r1 rejection rather than relying on a sibling function's.

subject: PRESENT-VALUE function
notes: test-needed. §15.74.3 r2 (cite.py --check: OK) — the value of argument-1 shall be greater than −1. This is a permissible-VALUE constraint, so §15.3 applies: 'If the evaluation of an argument results in an incorrect value for that argument … the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist'; Annex A.1 item 90 makes only the RETURNED VALUE implementor-defined when checking is off — the condition must still be SET, and must be raised when checking is on. CobolIntrinsics.PresentValue(double rate, params double[] amounts) performs no domain check on rate, unlike its file-mates Log/Log10 which call Exceptions.ExceptionState.ArgumentError, and the binder adds none. Reproduced with the built CLI: (a) COMPILE-TIME-detectable literal violation, edition-independent — `COMPUTE RESULT-X = FUNCTION PRESENT-VALUE(-1.5, 100, 200)` is accepted silently at --std 85 AND --std 2023 and prints 600.000000, so the divergence does not depend on the (2002+) EC machinery and holds at every edition; (b) runtime rate with checking explicitly enabled — `>>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON` then `FUNCTION PRESENT-VALUE(R2 AMT AMT)` with R2 = −2.00 prints 0 and CONTINUES, while the very next `FUNCTION LOG(0)` in the SAME program aborts with 'EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION (fatal)' — same directive, same run unit, so the mechanism exists and PRESENT-VALUE alone does not use it; (c) rate = −1.00 exactly makes 1+rate = 0, and the binary64 division through FromDouble SATURATES, printing 223372036.8547 with no exception and no diagnostic.

subject: PRESENT-VALUE function
notes: Holds under NATIVE arithmetic; the standard-arithmetic leg does not. The body `for (int i = 0; i < amounts.Length; i++) pv += amounts[i] / Math.Pow(1 + rate, i + 1)` is exactly Σ argument-2ᵢ / (1 + argument-1)^i for i = 1..n — §15.74.4 r1c, with r1a and r1b as its n = 1 and n = 2 cases — and §15.4.1 licenses 'an implementor-defined approximation' under native arithmetic. Verified with the built CLI: PRESENT-VALUE(0.100 1000 2000 3000) and the hand-written FUNCTION SUM EAE both give 4815.927873, which is also the exact hand-computed value. Annex A.1 item 92 ('Function returned values (characteristics, representation, and returned value for native arithmetic) … The value returned does not have to be documented') means the documentation test does NOT downgrade the native leg, and docs/CONFORMANCE.md already carries a §15.4.1 / §14.9.11.4 GR1 row. THE PARTIAL: §15.4.1 r1 requires the returned value to EQUAL the equivalent arithmetic expression when standard-decimal OR STANDARD-BINARY arithmetic is in effect, and instead of doing so IntrinsicBinder rejects the program with DiagnosticCatalog.ArithmeticStandardIntrinsic (COBOLNET0899, EditionSeverity.Error) — legal COBOL refused; confirmed by running an OPTIONS/ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL program. ⚠ NOTE FOR THE FIX SESSION: that staging condition is `ctx.Data.Options.Arithmetic is ArithmeticMode.Standard or ArithmeticMode.StandardDecimal` and OMITS ArithmeticMode.StandardBinary, which §15.4.1 covers equally. I checked whether that opens a SILENT-wrong-answer hole and it does not — today ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY is itself loud-rejected earlier by COBOLNET0806 ('obsolete feature … not supported') at --std 85/2002/2014/2023, so standard-binary can never be in effect — but if 0806 is ever lifted (obsolete is not removed; §11.9.5 still defines the phrase in 2023), the 0899 list must gain StandardBinary or PRESENT-VALUE will silently return the native double. The rule itself applies at all four editions; the failing leg needs the OPTIONS ARITHMETIC clause and so is reachable only from 2002. ⚠ TEST-REF CORRECTED: nist:IF403M was STRUCK on two independent grounds — it is registered 'pending / none / cataloged (not asserted)' in tests/nist/corpus.tsv line 406 so nothing runs it, and its sole PRESENT-VALUE statement compares the function to ITSELF (`IF FUNCTION PRESENT-VALUE (0, 23, 12, 9) = FUNCTION PRESENT-VALUE (0, 23, 12, 9)`), which tests determinism, never the equivalent arithmetic expression. nist:IF130A genuinely covers the native leg — F-PRES-VAL-01 range-checks PRESENT-VALUE(0, 23, 12, 9) against 43.9991..44.0009 and twenty-one further paragraphs range-check real values. No test covers the standard-decimal leg (tests/conformance/negative/arith-standard-intrinsic-staged.cob exercises VARIANCE, not PRESENT-VALUE, so it is deliberately not cited).

subject: RANDOM function
notes: PB1; 15.75.3 r1 (class numeric) covered. The VALUE half of RANDOM's rules (r2, zero-or-positive-integer) is a separate, still-open EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION question.

subject: RANDOM function
notes: Neither half of 'it shall be zero or a positive integer' is enforced at bind or at run time, and the §15.3 raise ('If the evaluation of an argument results in an incorrect value for that argument ... the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist') never fires for a RANDOM seed. (a) NEGATIVE: CobolIntrinsics.Float.Random(long seed) does `new Random((int)(seed & 0x7FFFFFFF))`, so a negative seed is silently ALIASED onto a large positive one — REPRODUCED: FUNCTION RANDOM(-5) and FUNCTION RANDOM(2147483643) both return 636542013 (the alias is the two's-complement mask 0x7FFFFFFB, NOT abs(), so it does not even agree with .NET's own Random(int) sign handling). (b) NON-INTEGER: IntrinsicRenderer.IntArg truncates to scale 0, so FUNCTION RANDOM(1.75) silently becomes seed 1 — REPRODUCED: RANDOM(1.75) and RANDOM(1) both return 248668584. Concrete failing input: `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION RANDOM(-5).` then `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION RANDOM(1.75).` — compiles exit 0, zero diagnostics. The EC machinery EXISTS and is already used by sibling intrinsics (Exceptions.ExceptionState.ArgumentError — CobolDate's DATE-OF-INTEGER/DAY-OF-INTEGER range checks, CobolIntrinsics.FromDouble on NaN); RANDOM simply never reaches it, so `>>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON` cannot catch it either. Fix shape: the seed range/integrality check belongs in the runtime body through ExceptionState.ArgumentError (a runtime-valued seed cannot be screened at bind), plus a bind-time diagnostic for the statically-known literal case. test-needed.

subject: RANDOM function
notes: Random(long seed) REPLACES the one static _random with a freshly seeded generator and returns its first value, so a subsequent seeded reference restarts the sequence. Re-verified independently at HEAD: RANDOM(42) -> 668106466, argument-less -> 140907298, argument-less -> 125518289, RANDOM(42) again -> 668106466, argument-less -> 140907298 — the restart reproduces the whole PREFIX, not merely the first value. Editions from the catalog window IntroducedIn 85 (the 1989 Intrinsic Function Module amendment, which this compiler treats as part of --std 85); FUNCTION RANDOM was confirmed to compile and run at 85, 2002, 2014 and 2023. Test-ref nist:IF131A was STRUCK by review: its five RANDOM paragraphs only range-check 0 <= r < 1 and never compare two same-seed references, so it does not exercise this rule. The surviving conformance-test asserts R1 = R3 across an intervening argument-less draw, which is exactly rule 3's observable.

subject: RANDOM function
notes: BARE QUESTION: shall the §15.75.3 rule-4 implementor-defined seed be a FIXED value, so an un-seeded FUNCTION RANDOM sequence is reproducible across runs, or stay the current per-process entropy seed? Why this is not CONFORMS: the field initializer is `private static Random _random = new()`, and on .NET 6+ the PARAMETERLESS Random constructor seeds xoshiro256** directly from OS entropy — there is no seed VALUE at all, which is precisely what Annex A.1 item 144 ('RANDOM function (seed value when no argument on first reference). This item is required.') names as the required determination. Documentation is genuinely waived by item 144 ('The seed value used by the implementor does not have to be documented'), so this is NOT a CONFORMANCE.md gap — it is an unmade choice with an observed user-visible consequence: four consecutive runs of the same program gave first values 925010183 / 038930312 / 356550812 / 117861222. The in-code rationale also misdescribes the mechanism as 'the .NET time-derived default', evidence the behaviour was inherited from the framework rather than chosen, and no compiler survey is recorded (feedback_survey_compilers_on_latitude requires one before settling implementor latitude). Test-ref nist:IF131A was STRUCK: it makes the first reference argument-less but can only range-check the result, so nothing about the seed determination is testable there.

subject: RANDOM function
notes: 15.75.3 r5 - a reference WITHOUT argument-1 returns the next number in the current sequence. Asserted STRUCTURALLY (the two unseeded references differ; a re-seed reproduces the first), never as this implementation's own numbers, because the numbers themselves are implementor-defined and pinning them would be pinning the implementation rather than the rule.

subject: RANDOM function
notes: The runtime body conforms (Random.NextDouble() is in [0,1)) and the FLOAT-receiver path (num.Receiver.Real) hands the double through unquantized. The FIXED-POINT receiver path does NOT: RenderFloat wraps the call in FromDouble(call, ws) with ws = Math.Max(num.Receiver.Scale, 9), and FromDouble ends in `(long)Math.Round(scaled, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero)`, so any returned value >= 0.9999999995 quantizes to exactly 1.000000000 — not 'less than one'. THE QUANTIZATION DEFECT IS DEMONSTRATED, not conjectured: on the same shared code path `01 R PIC 9V9(9). COMPUTE R = FUNCTION SQRT(0.999999999).` prints 1.000000000 while SQRT(0.999999998) prints 0.999999999. For RANDOM the top bucket is one draw in ~2.1e9 (the seeded back-compat generator's NextDouble is InternalSample() * (1.0/int.MaxValue) and only InternalSample() == 2147483646 clears the threshold; the argument-less xoshiro path has the same ~5e-10 probability), so no short deterministic COBOL input exhibits it — the bound is broken by the emitter's generic rounding, not by the generator. Fix shape: clamp (or round toward zero) at the quantization point for range-bounded functions instead of leaving the < 1 bound to FromDouble's AwayFromZero. test-ref conformance-test:...Random_SeededSequence_PinnedToSpec was STRUCK by review — its receivers are PIC V9(9), which has NO integer position, so a 1.000000000 result would silently store as .000000000, and the test asserts nothing about the range. nist:IF131A is kept as corroboration only (a NIST golden is a regression net, never spec-derived, so it cannot close the row); its WS-NUM is PIC S9(5)V9(6), which can represent 1.0, so its `WS-NUM < MAX-RANGE` legs would in principle catch the violation. test-needed: a spec-derived case pinning the < 1 bound on a receiver able to hold 1.0.

subject: RANDOM function
notes: Random(long seed) constructs `new Random(int)`, which on .NET 6+ is pinned to the back-compatible (Knuth subtractive) seeded implementation — deterministic for a given seed. Re-verified across FOUR separate processes at four editions: FUNCTION RANDOM(5) returned 338369841 every time while the argument-less draws in the same programs varied, so the determinism belongs to the seeded path and is not process reuse. Independently corroborated WITHOUT using the compiler as its own oracle: a from-scratch reimplementation of the .NET seeded subtractive generator reproduces the compiler's output exactly for seeds 0 (726243270), 1 (248668584), 5 (338369841), 42 (668106466, 140907298, 125518289) and 2147483643 (636542013) — the sequence is algorithmically determined by the seed, not incidentally stable. Residual TEST gap (not a conformance gap): the test asserts only same-seed equality within one process; no golden pins an actual RANDOM value, so a change of the underlying seeded generator would land silently.

subject: RANDOM function
notes: The BEHAVIOUR meets the numeric floor and this was MEASURED, not assumed: `new Random((int)(seed & 0x7FFFFFFF))` is the identity on 0..2147483647, and an independent reimplementation of the seeded generator (validated against the compiler's own output for five seeds) yields 32768 DISTINCT six-value sequences for the 32768 seeds 0..32767 — zero collisions. Seeds at or above 2^31 alias downward — verified at HEAD that FUNCTION RANDOM(2147483648) == FUNCTION RANDOM(0) == 726243270 and FUNCTION RANDOM(2147483649) == FUNCTION RANDOM(1) == 248668584 — which is legitimate latitude precisely BECAUSE rule 3 lets the implementor specify the subset. But rule 3's obligation is to SPECIFY that subset, and Annex A.1 item 145 makes it a required item that 'shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation'. Documented in CONFORMANCE.md section 7: NO — section 7 carries only items 2, 59, 158, 205, 206, 207, 208, 211, 215 plus one unnumbered §15.4.1 row, and the word RANDOM appears nowhere in that file. Conforming needs the entry as well as the behaviour, so PARTIAL until section 7 states the subset. NOTE for whoever writes it: only 0..32767 was actually measured for distinctness — do NOT write '0..2147483647' into CONFORMANCE.md without measuring it, because asserting an unverified subset is the wrongly-documented determination that section 7's own header calls worse than an absent one. test-needed (nothing asserts that two distinct seeds in 0..32767 yield distinct sequences, and nothing checks the CONFORMANCE.md entry).

subject: REM function
notes: DOWNGRADED from CONFORMS on adversarial review. HOLDS on the fixed-point path, verified by execution on both ISO 15.3 legs: RemScaled tests b == 0 on the SCALE-ALIGNED divisor (NumericRenderer.Align only ever widens to max(a.Scale,b.Scale), so no truncation can manufacture or hide a zero) and calls ExceptionState.ArgumentError -- with >>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON the run unit dies with 'EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION (fatal): REM with a zero divisor (15.77.3 rule 2)'; with checking off the implementor-defined default 0 is returned, for a literal 0, a zero-valued item and a zero-valued expression (Z - Z) alike. DOES NOT HOLD for two operand shapes ISO 15.3 item 10 permits, because REM does not COMPILE there at all, so a zero divisor can never reach the check: (a) a FLOAT argument-2 (USAGE COMP-2/COMP-1, category numeric per ISO 8.5.2.12 item 2) -- backend 'CS1503: cannot convert from double to System.Int128' at --std 85/2002/2014/2023; (b) under OPTIONS ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL an arithmetic-expression argument -- 'CS1503: cannot convert from CobolNet.Runtime.CobolDec to System.Int128' (2014+ only, where this compiler admits the clause). Do not chase it. test-needed: nothing anywhere exercises a zero REM divisor -- the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION tests (ExceptionConditionConformanceTests; IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests.OutOfDomain_EcDefaultZero_PinnedToSpec) use LOG/NUMVAL/SQRT/FACTORIAL, and the NIST REM cases pass a zero ARGUMENT-1 (IF133A F-REM-TEST-01: FUNCTION REM(0, 20)), never a zero argument-2. subject: REVERSE function
notes: DOWNGRADED FROM CONFORMS. The reversal ITSELF is exactly right - CobolIntrinsics.Reverse is a position-j <- position-(n-j+1) code-unit reversal with no length change, fed the operand's FULL fixed-width image, and re-verified live at every shape tried: X(6) VALUE "AB" -> [    BA  ] into X(8) (n = the declared width, not the trimmed value); ref-mod W-S(2:3) -> [  B     ]; A(5) -> [EDCBA   ]; N(5) -> [EDCBA   ]; numeric-edited ZZ9 VALUE 42 -> [24      ] (the EDITED image is reversed, correct); alphanumeric-edited XXBXX "AB CD" -> [DC BA   ]; an image-capable group -> [EDCBA   ]. Surrogates need no special handling - 8.5.1.4 item 2 and its closing paragraph ('Each two-octet code element of UTF-16 is treated in COBOL as though it were itself a character', cite-checked) make code-unit reversal the spec-mandated behaviour. BUT THREE LEGAL argument-1 SHAPES PRODUCE NO RETURNED VALUE AT ALL - each compiles clean at 85 and 2023 and then throws CobolNet.Runtime.NotImplementedCobolFeatureException at RUN time, where 15.78.4 r1 requires a character string of length n: (1) an alphanumeric GROUP item containing a float/COMP-5/INDEX leaf - `01 G2. 05 G2-A PIC X(3) VALUE "ABC". 05 G2-N PIC S9(4) COMP-5 VALUE 5.` then `MOVE FUNCTION REVERSE(G2) TO W-X.` -> 'whole-group image of G2 with a float/COMP-5/INDEX leaf - the Tier-C byte island'; the argument is legal because 8.5.2.1 makes an alphanumeric group item class AND category alphanumeric, which 15.78.3 r1 admits. (2) a FIGURATIVE CONSTANT - `MOVE FUNCTION REVERSE(SPACE) TO W-X.` -> 'intrinsic string argument BoundFigurative' (IntrinsicRenderer.StrArgVisitor.Visit(BoundFigurative) is a Loud arm); legal because 8.4.3.2.3 SR8 admits a literal, 8.3.3.6.4 GR1 makes SPACE an alphanumeric character value and GR3b fixes its length at one character position - exactly satisfying 15.78.3 r1. (3) `MOVE FUNCTION REVERSE(ALL "AB") TO W-X.` -> 'intrinsic string argument BoundAllLiteral' (the sibling Loud arm); 8.3.3.6.4 GR3c gives it the length of literal-1. The failures are LOUD, not wrong values, and the Tier-C group island is a general deferral (COBOLNET_DESIGN 4.2) rather than a REVERSE-specific bug - but it is NOT recorded in docs/CONFORMANCE.md (grep found no Tier-C / whole-group-image entry), so it is an open GAP, not documented non-support. Fixing StrArgVisitor's two Loud arms is the cheap half and closes the same hole for UPPER-CASE/LOWER-CASE/TRIM/CONCAT. TEST-REF STRUCK: `conformance:negative/reverse_national_result_to_an` was cited for this rule but does not cover it - it is a `*> reject-at: 2002 2014 2023` COMPILE-REJECT case for the 15.78.1 result-type table and the 14.9.25.3 Table 16 National->AN MOVE guard (CA25); the program never executes, so it cannot exercise a position-reversal rule. The surviving refs do exercise it (StringFamily_PinnedToSpec pins REVERSE("abc 12") -> [21 cba  ] against the SPEC; IF134A checks `IF FUNCTION REVERSE("CAPS") = "SPAC"`; ChannelMatrix reverses "ABCDE", though only differentially against the frozen legacy oracle). Test-needed: goldens for the group, figurative and ALL-literal shapes. Editions: the three failing shapes reproduce identically at every --std, and only the 2023 rule text was available, so the per-edition wording was not re-derived.

subject: SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME function
notes: §15.79.3 r1 has TWO halves and only one is implemented. LITERAL-ness is enforced — BindIntrinsicCore raises COBOLNET1517 when argument-1 is not a BoundStringLiteral (verified: `FUNCTION SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME(WS-FMT, "12:34:56")` with `01 WS-FMT PIC X(8)` → COBOLNET1517). The CLASS restriction ('national or alphanumeric') is NOT: ExpressionBinder.BooleanLiteralOperand yields a BoundStringLiteral carrying Category=Boolean, which passes the 1517 test, so `MOVE FUNCTION SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME(B"0011", "12:34:56") TO WS-F.` compiles clean at --std 2014 and prints +00000.00 with no diagnostic — a boolean literal is neither of the two classes Table 21 ('Anum1 or Nat1') and r1 admit. The prior adjudication argued this away as 'always resolves to EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION', but §15.3's EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION disposition is for an argument whose evaluation produces an INCORRECT VALUE; r1 is a static class rule, and this compiler's own precedent for a §15 argument class rule is a BIND-time diagnostic (CheckRepertoireArgs → COBOLNET1546 for DISPLAY-OF/NATIONAL-OF §15.26.3/§15.66.3). Correctly ACCEPTED and verified: alphanumeric ("hh:mm:ss"), the §8.3.3.2 Format-2 hexadecimal form (X"68686D6D7373" → +45296.00), national (N"hh:mm:ss"), and an §8.8.3 concatenation expression ("hh:" & "mm:ss" → +45296.00). Secondary over-restriction on the same check: `ALL "hh:mm:ss"` (an §8.3.3.6.4 Format-6 figurative constant representing an alphanumeric literal) binds to BoundAllLiteral, not BoundStringLiteral, and is REJECTED with COBOLNET1517 — verified. Fix shape: give the FORMATTED-*/INTEGER-OF-FORMATTED-DATE/SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME/TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME arm a category test (Alphanumeric or National) beside the literal test, in the same place the missing argument-2 class check for r3 must go. test-needed: the shared COBOLNET1517 arm is covered only for FORMATTED-DATE (conformance-test:IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests.FormattedDate_NonLiteralFormat_1517); there is no SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME leg and no negative test for a wrong-class literal. Editions from IntrinsicCatalog IntroducedIn=2014 (gate verified: --std 2002 → COBOLNET1502).

subject: SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME function
notes: Holds under the IMPLIED >>LEAP-SECOND OFF default, fails on the ON path. Analyze walks argument-2 segment by segment against the tokenized format, checking every data-bearing separator (colon, decimal separator, T, W, Z, offset sign), digit-only content, per-subfield ranges (hh 00-23, mm 00-59, offset-hours 00-23 / offset-minutes 00-59 per §15.3.3.6.2, zero-sign forcing zero magnitude per §15.3.3.6.1), short data and trailing data; a nonzero result routes to ExceptionState.ArgumentError, which sets EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION fatal when checking is enabled and otherwise returns 0 — the §15.3 implementor-defined result, which A.1 item 90 expressly says need NOT be documented, so no CONFORMANCE.md entry is owed. Verified: "256100"/'hhmmss' → +00000.00 and, under `>>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON`, 'abnormal run-unit termination: EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION (fatal)'; "12-34-56"/'hh:mm:ss' → 0; "1234"/'hhmmss' → 0; "123456Z"/'hhmmssZ' → +45296.00; "12:34:56+05:00"/'hh:mm:ss+hh:mm' → +45296.00; "12345650"/'hhmmss.ss' (phantom basic separator) → +45296.50. THE GAP: the seconds range is hardcoded `Fld.Second => (0, 59)` in Analyze — §15.3.3.3 requires 00..<61 when a LEAP-SECOND directive with the ON phrase is in effect, and >>LEAP-SECOND sits in ConditionalCompilationProcessor.KnownIgnoredDirectives, so it is consumed and silently ignored. Verified: a source beginning `>>LEAP-SECOND ON` with `FUNCTION SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME("hhmmss", "235960")` compiles without a word of complaint and returns +00000.00, rejecting a value §15.3.3.3 makes legal. CONFORMANCE.md §3 records >>LEAP-SECOND as documented non-support, but §7.3.17 is core language, not an Annex A.4 optional module, so §4.2.7 does not cover it and A.1 items 111/112 (both required + shall-be-documented) presuppose the directive works — resolving that is an owner call. test-needed: no test exercises an invalid argument-2 for this function, and none exercises >>LEAP-SECOND at all.

subject: SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME function
notes: A combined WEEK-date-and-time format whose argument-2 is VALID per §15.3.1.7 aborts the run unit with an unhandled .NET exception instead of returning a value. `MOVE FUNCTION SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME("YYYYWwwDThhmmss", "9999W527T235959") TO WS-F.` at --std 2014 → 'Unhandled exception. System.ArgumentOutOfRangeException … at System.Globalization.ISOWeek.ToDateTime … at CobolNet.Runtime.CobolDate.Analyze'. Every subfield satisfies §15.3.1.7: year 9999 is >1600 and <=9999; Jan 4 9999 is a Monday so 9999 is a 52-week ISO year and week 52 is inside the permitted 01..52; day-of-week 7 is inside 1..7. The expected result is +86399.00 — D.31.5.9 makes the date VALIDATED BUT DISCARDED for this function, so the integer date form is never needed here at all; Analyze computes it unconditionally at its `else if (hasWeek) integerDate = ISOWeek.ToDateTime(...)` leg, and ISO-9999-W52-7 falls on 10000-01-02, outside DateTime.MaxValue. Even on the most conservative reading (that the denoted date is out of range and r5 is therefore violated), §15.3 fixes the disposition as EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION or the implementor-defined result — never a raw CLR stack trace, which is neither a COBOL value nor a COBOL exception condition. Sibling sweep (same Analyze line, both verified crashing identically): `FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-FORMATTED-DATE("YYYYWwwD", "9999W527")` and `FUNCTION TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME("YYYYWwwD", "9999W527")` — the latter is the worse one, since §15.92 defines TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME as the VALIDATOR that returns an error position and can therefore never legitimately fault. Fix shape: bound-check the week-date reconstruction (and hand SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME a path that does not build integerDate at all). The rest of r5 is correct and was verified: the mandatory 'T' is required in the data (§15.3.3.7); the D.31.5.9 worked example `("YYYYMMDDThhmmss.ss+hhmm", "19950215T05142781+0500")` → +18867.81 with the offset correctly excluded; Feb-31 in the same format → the §15.3 default 0; the calendar boundary "99991231T235959" → +86399.00. test-needed.

subject: SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME function
notes: ((H*3600)+(M*60)+S) is computed exactly for fraction widths up to NINE digits — Analyze forms `((long)hh*3600 + mi*60 + ss) * 10^f + frac` at scale f, S correctly carrying the fractional-second digits of the seconds subfield (§15.3.3.2), and the offset/UTC subfields correctly NOT entering the sum; both D.31.5.9 worked examples reproduce exactly ("hhmmss.ss+hhmm"/"05142781+0500" and "YYYYMMDDThhmmss.ss+hhmm"/"19950215T05142781+0500" → +18867.81). It breaks at TEN or more fractional-second digits: Analyze accumulates every subfield through a local `int val = 0;` and then does `case Fld.Fraction: frac = val;` even though `frac` is already a long, so the fraction wraps at 2^31 in unchecked arithmetic. Verified at --std 2014: `("hhmmss.ssssssssss", "1234563000000000")` into `01 WS-A PIC +9(5).9(10).` returns +45295.8705032704 instead of +45296.3000000000 (3000000000 − 2^32 = −1294967296); twelve digits `("hhmmss.ssssssssssss", "123456812479168304")` into PIC +9(5).9(12) returns +45296.000730349360 instead of +45296.812479168304; nineteen digits returns +00000.01. §15.3.3.2 makes the maximum fraction width implementor-defined with a floor of nine; COBOL.NET neither enforces nor documents a maximum, and A.1 item 202 ('Time formats and corresponding function values (maximum precision not less than nine fractional digits)', required, 'This item shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation') is documented in CONFORMANCE.md §7: NO — §7 currently lists only items 2, 59, 158 and 205–215. So the conforming fix is BOTH halves: widen the accumulator (or reject past the defined maximum with EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION) AND add the item-202 row to CONFORMANCE.md §7. The two existing tests exercise the expression only at 0 and 2 fraction digits, so nothing covers the overflow.

ABS function
notes: PRINTED PAGE RE-RENDERED INDEPENDENTLY (scripts/render-spec-page.py 846; printed folio 816): the format is FUNCTION ABS ( argument-1 ) with FUNCTION and ABS underlined and NO bracketed or optional element, so the transcription is faithful and the lossy-diagram failure mode does not apply. NOT ALL LEGAL POSITIONS: 8.4.2.3.2 makes a subscript an arithmetic-expression-1, 8.8.1.1 admits an identifier referencing a numeric data item, 8.5.2.12 items 6/7 make a numeric/integer function exactly that, and 8.4.3.2.3 SR12 expressly names the integer form of ABS as the ONE integer function allowed where an unsigned integer is required -- yet DISPLAY E(FUNCTION ABS(I)) compiles and then throws NotImplementedCobolFeatureException "reference 'E(FUNCTION ABS(I))'" at run time, failing 4.2.2 paragraph 1. subject: ANNUITY function
notes: OVERTURNED FROM CONFORMS. The general format writes EXACTLY TWO arguments, and the implementation enforces that for every WRITTEN form — but it silently accepts a ONE-argument written form when an ALL subscript happens to expand to two. REPRODUCED (PROGRAM-ID ADVFMT07, zero diagnostics, exit 0): `01 T. 05 RT PIC S9(4)V9(4) OCCURS 2 TIMES.` / `MOVE 0.05 TO RT(1). MOVE 10 TO RT(2).` / `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION ANNUITY ( RT(ALL) ). DISPLAY "ALLSUB2=" R.` -> prints `00000129504E` (0.1295045), i.e. it was evaluated as ANNUITY(0.05, 10). §15.3 (validated: `cite.py --check 15.3 "permits an argument to be repeated a variable number of times"` -> OK §15.3 14)) licenses the ALL expansion only 'When the definition of a function permits an argument to be repeated a variable number of times' — ANNUITY's definition is fixed at two — and §8.4.2.3.4 GR1a makes the ALL subscript 'all of the possible values of a subscript for the associated table as specified in the rules for the functions for which the subscript ALL is allowed', of which ANNUITY has none. §8.4.2.3.3 SR6 (validated: OK §8.4.2.3.3 6)) permits ALL syntactically in ANY intrinsic argument, so the prohibition is inferential rather than an explicit 'shall not' — hence PARTIAL, not DIVERGES, and the row must stay open. ⚠ THE PRIOR RECORD'S OWN EVIDENCE WAS THE HAPPY PATH: it asserted 'RT(ALL) expands and is rejected the same way (4 given) — correct'. That rejection was an accident of that fixture's table having FOUR elements; at cardinality 2 the same construct is accepted with no diagnostic. ALSO CORRECTED: the prior record cited `python scripts/spec/render-spec-page.py 848` as its transcription proof; no such path exists (the script is `scripts/render-spec-page.py`), so that evidence was not reproducible as written. I rendered printed folio 818 = PDF page 848 myself and read it as an image: the format line is exactly `FUNCTION ANNUITY ( argument-1 argument-2 )` with FUNCTION and ANNUITY underlined, no brackets/braces/ellipsis, exactly two arguments — the markdown at §15.9.2 IS faithful, and Table 21 ('ANNUITY | Num1, Int2 | Num') corroborates the arity independently. WHAT I RE-VERIFIED AND HOLDS, each run on the built CLI: printed space separation with two literals AND with two data items (`FUNCTION ANNUITY ( RATE-X PER-X )`) -> 0.1295045; space-separated arithmetic-expression arguments `( A + B N + N )` -> 0.1295045; a nested `FUNCTION ABS` argument; the §8.7.1/§8.3.3.3.2 adjacency discrimination — `( RATE-X -4 )` binds as TWO arguments and runs while `( RATE-X - 4 )` binds as ONE and gives COBOLNET1504; 0, 1, 3 arguments and the bare `FUNCTION ANNUITY.` (no parens) each give `error COBOLNET1504: FUNCTION ANNUITY takes 2 argument(s); N given (ISO 15.3)`; the §8.4.3.2 SR2 keyword-omitted form `ANNUITY ( 0.05 10 )` under `REPOSITORY. FUNCTION ANNUITY INTRINSIC.`; and clean compiles at --std 85 / 2002 / 2014 / 2023. FIX: reject an ALL subscript in an argument of a fixed-arity intrinsic (§4.2.2 para 3 — statically decidable), the same disposition PB1 gave the argument-class screen. EDITIONS: all four — §15.9 carries no edition marker and no Annex E item names ANNUITY; IntrinsicCatalog's own IntroducedIn was not used as evidence. test-needed: no spec-derived test pins the ANNUITY arity/format.

  14.9.2.3 "shall reference numeric data items" -> OK §14.9.2.3 2)
  14.9.13.2 "selection-object" -> OK §14.9.13.2 (General format)

THE FORMAT ITSELF IS CONFIRMED AND IS CORRECTLY IMPLEMENTED. specs/ISO_COBOL.md carries the underlined transcription "<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>ASIN</u> ( argument-1 )" (the backtick form quoted in the input file is the stale copy in docs/rearchitecture/spec-rule-catalog.json). Two required words, exactly one argument, no bracketed or optional element. Verified against the compiler with src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/cobol.exe <file> --run:
 - ARITY: IntrinsicCatalog's ASIN row is Fixed 1..1 and IntrinsicBinder.BindIntrinsicCore's "args.Count < sig.MinArgs || args.Count > sig.MaxArgs" arm fires. "COMPUTE X = FUNCTION ASIN" -> COBOLNET1504 "FUNCTION ASIN takes 1 argument(s); 0 given"; "FUNCTION ASIN()" -> same; "FUNCTION ASIN(0.5 0.5)" -> "...2 given".
 - POSITIONS THAT WORK: COMPUTE, MOVE sending operand, DISPLAY operand, an IF relation on both sides, and PERFORM VARYING ... FROM — all yield 0.523598776 for ASIN(0.5).
 - ARGUMENT-1 SHAPES THAT WORK (§8.4.3.2.3 r8 admits identifier / literal / arithmetic expression): literal, signed literal, data-name, fixed subscript E(1), variable subscript E(I), arithmetic expression E(1) - E(2) (= ASIN(0.3) = 0.304692654), parenthesized (A), nested FUNCTION SIN(0.5) (= 0.500000000), and a COMP-2 item (the PB2 …Real route).
 - ASIN IS CORRECTLY NOT OVER-RESERVED (§8.11 lists it as an intrinsic-function-name, not a reserved word): "01 ASIN PIC 9 VALUE 3" coexists with FUNCTION ASIN(0.5) in the same program — ran it, printed X=0.523598776 and ASIN-ITEM=3.
 - IDENTICAL UNDER ALL FOUR EDITIONS: --std 85, 2002, 2014 and 2023 each ran the COMPUTE/MOVE/IF program and produced the same values.

WHY THIS IS NOT CONFORMS — two positions where source written to this general format is legal COBOL and the compiler does not accept it. These are DEMONSTRATED failures, not merely unverified edges:

(1) THE FOUR ARITHMETIC STATEMENTS REJECT IT AT THE PARSER. A function-identifier is an identifier (§8.4.3.1.2 Format 1); §8.4.3.2.4 r1 makes an intrinsic's temporary an elementary data item whose description is the function's (§15.10.1: "The type of this function is numeric"); §14.9.2.3 r2 asks only that identifier-1 "reference numeric data items"; and §8.4.3.2.3 bars a function-identifier only as a RECEIVING operand (r1) and only where an INTEGER operand is required (r11) — neither applies to ADD's sending operand. So this is legal COBOL, and I ran it:
    ADD FUNCTION ASIN(0.5) TO X
  -> error COBOL0001: no viable alternative at input 'ADDFUNCTION'
     error COBOL0001: cannot parse construct near 'FUNCTION'
  Same raw-parse rejection, each re-run by me: "SUBTRACT FUNCTION ASIN(0.5) FROM X" ('SUBTRACTFUNCTION') and "DIVIDE FUNCTION ASIN(0.5) INTO X" ('no viable alternative at input FUNCTION'); unchanged under --std 85. ROOT CAUSE READ IN THE GRAMMAR (CobolParserCore.g4): addOperand, subtractOperand, multiplyOperand and divideOperand are each exactly "dataReference | literal" with NO functionCall alternative, while CobolExpressions.g4's primaryExpression does list functionCall. CROSS-CUTTING, NOT ASIN-SPECIFIC: I reproduced the identical rejection with "ADD FUNCTION LENGTH(S) TO X", so one grammar fix closes it for every catalogued function.

(2) EVALUATE TRUE WITH A RELATION CONDITION LED BY THE FUNCTION COMPILES AND THEN CRASHES AT RUN TIME. §14.9.13.2 lists condition-2 among the selection-objects. I ran:
    EVALUATE TRUE
      WHEN FUNCTION ASIN(0.5) > 0.5
        DISPLAY "BIG"
      WHEN OTHER DISPLAY "SMALL"
    END-EVALUATE
  -> Unhandled exception. CobolNet.Runtime.NotImplementedCobolFeatureException: "EVALUATE TRUE/FALSE paired with a value WHEN object". CONTROLS I RAN THAT ISOLATE IT TO THE LEADING FUNCTION-IDENTIFIER: "WHEN X > 0.5" prints BIG; "WHEN (FUNCTION ASIN(0.5) > 0.5)" prints BIG; "WHEN 0.4 < FUNCTION ASIN(0.5)" prints GT4. Cause read in the source: evaluateWhenItem (CobolControlFlow.g4) orders "valueOperand" BEFORE "condition", ANTLR takes the first match, and EvaluateBinder.BindWhenItem then finds item.condition() null against a TRUE subject. Accepting-then-crashing is worse than a diagnostic.

WHY PARTIAL RATHER THAN DIVERGES: the ASIN format is implemented exactly as §15.10.2 draws it wherever the parser reaches it; the defect is that the format is not WIRED to every position the language permits a function-identifier. A future reader should treat this as a live gap, not a stylistic caveat — legal source is being rejected.

EDITIONS, ESTABLISHED WITHOUT READING IntrinsicCatalog's IntroducedIn FIELD: a full-text search of specs/ISO_COBOL.md returns ASIN in exactly seven places — the table of contents, the index, §8.11 Intrinsic function names, the §15.6 summary table ("| ASIN | Num1 | Num | Arcsine of argument-1 |"), and §15.10 itself. It appears in NO Annex E added/changed list, so nothing in the 2023 standard marks it introduced or altered after 1985. CAVEAT RECORDED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: intrinsic functions entered the 85 line through the 1989 Intrinsic Function Module amendment rather than base ISO 1989:1985, which is how this compiler models --std 85 (the CobolExpressions.g4 functionCall comment says exactly that); on that modelling all four editions apply, and I confirmed all four accept the format identically.

COVERAGE: no spec-derived test exists. A recursive grep of tests/Cobol.Net.Tests.Unit, tests/Cobol.Net.Tests.Conformance and tests/conformance restricted to *.cs/*.cob/*.json returns only incidental substring hits (AsIntrinsicArguments, ReadViewAsInteger, "sending-OPERAND", SkeletonGate); there is no ASIN case anywhere. The only real ASIN references in the repo are the frozen legacy tests/CobolSharp.Tests.Unit/Runtime/IntrinsicFunctionTests.cs#Asin_ViaDispatch and the NIST goldens IF103A/IF401M — a legacy-oracle test and a NIST golden, neither of which may close a row.

OUT-OF-SCOPE OBSERVATION FOR THE CALLER (no rule-id invented): in-asin.json contains NO rule for §15.10.3 (Arguments rules) at all, though that clause has two — r1 "Argument-1 shall be of class numeric" and r2 the -1..+1 domain (both cite.py-validated). ASIN is ABSENT from IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified (whose eleven rows are §15.7 and §15.70-15.79), so post-PB1 its argument class is still UNSCREENED. The extraction that produced this input dropped that clause; it should be re-extracted.

subject: ATAN function
notes:
SECOND ADVERSARIAL PASS: verdict SURVIVES as DIVERGES. I actively tried to soften this to PARTIAL (the natural overturn: "the FORMAT itself — required words, required parentheses, arity 1 — IS enforced; argument admissibility belongs to a §8.4.3.2.3 row") and the attempt FAILS on the grammar's own written contract, quoted below. Recorded here so the reasoning is not re-litigated.

THE FORMAT, FROM THE PRINTED PAGE (not the transcription alone). scripts/render-spec-page.py 850 rendered; printed folio 820 shows `FUNCTION ATAN ( argument-1 )` with FUNCTION and ATAN UNDERLINED, parentheses present, NO brackets and NO ellipsis — exactly one argument, both words required. The specs/ISO_COBOL.md transcription is faithful; the OCR did not introduce a false restriction here.

CITATIONS, all re-validated mechanically this pass: §15.11.2 resolves; `cite.py --check 8.4.3.2.3 "Argument-1 shall be an identifier, a literal"` => OK §8.4.3.2.3 8); `cite.py --check 8.4.3.2.3 "the word FUNCTION is required"` => OK §8.4.3.2.3 2); `cite.py --check 4.2.2 "syntactically distinguishable"` => OK. ⛔ The ONE-LEVEL-SHORT form FAILS and must not propagate: `cite.py --check 8.4.3.2 "Argument-1 shall be an identifier, a literal"` => FAIL. Note the shipped COBOLNET1544 diagnostic text still carries the short form "ISO 8.4.3.2 SR7" — a real, separate citation-hygiene defect worth a sweep.

ENFORCED HALVES, each re-run by this reviewer at default --std 2023. Arity is closed in BindIntrinsicCore from IntrinsicCatalog.Build's Fixed 1..1 row even though `functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (LPAREN functionArgList? RPAREN)?` is a deliberate grammar superset: `FUNCTION ATAN` and `FUNCTION ATAN()` both give "error COBOLNET1504: FUNCTION ATAN takes 1 argument(s); 0 given (ISO 15.3)"; `FUNCTION ATAN(1 2)` gives "...2 given". OMITTED is correctly rejected: `FUNCTION ATAN(OMITTED)` gives "error COBOLNET1544: OMITTED shall not be specified as an intrinsic-function argument". `FUNCTION ATAN(1)` binds and returns 0.785398163.

DIVERGENCE — CONCRETE FAILING INPUT, actually run, exit 0 with ZERO compile-time diagnostics:

       01 R PIC S9(3)V9(9).
       ...
           COMPUTE R = FUNCTION ATAN(LEADING).

It fails only at RUN time: "Unhandled exception. CobolNet.Runtime.NotImplementedCobolFeatureException: ... intrinsic argument 'LEADING'" (exit 127). `FUNCTION ATAN(TRAILING)` reproduces identically, so it is the whole phrase-word set, not one token.

PREMISE CHECKED, not just the rule (the CA12 trap). LEADING is a §8.9 RESERVED word — I grepped the §8.9 list and it is there, and I grepped the §8.10 context-sensitive list and it is NOT there — so it can never be a user-defined word and therefore never an identifier. §8.4.3.2.3 SR8 limits argument-1 to "an identifier, a literal, a boolean expression, or an arithmetic expression"; LEADING is none of the four. The violation is decidable from the token alone, and §4.2.2 requires it to be indicated.

WHY THIS BELONGS TO §15.11.2 AND NOT TO A §8.4.3.2.3 ROW — the point the softening attempt died on. The admission is structural: `functionArgument : fnArgPhraseWord | OMITTED | nonNumericLiteral | arithmeticExpression` with `fnArgPhraseWord : LEADING | TRAILING | LAST | FIRST | ANY | START | AFTER | ALPHANUMERIC | NATIONAL`. The grammar's own comment states the contract verbatim: "A superset rule: which words a given function admits is the binder's §15 job." The general format of §15.11.2 IS that §15 job for ATAN, and the binder has no arm discharging it — so the obligation the grammar delegates is the one this row owns. Those phrase words are legal only inside TRIM (§15.96), FIND-STRING (§15.37), SUBSTITUTE (§15.87) and CONVERT (§15.19). FIX SHAPE (CLAUDE.md rule 5 — the shape that makes the NEXT function automatic): the admissible phrase-word set belongs in the catalog row, empty for ATAN and for every function that takes none, screened once in BindIntrinsicCore with a drift test — never an ATAN-specific arm.

SECONDARY OBSERVATION, correctly attributed AWAY from this row and re-verified. `COMPUTE R = ATAN(1).` with NO REPOSITORY paragraph also compiles clean and dies at run time with "NotImplementedCobolFeatureException: ... reference 'ATAN(1)'". Tempting to book under §8.4.3.2.3 SR2, but the premise does not hold: ATAN is a §8.11 intrinsic-function-name and is NOT in the §8.9 reserved-word list (grepped, no match), so without REPOSITORY it is simply an UNDEFINED data-name and the compiler is right not to bind it as the intrinsic. Control re-run: `COMPUTE R = ZQWXYZ(1).` fails identically — a general undefined-subscripted-reference hole (§8.4.1/§4.2.2) belonging to a reference-resolution row. The LEGAL keyword-omitted form was also re-run and is CORRECT: with `REPOSITORY. FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC.` the same `COMPUTE R = ATAN(1).` compiles and prints 00078539816C (+0.785398163).

EDITIONS: as for AR-15.11.3-1 — Annex E.2 item 13's list of names new in 2023 does not include ATAN, so 2014 and 2023 are established; §15.11.2 carries no edition qualification; the 85/2002 boundary is not establishable from this document, so all four per the brief's fallback, NOT from IntrinsicCatalog's MinEdition column.

test-needed. Verified on disk: nothing under tests/conformance/** mentions ATAN, and no unit or conformance-test method exercises the ATAN format, its arity or its argument admissibility. The covering test must be a NEGATIVE case asserting a compile-time reject of `FUNCTION ATAN(LEADING)`; conformance:negative/... is the right home.

subject: BASECONVERT function
notes: UPHELD after INDEPENDENT re-verification rather than by accepting the prior report. PRINTED PAGE RE-RENDERED AND READ (python scripts/render-spec-page.py 851 = printed folio 821): the format is 'FUNCTION BASECONVERT ( argument-1 argument-2 argument-3 )' with separate underline rules under FUNCTION and under BASECONVERT and none under the parentheses or the arguments -- exactly three arguments, no brackets, no braces, no choice indicators, no ellipsis, so nothing is optional and nothing is repeatable. specs/ISO_COBOL.md:30184 now carries the matching <u>FUNCTION</u> <u>BASECONVERT</u> markup, so the transcription is faithful and the earlier reconciliation defect is repaired. GRAMMAR READ, NOT INFERRED: BASECONVERT is not a lexer token anywhere under src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/, so it arrives through `functionName : IDENTIFIER` and the generic `functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (LPAREN functionArgList? RPAREN)?`, with `functionArgList : functionArgument (FNARG_SEPARATOR? functionArgument)*`. Acceptance AND rejection re-run in both directions: BASECONVERT("FF" 16 10) (the printed juxtaposition form) -> 255; BASECONVERT("FF", 16, 10) (the §8.3.5 comma separator) -> 255; lowercase 'function baseconvert(...)' -> 255; argument-2/argument-3 as PIC 99 DATA ITEMS -> 255; as a DISPLAY operand and nested inside another BASECONVERT -> correct. Arity is enforced by BindIntrinsicCore against the IntrinsicCatalog Fixed 3,3 row: 2 arguments, 4 arguments and the bare 'FUNCTION BASECONVERT' with no parentheses each draw 'error COBOLNET1504: FUNCTION BASECONVERT takes 3 argument(s); N given (ISO 15.3)', and BASECONVERT(OMITTED, 16, 10) draws COBOLNET1544 per §8.4.3.2 SR7. EDITION taken from Annex E.3.3 item 22, NOT from the catalog row, and confirmed at the CLI: --std 85 / 2002 / 2014 each reject with COBOLNET1502 naming 2023. COVERING TEST verified on disk: tests/conformance/2023/intrinsics_string_2023.cob writes the three-argument format three times against tests/conformance/2023/intrinsics_string_2023.out, whose BASECONVERT lines (DEC=255, HEX=FF, BIN=A) I recomputed by hand from §15.12.4 -- spec-derived, not a legacy or GnuCOBOL comparison. ADJACENT, outside this rule's text and NOT counted against it: reference modification of the function result, FUNCTION BASECONVERT("FF", 16, 10)(1:2), is a PARSE ERROR ('COBOL0001: no viable alternative at input (') although §8.4.2.4 SR2 says 'If identifier-1 is a function-identifier, it shall reference an alphanumeric, boolean, or national function' -- an §8.4.2.4 grammar gap affecting every alphanumeric intrinsic, for whoever adjudicates that clause.

subject: BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER function
notes:
ADVERSARIAL PASS 2 - I tried to overturn this and could not; the CONFORMS is upheld on evidence I generated myself, not on the prior report. SCOPE OF THE CLAIM (stated so this row cannot be misread as 'BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER is done'): per scripts/spec/extract_rule_catalog.py, an FMT row is 'the unit of verify this diagram against the grammar rule that implements it' - it is the SYNTAX question only. The SEMANTICS of this function DIVERGE; see RV-15.13.4-1, which is DIVERGES on three independent sites.

(a) TRANSCRIPTION - I did not take the prior report's word for it. I extracted the PDF text layer independently (specs-private/ISO+IEC+1989-2023..., 0-based page 851 = printed folio 822) AND RENDERED THE PAGE IMAGE at 300 dpi (scripts/render-spec-page.py 852) because the standing rule is that OCR'd DIAGRAMS were systematically lossy toward falsely-restrictive syntax. The rendered diagram reads 'FUNCTION BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER ( argument-1  argument-2 )' with FUNCTION and BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER UNDERLINED and nothing else underlined, NO brackets, NO braces, NO ellipsis, one Format only. specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 30217 is faithful. §15.13.2 validated with scripts/spec/cite.py --check.

(b) ACCEPTANCE - every case below re-run by ME on src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/cobol.exe at --std 2023, all yielding 00000101: space-only '(5 8)'; comma '(5, 8)'; semicolon '(5; 8)'; spaces inside the parens '( 5 8 )'; identifier arguments '(IV LN)'; arithmetic-expression argument '(IV - 0, LN)'; SUBSCRIPTED argument '(E(2), 8)'; nested function argument '(FUNCTION INTEGER(5.2), 8)'; and the two forms the prior report did NOT test, which were my best shot at breaking it - SPACE-SEPARATED PARENTHESIZED arguments '((2 + 3) (4 * 2))' and a data-name-headed expression followed by a space-separated parenthesized argument '(N + 0 (4 + 4))', both of which stress the FNARG_SEPARATOR / SUBSCRIPT-mode boundary described in the CobolExpressions.g4 comment. Both accept correctly. Also verified: a USER DATA ITEM NAMED 'BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER' coexists with 'FUNCTION BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER(5, 8)' in the same program and both resolve correctly (the intrinsic-function-name is not wrongly reserved); the format binds in a STRING sending position; and the §8.4.3.2.3 SR2 FUNCTION-omitted form under 'REPOSITORY. FUNCTION BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER INTRINSIC.' works.

(c) REJECTION (the diagram's other half - no bracket means no other arity is legal): 0, 1 and 3 arguments and the bare no-parenthesis form all reject with COBOLNET1504 'FUNCTION BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER takes 2 argument(s); n given (ISO 15.3)', emitted in IntrinsicBinder.BindIntrinsicCore off the IntrinsicCatalog Fixed(2,2) row; OMITTED in an argument position rejects with COBOLNET1544 (§8.4.3.2 SR7). All four re-run by me.

(d) EDITIONS - NOT taken from the IntrinsicCatalog row (I verified that independently of the code). Annex E of the 2023 standard is the SUBSTANTIVE CHANGES list 'between the previous COBOL standard and this Working Draft' (i.e. 2014 -> 2023) and BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER appears nowhere in it - its only post-Annex-E occurrence in specs/ISO_COBOL.md is the Index entry - so 2014 and 2023 are identical. The 85 exclusion is EXTERNAL knowledge, honestly flagged: the 2023 text carries no introduction-edition statement, and the COBOL-85 + 1989 intrinsic-function amendment set of 42 functions contains no boolean function (boolean/bit data - PICTURE 1, USAGE BIT, B"..." literals - is a COBOL-2002 addition, and §15.13.1 makes this function's type boolean).

(e) test-needed (partial). tests/conformance/2002/intrinsics_boolean_conv.cob exists on disk, is registered in tests/conformance/2002/manifest.json AND in tests/CobolSharp.Tests.Integration/ConformanceTests.cs, and is spec-derived (expected values hand-derived from §15.13.4 r1 and the Annex D.10 544 -> low-6-bits example - not a characterization/nist/legacy asset); I re-ran it through the CLI and it reproduces its golden exactly. It covers the format POSITIVELY and only in the comma-separated style. The SPACE-separated form as actually printed in the diagram, and the whole wrong-arity/OMITTED rejection half, appear in NO test asset (COBOLNET1504 and COBOLNET1544 are in no test) - those halves rest on my manual CLI runs above.

(f) CHECKED AND CORRECTLY OUT OF SCOPE (I re-tested the prior report's two dismissals rather than accepting them). (i) 'MOVE BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER(5, 8) TO B8' with NO REPOSITORY entry compiles silently and dies at run time with an UNHANDLED NotImplementedCobolFeatureException instead of a bind-time 'undefined data item'. This is NOT a §15.13.2 leniency: I ran the control 'MOVE ZZ-UNDEFINED-THING(5, 8) TO B8' and 'MOVE UPPER-CASE("abc") TO B8' and BOTH are equally undiagnosed, so the missing diagnostic is the generic undefined-subscripted-reference gap, not this function's. (ii) Reference modification of a function-identifier is a parse error for UPPER-CASE too, so it is a §8.4.3.1.2 / §8.4.3.2 diagram gap, i.e. a different FMT row.

subject: BYTE-LENGTH function
notes: test-needed. VERDICT SURVIVES REVIEW, re-verified. The general format is `FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH ( argument-1 [ PHYSICAL ] )` (specs/ISO_COBOL.md, §15.14.2: FUNCTION, BYTE-LENGTH and PHYSICAL underlined, PHYSICAL bracketed = an OPTIONAL required-word phrase). I did NOT rely on the prior pass's page render: the transcription is corroborated INDEPENDENTLY by Table 21, whose BYTE-LENGTH row reads `Alph1 or Anum1 or Bool1 or Ind1 or Nat1 or Num1 or Obj 1 or Ptr1 or Type1, Key2` — the `Key2` is the PHYSICAL keyword argument, and §15.3 item 7 defines the Keyword argument type. §15.14.4 r6 and r7 both turn on whether PHYSICAL was specified, so the phrase is normative, not decorative. COBOL.NET accepts NO second argument: the catalog row is `Add(new("BYTE-LENGTH", IntrinsicType.Integer, IntrinsicArity.Fixed, 1, 1, "s", ...))` and the grammar has NO PHYSICAL token at all (zero hits for PHYSICAL under src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/; fnArgPhraseWord lists only LEADING/TRAILING/LAST/FIRST/ANY/START/AFTER/ALPHANUMERIC/NATIONAL), so the word arrives as a bare dataReference through functionArgument's arithmeticExpression alternative and counts as a SECOND argument. Failing input, legal COBOL-2023, run verbatim: `IDENTIFICATION DIVISION. PROGRAM-ID. RVPHYS01. DATA DIVISION. WORKING-STORAGE SECTION. 01 G. 05 A PIC X(5). PROCEDURE DIVISION. DISPLAY FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH(G PHYSICAL). STOP RUN.` -> `error COBOLNET1504: FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH takes 1 argument(s); 2 given (ISO 15.3)`. SIBLING TO SWEEP: §15.50.2 FUNCTION LENGTH carries the SAME `[ PHYSICAL ]` phrase and the same Fixed(1,1) catalog row, so the fix is one grammar phrase word plus two catalog rows and two binder arms, not one. Note the 2023 standard omits PHYSICAL from §8.9 and §8.10 (grep-verified: the only PHYSICAL occurrences are the two general formats, §15.14.4 r6/r7, §15.50.4 r7/r8 and the index) — an ISO editorial gap, not a licence to reject the format; src/Cobol.Net.Editions/ReservedWords.Table.cs already carries a PHYSICAL row. Editions per the AR-15.14.3-1 derivation (Annex E is silent on PHYSICAL).

subject: CHAR function
notes: Verdict unchanged; supplies the missing spec-derived test. Exact case: 15.15.4 r1 makes the argument an ORDINAL POSITION (1-based) in the alphanumeric program collating sequence, so CHAR(66) is the character with native code 65.

subject: CHAR-NATIONAL function
notes: UPHELD — re-verified independently rather than inherited. The transcription at §15.16.2 carries '<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>CHAR-NATIONAL</u> ( argument-1 )': both words underlined (required, §5.2.2), exactly one argument, no brackets, braces or choice indicators — nothing optional, nothing dropped. Grammar: 'functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (LPAREN functionArgList? RPAREN)?' with 'functionName : IDENTIFIER | DISPLAY | LENGTH | MERGE | NATIONAL | BIT | RANDOM | SIGN | SORT | SUM' — CHAR-NATIONAL has no lexer token, so it arrives as IDENTIFIER; the per-function shape is enforced from the catalog row (Fixed 1,1). RAN: 'FUNCTION CHAR-NATIONAL (65 66)' -> COBOLNET1504 '1 argument(s); 2 given'; 'FUNCTION CHAR-NATIONAL' with no parens -> COBOLNET1504 '0 given'; 'FUNCTION CHAR-NATIONAL (66)' compiles and runs at 2002/2014/2023 and is refused at --std 85 with COBOLNET1502. Also RAN the three legal argument shapes the format admits through §15.3 type 6, none falsely rejected: a subscripted operand 'FUNCTION CHAR-NATIONAL (ENTRYX (1))', an arithmetic expression 'FUNCTION CHAR-NATIONAL (64 + 2)', and a nested function 'FUNCTION CHAR-NATIONAL (FUNCTION ORD ("A"))' — all three printed A. The cited golden exists on disk (tests/conformance/2002/char_national.cob), writes this exact format, and was re-run green against its .out.

subject: COMBINED-DATETIME function
notes: OVERTURNED FROM CONFORMS. The general format carries TWO underlined REQUIRED words and only ONE of them is enforced. Citation validated: `cite.py --check 15.17.2 "COMBINED-DATETIME"` -> OK, format line `<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>COMBINED-DATETIME</u> ( argument-1 argument-2 )`. ENFORCED HALF (re-verified by me, not inherited): arity and the parentheses come from the catalog row (IntrinsicArity.Fixed, 2, 2) checked in BindIntrinsicCore - 1 argument, 3 arguments, `()` and a bare `FUNCTION COMBINED-DATETIME` with no parentheses each produce `error COBOLNET1504: FUNCTION COMBINED-DATETIME takes 2 argument(s); N given (ISO 15.3)`; the space-separated form the format literally prints, `FUNCTION COMBINED-DATETIME(WS-ID WS-S12)`, binds as two arguments and returns the same value as the comma form; the edition gate emits COBOLNET1502 at --std 85 and --std 2002 and is clean at 2014/2023. UNENFORCED HALF - the required word FUNCTION. §8.4.3.2.3 SR2 (cite.py --check 8.4.3.2.3 "the word FUNCTION is required" -> OK): 'If intrinsic-function-name-1 or the ALL phrase is specified in the REPOSITORY paragraph ... the word FUNCTION may be omitted from the function-identifier; otherwise the word FUNCTION is required.' CONCRETE FAILING INPUT, run at --std 2023 AND --std 2014, with NO REPOSITORY paragraph anywhere in the program: `01 WS-ID PIC 9(7) VALUE 143951. 01 WS-SEC PIC 9(5) VALUE 45296. 01 WS-CD5 PIC Z(6)9.9(5). MOVE COMBINED-DATETIME(WS-ID, WS-SEC) TO WS-CD5.` -> compiles with ZERO diagnostics, exit code 0, assembly written; it fails only at run time with `NotImplementedCobolFeatureException: ... reference 'COMBINED-DATETIME(WS-ID, WS-SEC)'`. The positive counterpart is correct (adding `REPOSITORY. FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC.` makes the same statement print `REP= 143951.45296`), so `IntrinsicBinder.KeywordOmittedFunction` implements SR2's permission but nothing enforces its 'otherwise'. ATTRIBUTION, stated honestly: the mechanism is GENERIC unresolved-reference staging in `ExpressionBinder.RefFailure`, not an intrinsic-path defect - `MOVE ZZ-NOT-DEFINED(WS-ID, WS-SEC) TO WS-CD5` behaves identically - so the fix belongs in name resolution; but the consequence is that this format's required word is not enforced, which is why the row cannot read CONFORMS. WHY THE PRIOR CONFORMS WAS NOT SAFE: its ALL-subscript evidence is false. It reported `WS-T(ALL)` 'rejected (expands to 3, arity error)', which was an artifact of a 3-element table. With a TWO-element table, `MOVE FUNCTION COMBINED-DATETIME(WS-T(ALL)) TO WS-CD5` compiles clean and prints `ALL= 143951.45296` - one argument specifier accepted where the format writes two. I do NOT downgrade on that, because §8.4.2.3.3 SR6 (cite.py-validated: 'The subscript ALL may be used only: - When the subscripted identifier is used as an intrinsic function argument') permits ALL in ANY intrinsic-function argument, which is broader than §15.3's 'When the definition of a function permits an argument to be repeated a variable number of times'; the two clauses are in tension and the compiler's acceptance is defensible under SR6. It is recorded because it shows the prior CONFORMS rested on an untested happy path. TEST: tests/conformance/2014/formatted_datetime.cob (read on disk, .out present) writes the general format at `MOVE FUNCTION COMBINED-DATETIME(WS-ID, WS-SEC) TO WS-CDT` and the golden pins `CDT= 153569.45296` - it covers the ACCEPT half only; test-needed for a negative fixture covering the arity rejections and the missing-FUNCTION rejection. EDITIONS: Annex E.2 item 13 establishes >= 2014 (COMBINED-DATETIME is not among the seven names new in 2023); the 2002/85 boundary is not derivable from this document, and the exclusion is asserted, not spec-derived. Not taken from IntrinsicCatalog's row.

subject: CONVERT function
notes:
SUSTAINED, both consequences re-run. THE ALTERNATIVES ARE RIGHT; THE POSITIONS ARE NOT. All four source words and all five destination shapes bind, with the 15.19.1 result type (NAT destination -> PicCategory.National, everything else Alphanumeric - re-verified: CONVERT(WS-N NAT NAT HEX) returns the digits as NATIONAL positions, 0030 0030 0034 0031). But BindConvert harvests EVERY keyword-shaped argument into `kws` irrespective of POSITION (`foreach (var a in argCtxs) { if (KeywordWordOf(a) is { } w && IsConvertFormatWord(w)) { kws.Add(w); continue; } operands.Add(...); }`), while the general format fixes `( argument-1 source-format destination-format )` (--check 15.19.2 "argument-1 source-format destination-format" -> OK).
(1) REJECTS LEGAL COBOL. ANUM/BYTE/HEX/NAT are CONTEXT-SENSITIVE words: I re-verified the 8.10 table rows in specs/ISO_COBOL.md - '| ANUM | CONVERT intrinsic function |', '| BYTE | CONVERT intrinsic function |', '| HEX | CONVERT intrinsic function |', '| NAT | CONVERT intrinsic function |' - and 8.10's lead-in (--check 8.10 "treated as a user-defined word" -> OK) says a context-sensitive word used where it is NOT permitted in the general format is treated as a user-defined word. 8.9 reserves only ALPHANUMERIC, ANY and NATIONAL. Argument-1 is not a position where those four words are permitted, so a data item so named is legal there. Re-run:
       01 NAT     PIC XX VALUE "41".
           MOVE FUNCTION CONVERT(NAT HEX ANUM) TO WS-R.
-> `error COBOLNET1504: FUNCTION CONVERT takes argument-1 source-format destination-format (ISO 15.19.2); 0 operand + 3 format keyword(s) given`. Expected SH=[A] (15.19.4 r1). The declaration itself is accepted, so only the CONVERT reference is turned away. Same defect for an item named ANUM, HEX or BYTE.
(2) ACCEPTS SYNTAX THE FORMAT DOES NOT ADMIT. Re-run: `CONVERT(ANUM WS-A ANUM HEX)` (source-format BEFORE argument-1) prints 41, and `CONVERT(ANUM ANUM HEX WS-A)` (argument-1 LAST, after the entire destination-format) also prints 41. The harvest is fully position-free.
Also latent: the IntrinsicCatalog row is `Add(new("CONVERT", IntrinsicType.Alphanumeric, IntrinsicArity.Variadic, 2, 4, "s", ...))` - min arity 2 where the format's minimum is 3 (argument-1 plus two format words), and the declared ArgKinds "s" is inert because CONVERT is absent from IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified.
FIGURE CHECK - the transcription is FAITHFUL and the printed FIGURE is the defective artefact; do NOT 'fix' the compiler toward it. The destination-format figure uses braces throughout, which literally makes HEX mandatory in the non-BYTE branch. Three places in the standard's own PROSE contradict that and are decisive: the 15.19.1 type-table rows 'ALPHANUMERIC alone' and 'NATIONAL alone' (--check 15.19.1 "The type of this function depends upon the keywords in the destination format list" -> OK), 15.19.4 r1/r3 ('When the destination-format is ANUM / NAT'), and 15.19.4 NOTE 3 b. Rule 3 (source differs from destination) is also unstatable without bare ANUM/NAT destinations. The compiler treats HEX as optional and is RIGHT to.
Test-ref kept for the alternatives half only; it does not exercise the position rule - a position test is still needed.
Editions: 2023 only, from Annex E item 24; NOT the IntrinsicCatalog row.
