subject: CURRENT-DATE function
notes: OVERTURNED PARTIAL -> DIVERGES, and a SECOND rejection of legal source the prior pass missed. Citations re-run: cite.py --check 15.21.2 '<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>CURRENT-DATE</u>' OK (the prior pass's plain-text form FAILS the checker - the format lives inside the <pre>/<u> markup); 15.21.1 'returns a 21-character alphanumeric value' OK; 8.4.3.2.3 SR2 'the word FUNCTION may be omitted from the function-identifier' OK; 8.4.3.2.3 SR6 'the left parenthesis is always treated as the left parenthesis of that function's arguments' OK; 8.4.3.3.3 SR2 'shall reference an alphanumeric, boolean, or national function' OK; 12.3.8.1 'intrinsic-function-names that may be used without specifying the word FUNCTION' OK; 15.23.3 r5 / 15.100.3 r5 '(FUNCTION NUMVAL (FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE (1:4)))' OK. ACCEPTING HALF IS CORRECT: IntrinsicCatalog#Build carries CURRENT-DATE as IntrinsicArity.Fixed 0..0; IntrinsicBinder#BindIntrinsicCore's MinArgs/MaxArgs arm rejects an argument. RAN 'MOVE FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE TO WS-CD' (PIC X(21)) at --std 85 and 2023 -> '2026073010394849-0700'; 'MOVE FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE(WS-N)' -> 'error COBOLNET1504: FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE takes 0 argument(s); 1 given (ISO 15.3)'. DIVERGENCE (a) REFERENCE-MODIFIED FORM REJECTED - ACTUALLY RUN, all four editions: source 'IDENTIFICATION DIVISION. PROGRAM-ID. CDR1. DATA DIVISION. WORKING-STORAGE SECTION. 01 WS-YR PIC X(4). PROCEDURE DIVISION. MOVE FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE (1:4) TO WS-YR DISPLAY "YR=[" WS-YR "]" STOP RUN.' -> 'CDR1.cob(8,39): error COBOL0001: no viable alternative at input '('' + 'error COBOL0001: unexpected '(''. It is legal: 8.4.3.3.3 SR2 permits reference modification of a function-identifier that references an alphanumeric function and 15.21.1 makes CURRENT-DATE alphanumeric; 8.4.3.2.3 SR6's argument-paren preemption is conditioned on 'If a function's definition permits arguments' and 15.21.2's format permits NONE, so the '(' can only be a reference-modifier. The standard writes this exact shape in NORMATIVE text three times - 15.23.3 r5, 15.25.3 r5, 15.100.3 r5 'FUNCTION NUMVAL (FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE (1:4))'. Root cause: CobolExpressions.g4#functionCall is 'FUNCTION functionName (LPAREN functionArgList? RPAREN)?' with NO refModPart tail (refModPart exists only in CobolParserCore.g4, reachable only from dataReference). Sibling sweep: 'MOVE FUNCTION UPPER-CASE("abc") (1:2) TO WS-A.' fails identically at col 44, so reference modification of ANY function-identifier is unimplemented. DIVERGENCE (b) NEW - THE KEYWORD-OMITTED ZERO-ARGUMENT FORM SILENTLY COMPILES AND CRASHES AT RUN TIME (missed entirely by the prior pass): source 'IDENTIFICATION DIVISION. PROGRAM-ID. CDR4. ENVIRONMENT DIVISION. CONFIGURATION SECTION. REPOSITORY. FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC. DATA DIVISION. WORKING-STORAGE SECTION. 01 WS-CD PIC X(21). PROCEDURE DIVISION. MOVE CURRENT-DATE TO WS-CD DISPLAY "CD=[" WS-CD "]" STOP RUN.' compiles with ZERO diagnostics and then throws 'CobolNet.Runtime.NotImplementedCobolFeatureException: ... reference 'CURRENT-DATE'' - reproduced at --std 2002, 2014 AND 2023, and identically with the explicit specifier 'FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE INTRINSIC.'. It is legal: 12.3.8.1 'It also allows declaration of intrinsic-function-names that may be used without specifying the word FUNCTION' + 8.4.3.2.3 SR2; and 8.4.3.2.2's general format makes the whole parenthesized argument list optional, so the bare name IS a complete function-identifier. The standard writes the combined keyword-omitted + reference-modified shape itself at D.14.3.6: 'MOVE FUNCTION LOCALE-DATE (CURRENT-DATE (1:8)) TO a-date-field.'. Root cause is structural and exact - IntrinsicBinder#KeywordOmittedFunction opens with 'var suffixes = dref.dataReferenceSuffix(); if (suffixes.Length != 1 || suffixes[0].subscriptPart() is not { } sp) return null;' so the path is reachable ONLY through a name(args) subscript shape; a ZERO-argument keyword-omitted reference has ZERO suffixes, never reaches IntrinsicCatalog, and falls through to an unresolved data reference (control: an undeclared 'NO-SUCH-NAME' produces the byte-identical loud stage). Sibling sweep: 'COMPUTE WS-P = PI' under FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC fails the same way, so EVERY zero-argument intrinsic (CURRENT-DATE, PI, E, WHEN-COMPILED, RANDOM, the EXCEPTION-* group) is unreachable in the keyword-omitted form. The fix is the suffix-count relaxation plus a zero-argument bind, not a per-function patch. SECONDARY, accepting too much: 'MOVE FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE () TO WS-CD' is ACCEPTED and evaluates, but 15.21.2's format carries no parentheses and 8.4.3.2.3 SR6 cannot make that '(' an argument paren for a function that permits no arguments, so it is a malformed reference-modifier and should be diagnosed. TEST COVERAGE: the cited test exists on disk at tests/Cobol.Net.Tests.Conformance/IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests.cs line 284 and is spec-derived - AssertSpec runs 'new CobolNetCompiler(dialect).CompileAndRun' and Assert.Equal against a literal, no legacy/GnuCOBOL oracle anywhere in the path - and it writes 'FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE' in the bare general-format shape, so it covers the accepting half ONLY. test-needed for (i) the 0-arity negative (COBOLNET1504), (ii) the 8.4.3.3.3 SR2 reference-modified form, (iii) the 12.3.8.1 keyword-omitted zero-argument form. BOOKKEEPING: CURRENT-DATE is absent from IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified; vacuous for a zero-argument function, but PI carries an explicit ["PI"] = (' ', '15.73.2 - no arguments') row for exactly this case, so CURRENT-DATE should carry the twin and keep IntrinsicArgumentClassDriftTests honest.

subject: DATE-OF-INTEGER function
notes: SURVIVES REVIEW. Independently re-verified rather than inherited. Symbols confirmed literally present: `functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (LPAREN functionArgList? RPAREN)?` at CobolExpressions.g4, `public static class IntrinsicCatalog`, and `BindIntrinsicArgs` in IntrinsicBinder.cs; the catalog row is `Add(new("DATE-OF-INTEGER", IntrinsicType.Integer, IntrinsicArity.Fixed, 1, 1, "i", "DateOfInteger", ...))` — Fixed 1..1, matching the single parenthesized argument-1 of §15.22.2. Positive forms RAN clean: `FUNCTION DATE-OF-INTEGER(143951)`, `FUNCTION DATE-OF-INTEGER ( 143951 )` (separator spaces), an identifier operand, an arithmetic-expression operand `(A + B)`, a numeric-edited operand, and the call as an EVALUATE subject and in an IF condition. Negative direction RAN: two arguments gives 'error COBOLNET1504: FUNCTION DATE-OF-INTEGER takes 1 argument(s); 2 given (ISO 15.3)'; the paren-less form is caught by the same arity arm ('0 given'), so the grammar's optional argument-list parenthesis does not let the format through. Identical acceptance under --std 85, 2002, 2014 and 2023 (all four print 16010101 for the epoch case). Test-ref re-verified ON DISK at tests/Cobol.Net.Tests.Conformance/IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests.cs line 265; its helper `AssertSpec` compiles and compares to a hand-written expectation with NO oracle involved (`AssertSameAsLegacy` is a different helper this method does not call), so it is genuinely spec-derived and it does compile the §15.22.2 form. Caveat, not a defect: the test pins only the POSITIVE form; the arity rejection is unpinned by any checked-in spec-derived test.

subject: DATE-TO-YYYYMMDD function
notes: SUSTAINED. PRINTED PAGE RE-RENDERED INDEPENDENTLY (python scripts/render-spec-page.py 867 = printed folio 837) because of the falsely-restrictive OCR risk: the printed format is character-for-character the transcription - FUNCTION and DATE-TO-YYYYMMDD underlined (required words), argument-1 unbracketed, argument-3 NESTED inside argument-2's brackets, so the optional arguments are strictly trailing. No alternative was lost. Grammar side: the reference is the GENERIC `FUNCTION functionName (LPAREN functionArgList? RPAREN)?` in CobolExpressions.g4, so no per-function rule can be falsely restrictive, and the arity comes from the catalog row via IntrinsicBinder's `if (args.Count < sig.MinArgs || args.Count > sig.MaxArgs)` -> COBOLNET1504. Verified by running the built CLI: 0 arguments and 4 arguments are both rejected ('FUNCTION DATE-TO-YYYYMMDD takes 1..3 argument(s)'); the 1-, 2- and 3-argument forms all compile and evaluate; SPACE-separated arguments `(851003 10 2002)` are accepted as well as comma-separated; arithmetic-expression arguments `(850000 + 1003, 5 + 5, 2000 + 2)` are accepted, as 8.4.3.2.3 SR8 requires ('Argument-1 shall be an identifier, a literal, a boolean expression, or an arithmetic expression'); the FUNCTION word is correctly optional under `REPOSITORY. FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC.` (`DATE-TO-YYYYMMDD(851003, 10, 2002)` -> 19851003), per 8.4.3.2.3 SR2; and OMITTED is correctly not applicable here (8.4.3.2.3 SR7 forbids it for an intrinsic-function-name). COVERAGE CAVEAT (not a downgrade): tests/conformance/2002/intrinsics_date_window.cob is on disk and exercises the 3-argument shape of this format through the real grammar with hand-derived values, but the 1- and 2-argument shapes and the arity rejection have no COBOL-level test - a narrow additional test-needed.

subject: DAY-TO-YYYYDDD function
notes:
⛔ OVERTURNED: CONFORMS -> PARTIAL. The adjudicator verified the ARITY half of the general format thoroughly and never tested the REQUIRED-WORD half, which is the other half of the same one-line format. Citation re-validated: `cite.py --check 15.25.2 "FUNCTION</u> <u>DAY-TO-YYYYDDD"` -> OK.
TRANSCRIPTION - INDEPENDENTLY CORROBORATED, so the printed-page claim is not merely inherited: the spec-reconciliation ledger docs/rearchitecture/spec-reconciliation/agents/compare-p867-p878.json records '870 15.25.2 FUNCTION DAY-TO-YYYYDDD ( argument-1 [ argument-2 [ argument-3 ] ] ) -- faithful' from the PDF pass. FUNCTION and DAY-TO-YYYYDDD are underlined (REQUIRED words), the parentheses are literal separators, argument-1 is unbracketed, argument-2/argument-3 are NESTED-optional. No OCR over-restriction; nothing to repair.
ARITY HALF - VERIFIED, RE-RUN, AND IT HOLDS. The shape comes from the generic `functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (LPAREN functionArgList? RPAREN)?` plus the catalog row `Add(new("DAY-TO-YYYYDDD", IntrinsicType.Integer, IntrinsicArity.OptionalTrailing, 1, 3, "iii", "DayToYyyyddd", ...))`, enforced by `if (args.Count < sig.MinArgs || args.Count > sig.MaxArgs)` -> COBOLNET1504. 1..3 OptionalTrailing IS the nested-optional format, because trailing arguments are positional. Every arm re-run: 0 arguments -> `error COBOLNET1504 ... 0 given`; 4 -> `error COBOLNET1504 ... 4 given`; 1, 2 and 3 all bind and evaluate; `FUNCTION DAY-TO-YYYYDDD(10004, OMITTED, 2002)` -> `error COBOLNET1544` (§8.4.3.2.3 SR7 read in the spec: 'The word OMITTED shall not be specified if intrinsic-function-name-1 is specified'), which is what keeps the nesting genuine; expression arguments and the nested-function argument `FUNCTION DAY-TO-YYYYDDD(FUNCTION INTEGER(F), 20, 2002)` both bind to 2010004.
REQUIRED-WORD HALF - NOT ENFORCED, AND THAT IS WHY THIS ROW STAYS OPEN. §8.4.3.2.3 SR2 (read in full): 'If intrinsic-function-name-1 or the ALL phrase is specified in the REPOSITORY paragraph ... the word FUNCTION may be omitted from the function-identifier; otherwise the word FUNCTION is required.' RAN, with NO REPOSITORY paragraph:
       01  R  PIC 9(7).
           COMPUTE R = DAY-TO-YYYYDDD(10004, 20, 2002)
The compiler accepts it, emits an assembly, and the program dies at RUN time with `Unhandled exception. CobolNet.Runtime.NotImplementedCobolFeatureException: ... a COBOL feature that is not yet implemented was reached at run time: reference 'DAY-TO-YYYYDDD(10004, 20, 2002)'` - no diagnostic naming the violation, and a message that tells the user the compiler is incomplete rather than that the source is in error. CONTROL runs isolating it: the same text WITH `REPOSITORY. FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC.` binds correctly (`REPO=2010004`), and an arbitrary undefined name of the same shape (`NO-SUCH-NAME(10004, 20, 2002)`) produces the IDENTICAL loud stub - so the enforcement point is a generic unresolved-reference fallback, not a rule about this format, and this format's required word is enforced only by accident. Graded PARTIAL rather than DIVERGES because the program does abort rather than return a wrong value, but the row must not close: §4.2.2's warning mechanism 'shall indicate violations of such rules', and a runtime 'not yet implemented' is not that indication.
TEST: tests/conformance/2002/intrinsics_date_window.cob and its .out are both on disk; T10/T11 write the full three-argument form, which exercises the format's maximal arm and its required words. GAP: no spec-derived test exercises the ONE- or TWO-argument arm, the over-arity reject, the OMITTED reject, or the missing-FUNCTION reject. test-needed: a negative case for `DAY-TO-YYYYDDD(...)` without REPOSITORY expecting a COMPILE-TIME diagnostic, plus positive cases for the 1- and 2-argument arms.
EDITIONS: the general format is unchanged across 2002/2014/2023 in the document under review; all four --std settings re-run (COBOLNET1502 at 85). Not derived from IntrinsicCatalog's row.

subject: DISPLAY-OF function
notes: UPHELD. I did NOT take the rendering on trust - I re-rendered the printed page myself (python scripts/render-spec-page.py 872 -> printed folio 842) and read it: the format is exactly 'FUNCTION DISPLAY-OF ( argument-1 [ argument-2 ] )', FUNCTION and DISPLAY-OF underlined, only argument-2 bracketed, no ellipsis, no repetition, no third operand. specs/ISO_COBOL.md 15.26.2 matches the printed page, so there is no falsely-restrictive OCR residue. Grammar: functionCall is the generic superset 'FUNCTION functionName (LPAREN functionArgList? RPAREN)?' (read at CobolExpressions.g4:264), so the per-function shape is the catalog arity - IntrinsicArity.OptionalTrailing, MinArgs 1 / MaxArgs 2 - enforced in BindIntrinsicCore. RAN MYSELF at --std 2023: 1 argument accepted; 2 arguments accepted; the bare keyword-only form FUNCTION DISPLAY-OF with no parentheses at all -> COBOLNET1504 'takes 1..2 argument(s); 0 given'; 3 arguments -> COBOLNET1504 '3 given'; and the 15.3 ALL-subscript shape FUNCTION DISPLAY-OF(N-E(ALL)) over an OCCURS 3 table -> COBOLNET1504 '3 given', i.e. rejected, which is the right outcome since 15.26 does not permit a repeated argument. conformance:2002/national_intrinsics verified on disk with its golden and its tests/conformance/2002/manifest.json entry, and it exercises both admissible shapes. NOTED, and deliberately NOT charged to this rule: FUNCTION DISPLAY-OF(N-SRC)(2:3) is a parse error (COBOL0001 'no viable alternative at input (') - the reference-modifier belongs to the 8.4.3.2 function-identifier format, not to the 15.26.2 general format, so it is out of scope here but is a real gap for whoever adjudicates 8.4.3.2.

subject: E function
notes: REFUTER RE-ADJUDICATION - verdict SURVIVES, both legs re-verified independently on the built CLI at src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/cobol.exe, and a SECOND defect leg added. Citations re-validated mechanically: cite.py --check 15.27.2 '<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>E</u>' -> OK; cite.py --check 15.27.1 'type of the function is numeric' -> OK; cite.py --check 8.4.3.2.3 'the word FUNCTION may be omitted' -> OK while cite.py --check 8.4.3.2 on the same phrase FAILS (the source comments at IntrinsicBinder.KeywordOmittedFunction and ReparseArgs cite '8.4.3.2 SR2' / '8.4.3.2 SR8' and are ONE LEVEL SHORT - the rules are in 8.4.3.2.3). WHAT CONFORMS (re-run by me, not inherited): FUNCTION E binds and evaluates in COMPUTE / MOVE / DISPLAY / IF; arity 0..0 is enforced - 'COMPUTE R05 = FUNCTION E (1).' -> COBOLNET1504 'FUNCTION E takes 0 argument(s); 1 given'; 'FUNCTION E ()' is accepted and prints 2.71828, which is CORRECT rather than lenient - the 8.4.3.2.2 function-identifier general format brackets argument-1 INSIDE the parenthesized group (figure note: the parentheses are literal separators, the bracketed item optional) and the 8.4.3.2.3 SR6 NOTE itself writes 'FUNCTION RANDOM ()'; a user data item named E coexists with the intrinsic ('01 E PIC 9 VALUE 7.' displays 7 while FUNCTION E returns e); the edition window is gated - --std 85 -> COBOLNET1502 'FUNCTION E was introduced by ISO/IEC 1989:2002', evaluates at 2002/2014/2023. EDITIONS DERIVED INDEPENDENTLY OF INTRINSICCATALOG: E is absent from the 1989 Intrinsic Function Module amendment's 42-function set and is a COBOL-2002 addition (same derivation the repo records for its other 2002 intrinsic rows, e.g. the BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER / YEAR-TO-YYYY constructs.json vcr notes: 'derive from the 2002 standard - absent from the 1989 Intrinsic Function Module set'); the 2023 Annex E.3 'intrinsic functions added or enhanced' list (BASECONVERT / CONCAT / CONVERT / EXCEPTION-FILE / FIND-STRING / MODULE-NAME / SMALLEST-ALGEBRAIC / SUBSTITUTE / TRIM) does not contain E, so it is not a 2023 addition either. LEG 1 - KEYWORD-OMITTED SPELLING SILENTLY MIS-COMPILES (re-run by me). 8.4.3.2.3 SR2 makes a bare E a legal function-identifier under REPOSITORY. FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC. IntrinsicBinder.KeywordOmittedFunction returns null unless the dataReference carries EXACTLY ONE suffix that is a subscriptPart ('if (suffixes.Length != 1 || suffixes[0].subscriptPart() is not { } sp) return null;'), and it is the ONLY routing path (the two dataReference chokepoints RefExpr / FieldOperand), so a ZERO-argument keyword-omitted intrinsic can never route. Verified input: 'IDENTIFICATION DIVISION. PROGRAM-ID. EOMIT01. ENVIRONMENT DIVISION. CONFIGURATION SECTION. REPOSITORY. FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC. DATA DIVISION. WORKING-STORAGE SECTION. 01 R05 PIC 9.9(5). PROCEDURE DIVISION. MAIN-PARA. COMPUTE R05 = E. DISPLAY "OMIT=" R05. STOP RUN.' at --std 2023 compiles with NO diagnostic and then throws NotImplementedCobolFeatureException "reference 'E'" at run time. Same one-pattern hole for every zero-argument intrinsic (E, PI, RANDOM, CURRENT-DATE, WHEN-COMPILED) - one fix; the fix must accept a bare cobolWord with ZERO suffixes when the name is a REPOSITORY-visible zero-arity intrinsic and resolves to no data item. LEG 2 - NEW, FOUND BY THIS REFUTER: the format FUNCTION E cannot be written as an operand of an ARITHMETIC STATEMENT at all. 'ADD FUNCTION E TO A30.' and 'SUBTRACT FUNCTION E FROM A.' and 'MULTIPLY FUNCTION E BY B.' are all rejected at parse time with COBOL0001 'no viable alternative at input ADDFUNCTION' / 'unexpected FUNCTION' (verified at --std 2023; identical rejection for 'ADD FUNCTION LENGTH(S) TO A30', so this is not E-specific but every function-identifier). Root cause read in the grammar: 'addOperand : dataReference | literal;' in CobolParserCore.g4 has no functionCall alternative, and the SUBTRACT / MULTIPLY operand rules follow the same shape. This is legal COBOL: 14.9.2.3 SR2 (validated verbatim) says 'Identifier-1 and identifier-2 shall reference numeric data items', 8.4.3.2.1 (validated verbatim) says 'A function-identifier references the unique data item that results from the evaluation of a function', and 15.27.1 (validated) makes that item numeric. Recorded on this row because it directly bounds where the 15.27.2 general format may appear; the fix belongs in the shared arithmetic-statement operand rule, not in an E-specific arm. BOOKKEEPING (not a conformance defect): E is absent from BOTH IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified and IntrinsicArgumentRules.DeliberatelyUnscreened, where the zero-argument sibling PI carries the explicit placeholder ['PI'] = (' ', '15.73.2 - no arguments') added, per its own comment, 'so the drift test can hold this table and the Phase-B batch's function list in agreement rather than silently tolerating a gap'. E takes no arguments so the PB1 15.3 class screen has nothing to screen, but IntrinsicArgumentClassDriftTests now has an unpaired name. TEST COVERAGE: test-needed. Re-grepped tests/conformance, tests/Cobol.Net.Tests.Unit, tests/Cobol.Net.Tests.Conformance and tests/version-matrix - NO test references FUNCTION E in any spelling (the only 'E' hits are string literals in literal_concat.cob, oo_method_indexed_search.cob, Condition88DifferentialTests.cs and CorrespondingDifferentialTests.cs). conformance-test:IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests.EmptyParens_NoArgFunction_2014 does exist on disk at tests/Cobol.Net.Tests.Conformance/IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests.cs line 857 but exercises PI, so it covers nothing here.

subject: EXCEPTION-FILE function
notes: UPHELD, and re-verified independently rather than inherited. I re-rendered the PRINTED page myself (python scripts/render-spec-page.py 874 -> folio 844): the diagram is exactly `FUNCTION EXCEPTION-FILE [(argument-1)]` with FUNCTION and EXCEPTION-FILE underlined and argument-1 not underlined inside the optional group -- the Markdown transcription is faithful, with no falsely-restrictive OCR artifact, and it is corroborated by the 15.2 function table row ("EXCEPTION-FILE | File1 | Anum ... If optional argument-1 is specified") and by Annex E.3.3 item 25. Grammar realizes the shape as a superset (`functionCall` : FUNCTION functionName (LPAREN functionArgList? RPAREN)?) and the catalog row pins arity 0..1. I re-ran every shape at --std 2023: `FUNCTION EXCEPTION-FILE` -> ok; `FUNCTION EXCEPTION-FILE(FA)` -> ok; `FUNCTION EXCEPTION-FILE()` -> ok, which is CONFORMING, not lax -- the standard's own 8.4.3.2.3 SR6 NOTE writes `FUNCTION MAX (FUNCTION RANDOM () A B)`; `FUNCTION EXCEPTION-FILE(FA FB)` -> "error COBOLNET1504: FUNCTION EXCEPTION-FILE takes 0..1 argument(s); 2 given (ISO 15.3)". Edition realization re-run at all four --std values from one source: the no-argument form is accepted at 2002/2014/2023 and rejected at 85 (COBOLNET1502), and the bracketed argument-1 form is accepted only at 2023, rejected at 85/2002/2014 (COBOLNET0900) -- the 2023 window taken from Annex E.3.3 item 25, not from the catalog row under review. Out of scope for THIS rule and not scored against it: `FUNCTION EXCEPTION-FILE(1:2)` fails to parse at every edition, but so does `FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE(1:4)` -- that is a general 8.4.3 reference-modification-of-a-function-identifier gap, not a defect in this function's general format. Docs debt (not a conformance defect): the IntrinsicCatalog.cs EXCEPTION-FILE row comment still says the 2023 file-connector-arg form "renders loud -- VCR row 68", and docs/VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE.md rows 68/69 still carry `new-feature-gate <!-- todo -->`; the form is implemented.

subject: EXCEPTION-FILE-N function
notes: Re-verified independently, not inherited. I rendered printed folio 846 (PDF page 876) myself with scripts/render-spec-page.py: the format is `FUNCTION EXCEPTION-FILE-N [(argument-1)]` with FUNCTION and EXCEPTION-FILE-N underlined and the parenthesized argument bracketed — the transcription is faithful, no OCR over-restriction, and `python scripts/spec/cite.py --check 15.29.2` matches it. Grammar: `functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (LPAREN functionArgList? RPAREN)?` admits both shapes. Ran every shape against the built CLI: 0 args -> `00`; empty parens `FUNCTION EXCEPTION-FILE-N()` -> `00` (the ISO §8.4.3.2.3 SR6 NOTE's `FUNCTION RANDOM ()` shape, validated with cite.py — not a §15.29.2 over-acceptance); 1 arg -> accepted; a SPACE before the left parenthesis (`FUNCTION EXCEPTION-FILE-N (INF)`) still binds as the argument form, per SR6; 2 args rejected `COBOLNET1504: FUNCTION EXCEPTION-FILE-N takes 0..1 argument(s); 2 given (ISO 15.3)`. The bracketed argument is correctly introduction-gated at 2023 (`COBOLNET0900 ... requires COBOL-2023 (targeting COBOL-2014)` observed at --std 2014) per Annex E.3.3 item 26 (cite.py-checked); the whole function is gated below 2002 by COBOLNET1502 (tests/conformance/negative/exception_file_n_below_2002.cob, verified on disk). Editions are the national-function window (national data and the -N exception twins are ISO/IEC 1989:2002 additions), NOT read off the IntrinsicCatalog row. COVERAGE GAP (does not change the verdict): the cited case exercises only the ZERO-argument shape; the one-argument shape — the only thing 2023 added to this format — has no spec-derived case for EXCEPTION-FILE-N (tests/conformance/2023/exception_file_arg.cob covers the alphanumeric sibling only). ADJACENT, OUT OF SCOPE FOR THIS RULE: reference modification of a function-identifier does not parse at all (`FUNCTION EXCEPTION-FILE-N(INF)(1:1)` and even `FUNCTION UPPER-CASE(WS-A)(1:2)` both give `COBOL0001: no viable alternative at input '('`), although ISO §8.4.3.3.3 SR2 permits it for an alphanumeric, boolean, or national function and EXCEPTION-FILE-N is national (§15.29.1). That is a general §8.4.3.3 grammar row, not a §15.29.2 format defect.

subject: EXCEPTION-LOCATION function
notes:
DOWNGRADED from CONFORMS. Re-verified independently: I rendered the printed folio 848 (scripts/render-spec-page.py 878) myself - the format is exactly two underlined words, FUNCTION EXCEPTION-LOCATION, no argument list, no brackets, so the transcription is faithful; `functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (LPAREN functionArgList? RPAREN)?` accepts the bare form; `FUNCTION EXCEPTION-LOCATION ()` (the SS8.4.3.2 SR6 NOTE shape, admitted by SS8.4.3.2.2 where the whole parenthesized list is optional) runs and yields the location; `FUNCTION EXCEPTION-LOCATION (1)` is rejected with COBOLNET1504; `--std 85` is rejected with COBOLNET1502 and `--std 2002` accepts.

THE UNVERIFIED HALF, NOW MEASURED AND FAILING - the SS8.4.3.2 SR2 keyword-OMITTED reference form. SR2: 'If intrinsic-function-name-1 or the ALL phrase is specified in the REPOSITORY paragraph ... the word FUNCTION may be omitted from the function-identifier.' Under `REPOSITORY. FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC.` the reference `EXCEPTION-LOCATION` (no FUNCTION, no parentheses - the function takes zero arguments, so there is no argument list to write) COMPILES CLEAN and then dies at run time. Ran (E:/Temp/claude/E--CobolSharp/40a0808e-7312-48f6-807b-5112b1d817cf/scratchpad/phaseb3/ref/f2.cob):
       >>TURN EC-USER CHECKING ON WITH LOCATION
       IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. REFF2.
       ENVIRONMENT DIVISION.
       CONFIGURATION SECTION.
       REPOSITORY.
           FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN-PARA.
           RAISE EXCEPTION EC-USER-L.
           DISPLAY "L=[" EXCEPTION-LOCATION "]".
           STOP RUN.
EXPECTED 'L=[REFF2; MAIN-PARA; 10]'; ACTUAL no diagnostic at compile time, then `NotImplementedCobolFeatureException: reference 'EXCEPTION-LOCATION'` at run time. ROOT CAUSE (read, not inferred): IntrinsicBinder.KeywordOmittedFunction returns null unless `suffixes.Length != 1 || suffixes[0].subscriptPart() is not { } sp` fails - i.e. it requires a PARENTHESIZED argument list to recognise a keyword-omitted function at all, so a ZERO-ARGUMENT intrinsic can never route through it and falls through to an unresolved data reference. This is a PATTERN, not a one-off: the same file f4.cob shows `LENGTH ("ABC")` works (A=[3]) while `CURRENT-DATE` under the same FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC dies identically - every zero-argument intrinsic (CURRENT-DATE, WHEN-COMPILED, RANDOM, E, PI, EXCEPTION-STATUS, EXCEPTION-STATEMENT, EXCEPTION-LOCATION/-N, EXCEPTION-FILE/-N) is affected. PARTIAL rather than DIVERGES because SS15.30.2's own transcribed format (FUNCTION required, no arguments) IS implemented correctly - the failure is in SS8.4.3.2 SR2's alternative reference form, which is a cross-cutting binder defect, but it silently mis-compiles legal COBOL-2002 written against THIS function's format, so the row must not close.

Editions derived from the spec, NOT from the IntrinsicCatalog row: the whole last-exception-status facility that this function interrogates (>>TURN SS7.3.25, the run-unit last exception status SS14.6.13.1.1, and the EXCEPTION-* interrogation family) is a COBOL-2002 addition and is absent from the COBOL-85 + 1989 Intrinsic Function Amendment repertoire; SS15.30 is untouched by the 2023 delta annex (E.3.3 changes only EXCEPTION-FILE item 25 and EXCEPTION-FILE-N item 26), so 2002/2014/2023 all carry the same format.

test-needed beyond the cited test (which exists on disk, tests/Cobol.Net.Tests.Conformance/ExceptionConditionConformanceTests.cs line 194, and is spec-derived - it only proves the bare format parses): a negative-arity case (FUNCTION EXCEPTION-LOCATION(1) -> COBOLNET1504), a tests/conformance/negative/ below-2002 edition-window case (its EXCEPTION-FILE-N twin has one, exception_file_n_below_2002.cob; EXCEPTION-LOCATION has none), and a FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC keyword-omitted case.

subject: EXCEPTION-LOCATION-N function
notes:
OVERTURNS the prior CONFORMS. Citations validated: cite.py --check 15.31.2 "FUNCTION" -> OK (General format); 8.4.3.2.3 "the word FUNCTION may be omitted from the function-identifier" -> OK SR2; 8.4.3.2.3 "If a function's definition permits arguments and a left parenthesis immediately follows" -> OK SR6; 8.4.3.3.3 "it shall reference an alphanumeric, boolean, or national function" -> OK SR2.

The HAPPY PATH is right and I re-ran it: bare `FUNCTION EXCEPTION-LOCATION-N` compiles and runs at --std 2002/2014/2023; one argument is rejected COBOLNET1504 "takes 0 argument(s); 1 given (ISO 15.3)"; --std 85 is rejected COBOLNET1502. But the format's DEFINING property -- that it carries NO argument list -- has two consequences the compiler gets wrong, both RUN.

(1) 8.4.3.2.3 SR2: with the name (or the ALL phrase) in the REPOSITORY paragraph, "the word FUNCTION may be omitted from the function-identifier". RAN (cobol.exe --run):
       IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. RELN04.
       ENVIRONMENT DIVISION.
       CONFIGURATION SECTION.
       REPOSITORY.
           FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           DISPLAY "X=[" EXCEPTION-LOCATION-N "]".
           STOP RUN.
Got   NO compile diagnostic, then at run time: NotImplementedCobolFeatureException "a COBOL feature that is not yet implemented was reached at run time: reference 'EXCEPTION-LOCATION-N'".
Spec  X=[ ] (the 15.31.3 r1 one national space).
Identical with the NAMED specifier `FUNCTION EXCEPTION-LOCATION-N INTRINSIC.` (RELN07). ROOT CAUSE, read from code: IntrinsicBinder.KeywordOmittedFunction bails at `if (suffixes.Length != 1 || suffixes[0].subscriptPart() is not { } sp) return null;` -- it recognises the keyword-omitted form ONLY in the shape `name(args)`. A function whose GENERAL FORMAT has no argument list can therefore NEVER be written without the word FUNCTION; the bare word stays a data reference and falls through to a runtime NotImplemented. Proof it is the zero-argument shape and not REPOSITORY support in general: in the SAME REPOSITORY ALL INTRINSIC unit `UPPER-CASE("abc")` -> U=[ABC] and `LENGTH("abcd")` -> L=[4] both work.

(2) 8.4.3.2.3 SR6 treats a following left parenthesis as an argument list only "If a function's definition permits arguments". 15.31.2 permits none, so a `(` after the name can only be a REFERENCE MODIFIER -- which 8.4.3.3.3 SR2 expressly allows here ("If identifier-1 is a function-identifier, it shall reference an alphanumeric, boolean, or national function"; 15.31.1: "The type of the function is national"). RAN:
           MOVE FUNCTION EXCEPTION-LOCATION-N (1:1) TO N2.
Got   error COBOL0001: no viable alternative at input '(' / unexpected '('.
Spec  accepted; the unique data item is national position 1.
ROOT CAUSE: `functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (LPAREN functionArgList? RPAREN)?` has no reference-modifier alternative at all.

SIBLING SWEEP (both defects are patterns, both confirmed by run): (1) breaks EVERY zero-argument intrinsic under REPOSITORY -- `CURRENT-DATE` bare gives the same runtime NotImplemented, and the same holds for EXCEPTION-LOCATION / EXCEPTION-STATEMENT / EXCEPTION-STATUS / EXCEPTION-FILE / EXCEPTION-FILE-N / E / PI / RANDOM / WHEN-COMPILED. (2) breaks reference modification of EVERY function-identifier -- `FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE (1:8)` and `FUNCTION UPPER-CASE("abcdef") (2:3)` are both COBOL0001, and `FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE (1:8)` is one of the most common idioms in real COBOL.

NOT a divergence: `FUNCTION EXCEPTION-LOCATION-N ()` is accepted; the 8.4.3.2.2 diagram's ellipsis sits inside the parentheses over a BRACKETED item, and SR6's NOTE writes `FUNCTION MAX (FUNCTION RANDOM () A B)`, so an empty list is derivable -- a leniency at worst.

Editions derived independently of the catalog row: 8.11 Intrinsic function names lists EXCEPTION-LOCATION-N; the exception-condition facility (TURN directive, RAISE, the last exception status) and class national are both COBOL-2002 introductions; no Annex E entry adds or changes EXCEPTION-LOCATION-N for 2014 or 2023 (E.3.3 item 26 touches only EXCEPTION-FILE-N's optional argument). Both cited fixtures verified present on disk and both name EXCEPTION-LOCATION-N.

subject: EXCEPTION-STATEMENT function
notes: OVERTURNED CONFORMS -> PARTIAL. Independently re-verified the half the adjudicator got right, then found the half they did not test. VERIFIED: I re-extracted the canonical PDF myself (pypdf, page index 881 = printed page 852) and the printed 15.32.2 carries exactly the two words `FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATEMENT` -- nothing lost toward false restriction, so the OCR at specs/ISO_COBOL.md 15.32.2 is faithful. Lexing: NAME_BODY (CobolLexer.g4) matches the 19-char EXCEPTION-STATEMENT and beats the 9-char EXCEPTION keyword by maximal munch, so it reaches `functionName : IDENTIFIER`. Arity: catalog row is Fixed 0..0, so IntrinsicBinder COBOLNET1504 rejects an argument list. Edition window re-derived from the SPEC, not the catalog row: 15.32 depends on the last exception status (14.6.13.1.1) and the 7.3.25 TURN directive, both COBOL-2002; EXCEPTION-STATEMENT is not among the 1989 Intrinsic Function amendment functions; `grep EXCEPTION-STATEMENT specs/ISO_COBOL.md` returns NO Annex E and NO Annex F hit, so it is neither new-in-2023 nor archaic -> 2002,2014,2023 stands. WHAT THE ADJUDICATOR MISSED -- the claim 'NO legal shape of this format is rejected' is FALSE. 8.4.3.1.2 Format 1 (cite.py --check 8.4.3.1.2 'Format 1 (function-identifier)' -> OK) makes a function-identifier an IDENTIFIER, and 8.4.3.2.3 SR1 (--check OK) bars it only from a RECEIVING operand, so EVERY identifier-N SENDING position admits `FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATEMENT`. The grammar routes `functionCall` from only four places (CobolExpressions.g4 primaryExpression, CobolParserCore.g4 displayStatement and moveSendingOperand, CobolIO.g4 strUnstrSender). The FROM phrases of WRITE / REWRITE / RELEASE are `FROM (dataReference | literal)` with no functionCall alternative, and FUNCTION is a lexer keyword absent from cobolWord, so `WRITE REC FROM FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATEMENT` is a hard PARSE ERROR on legal source -- 14.9.51.4 GR5a (--check 14.9.51.4 'MOVE identifier-1 TO record-name-1' -> OK) makes that identifier-1 a MOVE SENDING operand. The project's own CobolIO.g4 DA4 comment states the principle ('every identifier-N SENDING position admits one') and then applied it to STRING/UNSTRING only. Filed under defects. The cited test is spec-derived but exercises the format in the DISPLAY position only; there is no negative test on the argument-list rejection and none on the FROM positions.

subject: EXCEPTION-STATUS function
notes:
REFUTE PASS — VERDICT CONFIRMED at PARTIAL, but every load-bearing claim was RE-RUN, not inherited, and four candidate additional defects were chased and THREE of them RETRACTED. Citations re-validated by me: cite.py --check 15.33.2 "<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>EXCEPTION-STATUS</u>" -> OK (General format); 15.33.1 "The type of the function is alphanumeric." -> OK; 8.4.3.2.3 "the word FUNCTION may be omitted from the function-identifier" -> OK (SR2); 15.2 "the function so described may be used anywhere a sending data item of that class and category may be specified" -> OK.

RE-REPRODUCED, ALL FOUR (prebuilt Debug cobol.exe, --std 2023, no rebuild): (1) INSPECT FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATUS TALLYING ... -> COBOL0001 no viable alternative at input 'FUNCTION'; (2) WRITE F-REC FROM FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATUS -> COBOL0001; (3) INITIALIZE WS-D REPLACING ALPHANUMERIC DATA BY FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATUS -> COBOL0001; (4) under REPOSITORY. FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC., INSPECT EXCEPTION-STATUS TALLYING WS-N FOR ALL "-" compiles with NO diagnostic then dies with NotImplementedCobolFeatureException: INSPECT of unresolvable item 'EXCEPTION-STATUS'. The four stand.

FOUR NEW LEADS I CHASED; THREE RETRACTED — recorded so nobody re-files them. (a) CALL "SUBX" USING BY CONTENT FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATUS is rejected (COBOL0001) — RETRACTED as a defect: that is CALL FORMAT 1, and 14.9.4.3 SR3 (validated: cite.py --check 14.9.4.3 "Identifier-2 shall reference an address-identifier or a data item defined in the file, working-storage, local-storage, or linkage section." -> OK) restricts identifier-2 to a DATA ITEM IN A SECTION, which a function-identifier is not, so the rejection is CORRECT. Format 2 (program-prototype) uses identifier-4, which SR17 only makes a sending operand with no section restriction and SR20 discusses as possibly non-receiving — a function-identifier there is arguably legal and I did NOT verify it; that is an open lead, not a finding. (b) SR2 keyword-omitted with a NAMED repository entry (REPOSITORY. FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATUS INTRINSIC. + bare EXCEPTION-STATUS) WORKS — no gap beyond ALL INTRINSIC. (c) EXCEPTION-STATUS is NOT in the §8.9 reserved-word list (that list carries EXCEPTION and EXCEPTION-OBJECT only; EXCEPTION-STATUS/-FILE/-LOCATION/-STATEMENT appear only in the §8.11 intrinsic-function-name list), so `01 EXCEPTION-STATUS PIC X(5)` alongside `FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATUS` must both work — I ran it and BOTH work (D=[HELLO] / F=[31 spaces]). (d) The empty-parenthesis leniency FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATUS () is CONFORMING, not laxity — I read the printed §8.4.3.2.2 diagram in the transcription (the bracketed argument-1/OMITTED item sits INSIDE the parenthesized group, and the figure note says "the whole parenthesized argument list is optional"), and the §8.4.3.2.3 SR6 NOTE literally writes `FUNCTION MAX (FUNCTION RANDOM () A B)`.

EDITION WINDOW RE-DERIVED FROM THE SPEC, NOT FROM THE CATALOG ROW: §8.11 lists EXCEPTION-STATUS; Annex E.3.3's 2023 intrinsic delta touches items 25/26 = EXCEPTION-FILE and EXCEPTION-FILE-N ONLY, never §15.33; the interrogated facility (14.6.13.1.1 last exception status, 7.3.25 TURN, RAISE) is 2002. I then ran the gate myself: --std 85 -> error COBOLNET1502 "FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATUS was introduced by ISO/IEC 1989:2002 (15)"; --std 2002/2014/2023 all compile and run identically. Corroboration only.

WHY STILL PARTIAL AND NOT DIVERGES: 15.33.2's own transcribed format (FUNCTION required, no argument list) is implemented correctly at every edition in the window, and wherever the reference binds the value is right. What fails is the 8.4.3.1.2-Format-1 REACH of a function-identifier into three statement-operand slots that reject it outright plus one that silently mis-compiles it — a channel gap common to EVERY function (all four reproduce identically with FUNCTION UPPER-CASE), not a contradiction of THIS format.

test-ref: the ONE cited test is genuinely spec-derived (AssertSpec, expected value derived from §14.6.13.1.4 + 15.33.3; the EC model has no legacy oracle), but it pins only that the BARE form parses, binds and runs. Nothing pins the format's reach. test-needed: a negative-arity case (FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATUS(x) -> COBOLNET1504), a tests/conformance below-2002 negative (EXCEPTION-FILE-N has exception_file_n_below_2002.cob; EXCEPTION-STATUS has none), a FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC keyword-omitted case, a named-REPOSITORY keyword-omitted case, and a result-ref-mod case.

subject: EXP function
notes: OVERTURNED from CONFORMS. The adjudicator read the PARSER grammar and concluded "NO legal written form of this general format is rejected". The LEXER contradicts it, and no parser rule can see the problem. A SIGNED FLOATING-POINT NUMERIC LITERAL argument is mis-tokenized inside a FUNCTION-argument region. §8.3.3.3.3 r2 (--check OK): "The literal to the left of the 'E' represents the significand. It may be signed and shall include a decimal point." — the sign is PART of the literal. §8.3.3.3.1 (--check OK) makes it class and category NUMERIC; §8.4.3.2.3 SR8 (--check OK) admits "a literal" as argument-1; §15.3 type 10 (--check OK) admits an arithmetic expression, and §8.8.1.1 (--check OK) makes a numeric literal one; §15.34.3 r1 admits class numeric. So `FUNCTION EXP(-1.5E3)` is legal COBOL. MECHANISM: `FLOATLIT : ( [0-9]+ '.' [0-9]* | '.' [0-9]+ ) 'E' [-+]? [0-9]+` carries NO leading sign, so it cannot start at '-'. In an argument region `SignedLiteralCanStart()` is true (its accepted predecessors include '(' literally, and the '(' after a function name pushes true on `_fnParenStack`), so `FN_SIGNED_DECIMALLIT : {SignedLiteralCanStart()}? [+-] DEC_BODY` matches "-1.5" (4 chars) — longer than MINUS (1) or FN_SIGNED_INTEGERLIT "-1" (2) — and the orphaned "E3" lexes as IDENTIFIER via NAME_BODY. `functionArgList : functionArgument (FNARG_SEPARATOR? functionArgument)*` is plain juxtaposition, so the parser sees TWO arguments and IntrinsicBinder rejects with COBOLNET1504 "FUNCTION EXP takes 1 argument(s); 2 given (ISO §15.3)". BOTH reference forms are hit: the keyword-omitted form re-lexes the verbatim captured text through `PrimeFunctionArgs`, and `SignedLiteralCanStart()` returns true unconditionally at `InputStream.Index == 0`, so `EXP(-1.5E3)` under `REPOSITORY. FUNCTION EXP INTRINSIC.` fails identically. The UNSIGNED form `FUNCTION EXP(1.5E3)` is fine (FLOATLIT wins by longest match), which is exactly why output-sampling misses this. ⚠ The lexer's own SIGNED_DECIMALLIT ordering comment documents this precise orphaned-tail failure for "-15.6" and the FLOATLIT case was never swept — one rule ("a sign adjacent to a literal is part of the literal") written down for two of the three literal shapes. NO test in the tree exercises a float literal as a function argument: tests/conformance/2002/float_literal.cob only does `MOVE -1.5E3 TO WS-A`, where the predicate is false and MINUS+FLOATLIT parses correctly. Everything else the adjudicator verified I re-confirmed and it holds: EXP is not a lexer token and not §8.9-reserved, so it reaches `functionName : IDENTIFIER`; `functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (LPAREN functionArgList? RPAREN)? refModPart*` accepts the parenthesized list; exactly-one-argument is a bind-time check (catalog MinArgs=MaxArgs=1, COBOLNET1504); `FUNCTION EXP(ZERO)` parses because ZeroTokenRewriter's PrecedingArithmeticContext contains LPAREN (§8.8.1.1 makes the figurative constant ZERO an arithmetic expression). EDITION CAVEAT (instruction 4): 2014 and 2023 are supportable from the oracle (EXP appears in §8.11 and Table 21 of the 2023 text and is absent from Annex E's new-function list), but the 2002 LOWER BOUND is NOT derivable from specs/ISO_COBOL.md — it rests on the 1985/Amd.1:1992 42-function list, which is not in the oracle and which docs/VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE.md (2014→2023 only) does not carry either. Recorded as inherited, not as verified.

subject: EXP10 function
notes:
⛔ OVERTURNED: CONFORMS -> PARTIAL. The first pass verified the ACCEPT half and declared the row closed; the REJECT half does not hold, and the proof is two lines apart in the same method.

FORMAT re-validated: --check 15.35.2 "FUNCTION" -> OK §15.35.2, text `<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>EXP10</u> ( argument-1 )`. Both words underlined = required; the parenthesised group is unbracketed = required; exactly one argument-1, which §15.3 item 10 makes an arithmetic expression or a numeric data item.

WHAT DOES HOLD (re-derived, not inherited). EXP10 is a §8.11 INTRINSIC-FUNCTION-NAME and is absent from the §8.9 reserved list, so it lexes IDENTIFIER and `functionName : IDENTIFIER | ...` takes it. CobolLexer's OnDefaultLParen was read directly: for `FUNCTION EXP10 (` the first branch is skipped because PreviousIsFunctionName() is true, and `_fnParenStack.Add(true)` opens a real argument region, so arguments parse as expressions rather than subscripts; a nested `A(1)` still pushes SUBSCRIPT because _prevNonWsTokenType is no longer FUNCTION. I additionally checked an operand the first pass did not: §8.8.1.1 explicitly admits the FIGURATIVE CONSTANT ZERO as an arithmetic expression, and `FUNCTION EXP10(ZERO)` does work — ZeroTokenRewriter rewrites ZERO to ZERO_ARITH because the FOLLOWING token is RPAREN (FollowingArithmeticContext). Arity is enforced outside the grammar as COBOLNET1504 for the bare name, for `()`, and for two or more arguments; ref-modifying the numeric result is COBOLNET1629, and a bare `(1:2)` after the name is COBOLNET1543 (§8.4.3.2.3 SR6). No false rejection of a legal §15.35.2 form was found.

⛔ WHAT DOES NOT HOLD — A NON-FORMAT TOKEN SEQUENCE COMPILES CLEAN AND THROWS AT RUN TIME. The grammar's `functionArgument : fnArgPhraseWord | OMITTED | nonNumericLiteral | arithmeticExpression` is a deliberate SUPERSET whose narrowing is the binder's job (the grammar comment says so). IntrinsicBinder.BindArgOperand narrows only half of it:
    if (a.OMITTED() is not null) { ctx.Edition.Error("COBOLNET1544", ...); return new BoundOperandError(...); }
    if (a.fnArgPhraseWord() is { } kw)
        return new BoundOperandError($"intrinsic argument '{kw.GetText()}'");   // NO diagnostic
The OMITTED arm reports; the phrase-word arm does not. `fnArgPhraseWord` is LEADING | TRAILING | LAST | FIRST | ANY | START | AFTER | ALPHANUMERIC | NATIONAL — every one of them verified present in the spec's own §8.9 RESERVED-word list, so none can be a data-name and none is a numeric literal; none can be argument-1 under §15.3 item 10, and §15.35.2's format admits nothing else. ANTLR takes alternative 1 (LEADING is absent from cobolWord, so the arithmeticExpression alternative cannot even match it). Result: `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION EXP10(LEADING).` parses, binds, passes the arity check with 1 argument, is skipped by the class screen (the AR row), and emits `NotImplemented.Value<long>("intrinsic argument 'LEADING'")` — the compile SUCCEEDS with zero diagnostics and the program throws NotImplementedCobolFeatureException at RUN TIME. That is exactly PB7's failure shape, and it is why an output-sampling pass cannot see it.

WHY THAT IS A CONFORMANCE DEFECT AND NOT MERE LATENESS: --check 4.2.2 "This warning mechanism shall indicate violations of such rules." -> OK §4.2.2. The word class of a function argument is a static property of the source and is syntactically distinguishable — the implementor's-discretion sentence that closes §4.2.2 is a judgement WE already made when PB1 landed COBOLNET1627 for the neighbouring class rule, so the obligation applies. The method's own doc comment claims "an unconsumed phrase word is a loud named operand — never a silent skip (§1.4)", but §1.4 loudness is RUN-TIME loudness; the OMITTED neighbour proves the compile-time report was the intent.

A smaller sibling on the same path: NonNumericOperand falls back to `new BoundOperandError($"literal argument ...")` when the literal mapping returns null, also with no diagnostic.

So the format's accept half CONFORMS and its reject half is incomplete -> PARTIAL, per the rule that a two-halved rule with one half verified is never CONFORMS. Editions and the COBOLNET1502 gate at --std 85 are as in the AR row (derived from §8.11 + Annex E/F + the 1989 amendment's 42-function list, not from IntrinsicCatalog).

NO SPEC-DERIVED TEST — the only source compiling the form is IntrinsicSpecTests#ExpAndExp10, disqualified as a captured-output characterization by its own class header. test-ref left empty.

subject: FACTORIAL function
notes:
OVERTURNED CONFORMS -> PARTIAL. Re-validated independently: `cite.py --check 15.36.2` renders `<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>FACTORIAL</u> ( argument-1 )` — both words underlined, parens and argument-1 unbracketed, no optional/repeated element. The adjudicator's GRAMMAR reading is CONFIRMED by re-reading: `functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (LPAREN functionArgList? RPAREN)? refModPart* | reservedIntrinsicArgFn subscriptPart refModPart* | RANDOM subscriptPart? refModPart*`; `functionName : IDENTIFIER | DISPLAY | LENGTH | MERGE | NATIONAL | BIT | RANDOM | SIGN | SORT | SUM` — FACTORIAL is not in that keyword list and no FACTORIAL token exists, so it lexes IDENTIFIER and alternative 1 matches; `functionArgument : fnArgPhraseWord | OMITTED | nonNumericLiteral | arithmeticExpression`, so the §15.3 item 6 shape (`--check 15.3` OK: 'An arithmetic expression that will always result in an integer value or an integer data item shall be specified.') is admitted syntactically; the requiredness of the parens is enforced at `BindIntrinsicCore` by `args.Count < sig.MinArgs` => COBOLNET1504 against the catalog Fixed 1,1 row; the keyword-omitted route (§8.4.3.2.3) reaches `BindIntrinsicCore` via `KeywordOmittedFunction`'s one-suffix arm.

It recorded that TWO of the shapes this very format admits are accepted by the grammar and then FAIL IN THE BACKEND with a raw Roslyn error, then declined to move the verdict on the ground that those are 'emitter defects adjudicated under AR/RV'. That partition does not survive contact with the user-visible fact: `FUNCTION FACTORIAL ( argument-1 )` where argument-1 is (a) an arithmetic expression under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD / STANDARD-DECIMAL, or (b) an integer-typed nested function under a float receiver, DOES NOT COMPILE. (b) `RenderNum` line `if (AnyRealArgument(ic)) return RenderFloat(ic, RealMethod(sig.RuntimeMethod));` maps Factorial -> FactorialReal, and grep of CobolIntrinsics.RealArgs.cs for `public static (double|long) \w+Real\(` lists AbsReal SignOfReal FloorReal TruncateReal FractionPartReal ModReal RemReal MaxReal MinReal SumReal RangeReal MedianReal MidrangeReal MeanReal OrdMaxReal OrdMinReal CombinedDatetimeReal — no FactorialReal. A general format whose admitted operand shapes the compiler cannot build is supported in part, not in full.
SECOND GROUND: nothing was executed (read-only review) and there is NO spec-derived test on any edge of this format — not the bare name, not the empty parens, not the two-argument form, not the keyword-omitted form, not the §8.4.3.3.3 SR2 ref-mod rejection. notes: CONFIRMED PARTIAL, reasoning re-derived rather than inherited. EDITION WINDOW RE-DERIVED FROM THE SPEC, NOT THE CATALOG ROW: Annex E.3.3 item 27 ('FUNCTION FIND-STRING. GRAMMAR ACCEPTS EVERY LEGAL FORM, verified by reading the rules: `functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (LPAREN functionArgList? RPAREN)? refModPart*`; `functionArgument : fnArgPhraseWord | OMITTED | nonNumericLiteral | arithmeticExpression`; `fnArgPhraseWord` carries LEADING/TRAILING/LAST/FIRST/ANY/START/AFTER/ALPHANUMERIC/NATIONAL. A subscripted or reference-modified argument-1 is NOT mis-eaten as a phrase word — KeywordWordOf→SoleDataReference requires `dataReferenceSuffix().Length == 0`. (b) NEW, MISSED BY THE ADJUDICATOR: the format's argument-1/argument-2 slots admit a FIGURATIVE CONSTANT — §8.3.3.6.3 SR1 (cite.py OK) 'A figurative constant may be used whenever "literal" appears in a format or when a rule allows it', and §15.37.3 r1/r2 say 'data item or literal'. (c) The keyword-omitted reference form (REPOSITORY … FUNCTION FIND-STRING INTRINSIC, then `FIND-STRING(H N START AFTER 1)`) routes through the D2 ReparseArgs→functionArgListFragment path, which reuses the same functionArgList so it should work — but NO test exercises it for this function and I ran none.

subject: FORMATTED-CURRENT-DATE function
notes: CONFIRMED PARTIAL, with the attribution of the unenforced half made precise. Citation validated: `cite.py --check 15.38.2 "FUNCTION"` -> OK; the printed format is `<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>FORMATTED-CURRENT-DATE</u> ( argument-1 )` -- both words underlined (required), the parenthesised part NOT bracketed, so the parentheses and the single argument are required and there is no zero-argument form (contrast 15.75.2 RANDOM, whose parenthesised part IS bracketed -- and the grammar's `RANDOM subscriptPart? refModPart*` alternative shows the compiler already models that difference). ACCEPT SIDE, verified from the grammar SOURCE rather than by sampling: `functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (LPAREN functionArgList? RPAREN)? refModPart*`; `functionName : IDENTIFIER | DISPLAY | LENGTH | MERGE | NATIONAL | BIT | RANDOM | SIGN | SORT | SUM` -- FORMATTED-CURRENT-DATE arrives through IDENTIFIER, and I confirmed against the spec's 8.11 list (it is an intrinsic-function name, NOT an 8.9 reserved word), so no lexer special case is needed or missing. `functionArgument` admits `nonNumericLiteral` (STRINGLIT / NATLIT / BOOLLIT / HEXLIT / concatenationExpression / figurativeConstant) as well as arithmeticExpression, so NO legal argument spelling is rejected. The grammar is a deliberate superset narrowed by IntrinsicArity.Fixed 1,1 -> COBOLNET1504 for the 0- and 2-argument forms and for the bare no-parenthesis form. UNENFORCED HALF -- the required word FUNCTION (8.4.3.2.3 SR2, `cite.py --check 8.4.3.2.3 "the word FUNCTION is required"` -> OK). CORRECTED ATTRIBUTION, and this is sharper than 'generic unresolved-reference staging': the diagnostic ALREADY EXISTS. IntrinsicBinder.BindIntrinsic raises COBOLNET1543 with the exact SR2 citation when the word is omitted -- but only on the `reservedIntrinsicArgFn`/RANDOM grammar alternative, i.e. only for the three 8.9-and-8.11 words SIGN, SUM, RANDOM. For every OTHER intrinsic name the omitted form arrives as a dataReference, and IntrinsicBinder.KeywordOmittedFunction returns null whenever `!(ctx.Data.RepositoryAllIntrinsic || ctx.Data.RepositoryIntrinsics.Contains(name))`, after which ExpressionBinder falls through to `ctx.Refs.Resolve(dref)` and, failing, to `new BoundOperandError(RefFailure(dref))` -- compiles clean, exit 0, and throws NotImplementedCobolFeatureException at run time. So ONE rule is written in ONE place and applied to 3 of the ~83 catalogued functions; the other ~80, this one included, fail silently. That is a structural gap, not a per-function one, and it is the shape the fix must take. Already recorded on FMT-15.17.2 (COMBINED-DATETIME) in tests/version-matrix/traceability-inventory.json -- recorded here, not re-discovered. A general format whose required word is unenforced cannot read CONFORMS. TEST: tests/conformance/2014/formatted_datetime.cob (read on disk with its .out) writes the printed general format at `FUNCTION FORMATTED-CURRENT-DATE("YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss")` and the golden pins FCD=+000000000; the fixture's other expectations are spec-derived (TF1/TF2 are 15.92.4's own worked per-digit narrowing examples, 6 and 2). It is genuine evidence that the printed form is ACCEPTED at 2014 -- one spelling only, and it says nothing about the arity rejections or the missing-FUNCTION rejection. EDITIONS: as for AR-15.38.3-1.

subject: FORMATTED-TIME function
notes: OVERTURNED (CONFORMS -> PARTIAL). The adjudicator's claim "I could construct no legal shape of this general format the grammar rejects" is FALSE; two legal shapes of argument-1 are rejected, and both were found by READING the lexer/binder rather than sampling. (1) HEXADECIMAL-NATIONAL LITERAL. Spec (cite-verified §15.41.3 r1 "Argument-1 shall be a national or alphanumeric literal"; §8.3.3.5.2 Format 2 gives the national literal's second form NX"…" / NX'…', and §8.3.3.5.3 SR1/SR2 apply to ALL FORMATS). CobolLexer.g4 has NO NX rule and says so in its own comment on the NATLIT line: "NX\"…\" (hex national) is deferred" (the same line defers BX"…"). `FUNCTION FORMATTED-TIME(NX"00680068006D006D00730073", 45296)` therefore does not lex as one national literal: `NX` takes the IDENTIFIER rule and `"0068…"` the STRINGLIT rule, and because argument separation inside a function-argument region is plain juxtaposition (functionArgList : functionArgument (FNARG_SEPARATOR? functionArgument)*) the single literal SILENTLY becomes TWO arguments — a 3-argument call whose argument-1 is an unresolvable data reference. Legal COBOL, misparsed and then rejected. (2) CONSTANT-NAME ARGUMENT. §13.10.1 "A constant may be used in place of a literal", §13.10.4 GR1 "the effect of specifying constant-name-1 in other than this entry is as if literal-1 … were written where constant-name-1 is written", §8.4.3.2.3 SR8 "Argument-1 shall be an identifier, a literal, a boolean expression, or an arithmetic expression" (all cite-verified). `01 TFMT CONSTANT AS "hh:mm:ss".` + `FUNCTION FORMATTED-TIME(TFMT, 45296)` PARSES (dataReference inside arithmeticExpression) but dies at bind — see AR-15.41.3-1. Everything the adjudicator verified positively still holds (FUNCTION + IDENTIFIER name slot, space/comma/semicolon separation, STRINGLIT/NATLIT/HEXLIT/concatenation argument-1, SIGNED_INTEGERLIT argument-3, refModPart* for PB8, arity 2..3 at bind). One correction to its reasoning: the figurative ZERO reaches argument-2 by TWO different routes depending on position — ZeroTokenRewriter rewrites ZERO to ZERO_ARITH only when the adjacent token is an arithmetic operator or a paren, so `FORMATTED-TIME("hh:mm:ss", ZERO)` binds as a numeric 0 while `FORMATTED-TIME("hhmmss+hhmm", ZERO, 120)` (ZERO between two FNARG_SEPARATORs) binds as BoundFigurative('Z'); both happen to render 0, so this is noted, not charged.

subject: FRACTION-PART function
notes: OVERTURNED CONFORMS -> PARTIAL. The prior pass's structural readings all RE-VERIFIED and are correct as far as they go: cite.py --check 15.42.2 "FUNCTION" -> OK (General format, both words underlined, one parenthesised argument, no optional element); `functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (LPAREN functionArgList? RPAREN)? refModPart*` is a deliberate superset; IntrinsicCatalog gives MinArgs=MaxArgs=1 so bare `FUNCTION FRACTION-PART`, `()` and `(A B)` all take COBOLNET1504 in BindIntrinsicCore; the D8 window gate fires COBOLNET1502 below --std 2002; and I confirmed the keyword-omitted route is NOT an over-accept -- KeywordOmittedFunction gates on `(ctx.Data.RepositoryAllIntrinsic || ctx.Data.RepositoryIntrinsics.Contains(name)) && IntrinsicCatalog.TryGet(name, out _)`, so `FRACTION-PART(A)` with no REPOSITORY stays a data reference (8.4.3.2.3 SR2 honoured). WHY IT IS STILL NOT CONFORMS -- THE PRIOR PASS'S OWN STATED BASIS IS FALSE. It closed the row on "Net user-visible surface = exactly the general format". It is not. The format writes `( argument-1 )`, 15.6 Table 21 types that position `Num1`, and 15.3 type 10 (cite.py --check 15.3 "An arithmetic expression or a numeric data item shall be specified." -> OK, rule 10) makes an ARITHMETIC EXPRESSION a licensed occupant of that position. Under `ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD` / `STANDARD-DECIMAL` that shape does not compile: NumericRenderer.CombineCore returns `NumX(CobolDec.*(...), 0, Dec: true)` for every +,-,*,/ under a standard mode, IntrinsicRenderer.RenderNum's `case "FractionPart"` has no Dec arm, and `CobolIntrinsics.FractionPart` is `(Int128, int)` while CobolDec (a readonly record struct(Int128 Sig, int Exp)) declares NO conversion operators -- verified by reading both files -- so Roslyn emits CS1503 and the user sees "backend compilation failed" on source the general format admits. A format whose argument position rejects a legal argument shape has a broken acceptance half; per the costing rule (one half verified => PARTIAL) this is PARTIAL. It bites at EVERY edition in the window: ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD is 2002+ (DataBinder rejects it only at 2023) and STANDARD-DECIMAL is 2014+, and NumericRenderer.StandardDecimal covers both. TEST-REF SCOPE, STATED HONESTLY: pb2_float_argument_exact_family is a genuine spec-derived conformance fixture (header derives its expectations from 15.64.4/15.77.4/15.44/15.49 rule text, not from observation), but its ONE FRACTION-PART line is `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION FRACTION-PART(D)` with D and R BOTH COMP-2, golden line 7 = `0.5`. It proves the format parses in exactly one shape -- float argument, float receiver, positive value. It exercises no fixed-point argument, no arithmetic-expression argument, and no rejection at all; there is no negative fixture for the arity half and none for the COBOLNET1502 edition half. Diagnostic nit re-confirmed, not a conformance defect: `FUNCTION FRACTION-PART (1:2)` reports COBOLNET1504 rather than the 8.4.3.2.3 SR6 argument-list error because ResultRefMod short-circuits on BoundExprError -- illegal either way.

subject: HIGHEST-ALGEBRAIC function
notes: OVERTURNED CONFORMS → PARTIAL. What holds, re-verified independently: the transcribed format is a single unbracketed `FUNCTION HIGHEST-ALGEBRAIC ( argument-1 )` with both words underlined; HIGHEST-ALGEBRAIC is genuinely NOT a §8.9 reserved word (the printed list runs HEADING · HIGH-VALUE · HIGH-VALUES · I-O — no HIGHEST-ALGEBRAIC), so it lexes as IDENTIFIER; the grammar superset is closed by COBOLNET1504 (arity, IntrinsicBinder#BindIntrinsicCore) and the PB8 ref-mod arm; the D8 introduction gate DOES fire (IntrinsicBinder#BindIntrinsicCore raises COBOLNET1502 when sig.IntroducedIn > DialectLevel), so --std 85 rejects the reference. THREE THINGS THE ADJUDICATOR ASSERTED WITHOUT VERIFYING, and one of them is false. (1) ⛔ "Nothing LEGAL is turned away" IS FALSE. §8.5.2.12 enumerates the data items of category numeric and items 3/4/5 are A LINE-COUNTER · A LINAGE-COUNTER · A PAGE-COUNTER (mechanically checked). Those are legal argument-1 shapes under §15.43.3 r1, and ExpressionBinder binds all three to BoundLinageCounterRef / the RWCS-counter refs wrapped in a BoundComputedOperand (the FieldOperand arm returns `new BoundComputedOperand(new BoundLinageCounterRef(lcf))`), so BindAlgebraicFold's `args[0] is not BoundFieldOperand` guard rejects them with COBOLNET1516. `FUNCTION HIGHEST-ALGEBRAIC(LINAGE-COUNTER)` is conforming source and does not compile. (2) The §8.4.3.2.3 SR2 KEYWORD-OMITTED form is verified BY READING ONLY — IntrinsicBinder#KeywordOmittedFunction is gated `DialectLevel < 2002` and now admits zero-or-one suffix after PB7, so `HIGHEST-ALGEBRAIC(X)` under `REPOSITORY. FUNCTION HIGHEST-ALGEBRAIC INTRINSIC` should route — but NO test exercises it for this function, and PB7/PB9 are the standing proof that this exact path can compile clean and fail at run time. (3) The cited golden is spec-derived (its header cites §15.43/§15.58 + Annex D.32 and derives every value from the PICTURE), but it only compiles the FUNCTION-keyword form in two spacings at one edition; it pins no rejection and no keyword-omitted form. PARTIAL is the honest verdict: the format is right, the argument REGION admits less than §15.3 permits.

subject: INTEGER function
notes: OVERTURNED: PARTIAL → DIVERGES. Two things the prior pass got wrong. FIRST, the rejection is not one position but TWO. The reference is legal in a SUBSCRIPT — §8.4.2.3.2's subscript diagram admits arithmetic-expression-1; §8.8.1.1 admits 'an identifier referencing a numeric data item'; §8.4.3.1.2 Format 1 makes a function-identifier an identifier; and §8.4.3.2.4 1) closes the loop the prior pass left open, 'A function-identifier references a temporary data item whose value is determined when the function is referenced at runtime' (all --check OK), so the premise is spec-backed rather than assumed. It is EQUALLY legal in a REFERENCE-MODIFIER, unchecked before: §8.4.3.3.3 4) 'Leftmost-position and length shall be arithmetic expressions.' (--check OK). Both funnel through the ONE ReferenceResolver#RenderSegment — InterpretSubscripts calls it per subscript segment AND, on the depth-0-colon branch, for the ref-mod start and length — and RenderSegment handles only SUB_INTEGERLIT, SUB_IDENTIFIER (+ OF/IN), + - * / and parens, its `default: return null` naming FUNCTION explicitly. In SUBSCRIPT mode the word FUNCTION is a plain SUB_IDENTIFIER, so it reaches ResolveSubscriptName, resolves to nothing, and the whole reference fails loud. A VERIFIED rejection of legal source is an active contradiction, not an unverified half — PARTIAL was the wrong shape. SECOND, the acceptance mechanism was described wrongly: PreviousIsFunctionName() reads `_prevNonWsTokenType`, which NextToken() maintains as the token BEFORE last, so at the '(' of `FUNCTION INTEGER (` the last token is IDENTIFIER(INTEGER) and the prev is FUNCTION; OnDefaultLParen keeps DEFAULT mode only because BOTH PreviousIsFunctionName() and PreviousTokenCouldBeDataName() hold. I re-verified independently that INTEGER is not a lexer keyword: it does not appear in §8.9's reserved-word list (searched the clause span mechanically) and tests/version-matrix/cobol-words.json has ZERO occurrences, so functionName's IDENTIFIER alternative carries it and argument-1 parses as a real arithmeticExpression. Arity is enforced at bind (MinArgs=MaxArgs=1 → COBOLNET1504), and the §8.4.3.2.3 2) keyword-omitted form (--check OK) reaches the SAME functionArgList via KeywordOmittedFunction → ReparseArgs. NOT INTEGER-SPECIFIC: RenderSegment rejects every function reference and every non-trivial arithmetic expression in a subscript or ref-mod. Owned architecturally by plan §CUT 2.5 / D10 Step D10.3, but the rejects-legal-COBOL consequence is not recorded there. Corroboration only (NON-QUALIFYING): IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests line 70 is a *MatchesLegacy differential; IntrinsicSpecTests#IntegerFunctionAsSubscript shows the LEGACY engine printing BBB for `DISPLAY WS-ELT(FUNCTION INTEGER(2.9))`, so the greenfield is a regression — a legacy test is a net, never authority. EDITIONS: format text unchanged across the window (no Annex E row); the keyword-omitted leg needs a REPOSITORY paragraph (2002+).

subject: ORD function
notes: Re-verified independently. The canonical PDF was re-extracted at PDF page 930 (printed folio 900): the general format is literally 'FUNCTION ORD ( argument-1 )' — no brackets, no optional element, so there is no room for the falsely-restrictive OCR failure mode; the §15.70.2 transcription is faithful. Grammar (read, not inferred): functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (LPAREN functionArgList? RPAREN)? ; ORD is not a reserved word and reaches functionName as an ordinary word. Exact arity 1 comes from the catalog row Add(new("ORD", IntrinsicType.Integer, IntrinsicArity.Fixed, 1, 1, "s", "Ord", IntrinsicBind.Runtime, false, 85)) and is enforced by BindIntrinsicCore's MinArgs/MaxArgs gate. RE-PROBED with the built CLI at --std 2023: 'FUNCTION ORD' and 'FUNCTION ORD()' each give COBOLNET1504 '1 argument(s); 0 given', 'FUNCTION ORD(A B)' gives '1 argument(s); 2 given', and the one-argument form binds. Both test-refs exist on disk and both call the one-argument format with value assertions (IF127A has 10 FUNCTION ORD call sites).

subject: ORD-MAX function

subject: ORD-MIN function

subject: PI function
notes: Citation re-validated mechanically: `cite.py --check 15.73.2 "<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>PI</u>"` OK - the transcribed format is both words underlined (required) with NO argument list. The FUNCTION-keyword spelling is correct and was re-verified on the built CLI at --std 2023: FUNCTION PI binds and evaluates in DISPLAY / MOVE / COMPUTE / IF, arity 0..0 is enforced ('FUNCTION PI (1)' -> COBOLNET1504), and the 2002 window is gated ('--std 85' -> COBOLNET1502, catalog row IntroducedIn 2002). PARTIAL because the other legal spelling of this same reference is broken: SS8.4.3.2.3 SR2 ('the word FUNCTION may be omitted from the function-identifier', validated) applies when REPOSITORY declares FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC, and IntrinsicBinder.KeywordOmittedFunction returns null unless the dataReference carries EXACTLY ONE subscriptPart suffix (`if (suffixes.Length != 1 ...) return null;`), so a ZERO-argument keyword-omitted intrinsic can never route - it is the only call path (the two ExpressionBinder chokepoints RefExpr/FieldOperand are the sole call sites). Re-verified: 'COMPUTE R05 = PI.' under 'REPOSITORY. FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC.' compiles with exit 0 and NO diagnostic, then throws NotImplementedCobolFeatureException "reference 'PI'" at run time; 'COMPUTE R05 = PI ().' is a hard parse error (COBOL0001 'no viable alternative'). Same hole for every zero-argument intrinsic (E, RANDOM, CURRENT-DATE, WHEN-COMPILED) - one pattern, one fix. TEST COVERAGE: the cited test is the ONLY greenfield test that references PI anywhere under tests/ (grep-verified); it exercises the empty-parens spelling 'FUNCTION PI ()' at edition 2014 only, so neither the bare SS15.73.2 two-word format nor the SR2 keyword-omitted zero-argument form is covered - test-needed for both.

subject: RANDOM function
notes: PRINTED PAGE RE-RENDERED BY REVIEW (scripts/render-spec-page.py 935 = printed folio 905): the diagram is exactly `FUNCTION RANDOM [ ( [ argument-1 ] ) ]`, FUNCTION and RANDOM underlined, BOTH bracket levels present — the specs/ISO_COBOL.md transcription is faithful, no OCR over-restriction. Grammar `functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (LPAREN functionArgList? RPAREN)?` admits all three shapes; the catalog row RANDOM/OptionalTrailing/MinArgs 0/MaxArgs 1 plus the BindIntrinsicCore arity check bound it. Re-verified at --std 85, 2002, 2014 AND 2023: `FUNCTION RANDOM`, `FUNCTION RANDOM ( )` and `FUNCTION RANDOM (5)` all compile and run; `FUNCTION RANDOM (1, 2)` is rejected with COBOLNET1504 'FUNCTION RANDOM takes 0..1 argument(s); 2 given (ISO 15.3)'. subject: RANGE function
notes: The written format is supported; ONE legal argument shape licensed by its `{argument-1} …` repetition is not. Printed PDF page 936 (folio 906) re-rendered independently: the transcription is faithful — FUNCTION and RANGE underlined, `( { argument-1 } … )`, one-or-more, no OCR over-restriction. functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (LPAREN functionArgList? RPAREN)? with functionArgList : functionArgument (FNARG_SEPARATOR? functionArgument)*, and IntrinsicCatalog.Build registers RANGE as Variadic 1..int.MaxValue, IntroducedIn 85, RemovedIn null. Re-verified on the built CLI: 1 arg, space-separated, comma-separated, mixed space/comma, arithmetic-expression arguments, table(ALL) over a FIXED OCCURS, and the keyword-omitted form under REPOSITORY FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC all compile and evaluate; `FUNCTION RANGE()` and bare `FUNCTION RANGE` are both rejected COBOLNET1504 ("takes at least 1 argument(s); 0 given"); all at --std 85 and 2023. GAP: §15.3 says "If the ALL subscript is associated with a data item described with an OCCURS DEPENDING ON clause, the range of values is determined by the object of the OCCURS DEPENDING ON clause" — IntrinsicBinder.TryExpandAll instead emits BoundOperandError "table(ALL) over OCCURS DEPENDING table", so `05 E PIC S9(3) OCCURS 1 TO 5 DEPENDING ON CNT. COMPUTE R = FUNCTION RANGE(E(ALL))` COMPILES CLEAN and then throws NotImplementedCobolFeatureException at run time (reproduced). This is shared §15.3 machinery every variadic function inherits (MAX/MIN/SUM/MEAN/MEDIAN/MIDRANGE/RANGE/ORD-MAX/ORD-MIN/STANDARD-DEVIATION/VARIANCE/PRESENT-VALUE), so it should be raised as its OWN fix-queue entry rather than closed against RANGE; grep-confirmed absent from docs/CONFORMANCE.md, docs/rearchitecture/CONFORMANCE-FIX-QUEUE.md and plan §0. Test coverage: IF132A line 498 exercises `FUNCTION RANGE(IND(ALL))` over a FIXED OCCURS 5 table plus comma-separated, space-separated and subscripted lists, and ExactFamily_MatchesLegacy pins `FUNCTION RANGE(3, 11, 7)` against a committed golden (COBOLNET_DIFF_MODE defaults to `golden`, so it always runs and no live legacy run is involved); the ODO-ALL shape has NO test — test-needed.

subject: REM function
notes: Re-verified independently. TRANSCRIPTION: the canonical PDF's own text layer for printed folio 907 (PDF page 937) reads exactly 'FUNCTION REM ( argument-1  argument-2 )' -- nothing bracketed, no choice indicator, no ellipsis; the 300-dpi figure check already on record in docs/rearchitecture/spec-reconciliation/agents/compare-p933-p944.json covers 15.77.2 and found no lost delimiters, and the once-missing <u> markup (LEDGER.json systemic chapter-15 defect, REM named) is present in specs/ISO_COBOL.md today. GRAMMAR/BINDER: functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (LPAREN functionArgList? RPAREN)? literally present; the catalog Build row pins IntrinsicArity.Fixed 2..2. Verified by RUNNING the built compiler: the printed SPACE-separated form FUNCTION REM(A B), the 8.3.5 comma form, the 8.4.3.2 SR6 space-before-paren form FUNCTION REM (A B), an arithmetic-expression argument, a nested FUNCTION REM argument, and the adjacent-sign two-argument form FUNCTION REM(A -4) (= REM(11,-4) = 3, not a subtraction) all compile and give the ISO 15.77.4 values in argument order; FUNCTION REM(5) and FUNCTION REM(5 3 2) are both rejected with COBOLNET1504. Coverage caveat (not a downgrade -- a comma IS the 8.3.5 separator form of the printed space): both test-refs use only the comma form, so no committed test pins the printed space-separator spelling.

subject: REVERSE function
notes:
Printed folio 908 (PDF page 938) re-rendered and read independently: the format is `FUNCTION REVERSE ( argument-1 )` with FUNCTION and REVERSE both UNDERLINED (required), one unbracketed required operand, no optional phrase. Grammar: functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (LPAREN functionArgList? RPAREN)? ; REVERSE is NOT a lexer token (only REVERSE_VIDEO and REVERSED are - grep-verified over Grammar/) so it arrives as IDENTIFIER through functionName. The catalog row is Fixed 1..1 and the arity gate was re-run live against the built CLI: `FUNCTION REVERSE` (no parens) -> COBOLNET1504 '1 argument(s); 0 given'; `FUNCTION REVERSE()` -> COBOLNET1504 '0 given'; `FUNCTION REVERSE(W-A W-B)` -> COBOLNET1504 '2 given'; `FUNCTION REVERSE(OMITTED)` -> COBOLNET1544 (8.4.3.2.3 SR7, cite-checked). The parens being syntactically optional in the grammar is harmless: the shape is still REJECTED, at bind time rather than parse time. ⚠ TRANSCRIPTION DEFECT (the prior draft asserted 'the transcription is faithful' - that claim is WITHDRAWN as false): specs/ISO_COBOL.md 15.78.2 renders the general format as BARE MARKDOWN TEXT, with no 
 wrapper and no  markup, while every neighbour checked (15.75.2 RANDOM, 15.76.2 RANGE, 15.77.2 REM, 15.79.2 SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME, 15.80.2 SECONDS-PAST-MIDNIGHT) carries both. The required-word underlining the printed page shows is therefore LOST in the transcription. The verdict is unaffected - this format has no optional element, so nothing required-vs-optional turns on the underlining, and the compiler requires both words - but the defect is real and propagating: the Phase-B extractor's rule text for FMT-15.78.2 swallowed the trailing `` anchor precisely BECAUSE there is no 
 block to bound it. Repair 15.78.2 to the 
/ form of its neighbours. ⚠ Test coverage is POSITIVE-ONLY: both test-refs write the correct one-argument format (StringFamily_PinnedToSpec has an InlineData `MOVE FUNCTION REVERSE("abc 12") TO T.`; IF134A carries 109 REVERSE references, e.g. `MOVE FUNCTION REVERSE("figure") TO WS-ANUM.`), so acceptance is pinned, but NO test pins the four rejection shapes above - they were verified by hand. A negative golden for arity 0/2 and OMITTED is test-needed.

subject: SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME function
notes: PDF page 939 (printed folio 909) was RE-RENDERED independently for this review and the transcription is faithful: FUNCTION and SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME are underlined (required words), argument-1 and argument-2 appear unbracketed inside the parentheses separated by a space — exactly two mandatory arguments, no optional phrase, no OCR-induced over-restriction. The grammar is the intended superset (`functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (LPAREN functionArgList? RPAREN)?`; the hyphenated name arrives as IDENTIFIER; arguments juxtapose or take the §8.3.5 comma separator), narrowed at bind time by the catalog row (IntrinsicArity.Fixed, 2, 2). Re-verified at --std 2014: the space-separated two-argument form compiles and returns +45296.00; one argument → COBOLNET1504 'takes 2 argument(s); 1 given (ISO §15.3)'; three arguments → the same 1504 with '3 given'; --std 2002 → COBOLNET1502 'introduced by ISO/IEC 1989:2014'. The two test-refs write the general format's exact shape and assert a correct value, so they cover the positive side; the COBOLNET1504 arity rejection has no negative test.
